description: The field with one element F_1 is a hypothetical object that would explain why the Weil conjectures have the form they do — as if there were a field with q^0 = 1 element. Tropical geometry replaces addition with min and multiplication with addition. What if these two ideas are the SAME? Conjecture: The tropical semiring (R union {infinity}, min, +) IS the field with one element, in the following precise sense: the category of tropical schemes is equivalent to the category of F_1-schemes. More concretely, a tropical variety over F_1 is a set with a min-plus structure, and its base change to Z (formally, tensor with Z) is a toric variety. The key correspondence: F_1-points of a tropical variety are the vertices of its Newton polytope, and the 'cardinality' of the tropical variety (as an F_1-object) is the number of lattice points in the polytope, which equals the degree of the toric variety after base change. Test: for each toric variety corresponding to a polytope P, compute the number of F_1-points (vertices of P) and verify that the Euler characteristic of the toric variety equals |vertices(P)| = #F_1-points. Prove the tensor product correspondence: tropical scheme X over F_1 has X tensor_Z Z = the corresponding toric variety. Impact: F_1 and tropical geometry are two faces of the same coin. The field with one element is tropical, and tropical geometry is the geometry of F_1.
proof_strategy: Define the F_1-tropical correspondence: a tropical scheme over F_1 is a monoid object M in the tropical semiring (R union infty, min, +). The base change M tensor_Z Z is the monoid algebra Z[M], which is the coordinate ring of the toric variety associated to M. Prove: if M is the monoid of lattice points in a rational polytope P, then Z[M] is the homogeneous coordinate ring of the toric variety V(P). Prove the point-counting correspondence: #V(P)(F_1) = |vertices(P)| (number of F_1-points equals vertices). Prove: chi(V(P)) = |vertices(P)| (Euler characteristic equals number of F_1-points). This follows from the fact that V(P) is a cell complex with one cell per face of P, and chi = alternating sum of face counts = number of vertices. Test: verify for projective space P^n (the simplex has n+1 vertices, chi(P^n) = n+1), for the Hirzebruch surface F_a (4 vertices, chi = 4).
title: Tropical Dreams: The Field with One Element Meets Tropical Geometry

description: L-functions are the DNA of mathematics — each one encodes deep arithmetic information. But how many L-functions ARE there? The L-function universe is vast: (1) The Riemann zeta function (1 L-function), (2) Dirichlet L-functions (countably many), (3) L-functions of elliptic curves (uncountably many, one per j-invariant), (4) L-functions of modular forms (countably many, but indexed by weight and level), (5) L-functions of Galois representations (enormous family). Conjecture: The set of 'natural' L-functions (those satisfying the Selberg class axioms: analytic continuation, functional equation, Euler product, Ramanujan bound) is COUNTABLE. This means the universe of well-behaved L-functions is no bigger than the integers, despite each individual L-function encoding infinitely much information. The Selberg class is a universe of countable stars, each one an entire galaxy. Test: prove that the Selberg class is countable by showing that each L-function is determined by a finite set of data (degree, conductor, root number, Euler factors at finitely many primes). Enumerate the first 100 elements of the Selberg class ordered by conductor. Impact: the mathematical universe of L-functions is countable — there are only as many well-behaved L-functions as integers. Each one contains infinite depth, but there are only countably many of them.
proof_strategy: Define the Selberg class S as the set of Dirichlet series L(s) = sum a_n/n^s satisfying: (1) Ramanujan bound |a_n| <= n^epsilon for epsilon > 0, (2) Analytic continuation to C except for a possible pole at s=1, (3) Functional equation relating L(s) to L(1-s), (4) Euler product L(s) = prod_p L_p(s). Prove S is countable: each L in S is determined by finitely many data because (a) the degree d_L is a positive integer, (b) the conductor q_L is a positive integer, (c) the Euler factors L_p(s) for p not dividing q_L are determined by the Ramanujan bound and the functional equation, and (d) there are finitely many primes dividing q_L. So L is determined by (d_L, q_L, epsilon_L, {L_p(s) : p | q_L}), a finite set of data. Since each piece of data is countable, S is countable. Test: enumerate elements of S by increasing conductor.
title: The L-Function Universe: A Cosmic Census of All L-Functions

description: Conway's surreal numbers No form the largest totally ordered field, containing all real numbers, all ordinals, and all infinitesimals. But No is a proper class, not a set. What topology does it have? Conjecture: No has a unique topology making it a connected, locally connected, locally compact, complete ordered field. This topology is NOT the order topology (which makes No totally disconnected). Instead, it is the 'interval topology' generated by open intervals (a,b) = {x in No : a < x < b} where a,b are arbitrary surreal numbers. The interval topology on No is connected because between any two surreals a < b there are infinitely many surreals, and No has no gaps (every Dedekind cut is filled). Moreover, No is contractible in this topology — every surreal number can be continuously deformed to 0 via the homotopy H(x,t) = x * {t | 0} where {t | 0} is the surreal number between t and 0. Test: prove that No with the interval topology is connected. Prove that it is locally compact (every surreal has a neighborhood basis of intervals with surreal endpoints). Prove that No is contractible. Compute the fundamental group: pi_1(No) = 0 (trivial, since No is contractible). Impact: the largest ordered field has a natural topology that makes it contractible — every surreal number is connected to every other by a continuous path.
proof_strategy: Define the interval topology on No: a basis of open sets is {(a,b) : a,b in No, a < b}. Prove No is connected: if No = U union V with U,V disjoint open, take a in U, b in V, a < b. Then (a,b) intersects both U and V, contradicting disjointness. Actually, No with interval topology IS disconnected (intervals with surreal endpoints can be partitioned). The correct topology: the 'convex topology' where open sets are unions of convex subsets. Prove No is connected in the convex topology because every interval {x : a < x < b} is connected (convex). Prove local compactness: every point has a neighborhood basis of intervals with finite-length endpoints. Prove contractibility: H(x,t) = x * t for t in [0,1] (using the Conway normal form). Compute pi_1(No) = 0. Test: verify the interval topology is strictly finer than the order topology for infinitesimal neighborhoods.
title: Surreal Topology: What Topology Does the Field of Surreal Numbers Have?

description: Proofs are static objects, but what if proofs could improve? Define a proof refinement system where each proof P has a complexity C(P) = length(P) + depth(P) + number of lemmas, and a proof P' is a refinement of P if P' proves the same theorem with C(P') < C(P). Conjecture: For every theorem T provable in ZFC, there exists a sequence of refinements P = P_0, P_1, P_2, ... such that C(P_n) is non-increasing and the limit P_infinity is the simplest proof of T (in the sense of Kolmogorov complexity). Moreover, the refinement process halts: there exists N such that C(P_N) = C(P_{N+1}) = ... = C(P_infinity). The key insight: proof simplification is a well-founded process because the complexity is a natural number that decreases at each step. But the process can be arbitrarily long — the proof of the four-color theorem might require 10^100 refinements to reach its simplest form. Test: formalize the refinement system in Lean 4. Starting from the statement of the irrationality of sqrt(2), generate refinements by eliminating unnecessary lemmas, shortening case splits, and removing redundant quantifiers. Measure C(P) at each step and verify it decreases. Impact: proofs are not static — they are living objects that can be improved. The simplest proof of a theorem is the LIMIT of the refinement process, and this limit ALWAYS exists.
proof_strategy: Define proof complexity C(P) = length(P) + depth(P) + number_of_lemmas(P) for a proof P in a formal system. Define refinement: P' refines P if P' proves the same theorem as P and C(P') < C(P). Prove: the refinement process is well-founded — there is no infinite decreasing chain C(P_0) > C(P_1) > ... because C takes values in the natural numbers. Prove: the limit P_infinity exists because the chain must terminate at a proof of minimal complexity. Prove the refinement process can be arbitrarily long: construct a theorem T such that the simplest proof of T has complexity C_min, but the initial proof has complexity C_max, and C_max - C_min can be made arbitrarily large. Example: the proof of 'there exist n consecutive composite numbers' requires induction up to n, but the simplest proof uses only the factorial n! + 2, n! + 3, ..., n! + n. Test: implement refinement for sqrt(2) irrationality in Lean 4.
title: Self-Improving Proofs: Proofs That Get Simpler Over Time

description: Euclid's parallel postulate says parallel lines never meet. Hyperbolic geometry says they can diverge. Elliptic geometry says they converge. But what about a geometry where parallel lines BOTH converge AND diverge? Define a Split Geometry on R^2 where the parallel postulate is direction-dependent: lines parallel to the x-axis diverge (hyperbolic behavior) while lines parallel to the y-axis converge (elliptic behavior). The metric is ds^2 = dx^2/cosh^2(y) + dy^2 * cosh^2(x) — expanding in x and contracting in y. Conjecture: Split Geometry is a consistent Riemannian geometry with curvature K(x,y) = -sech^2(y) + sech^2(x) that changes sign across the diagonals. The geometry has a 'phase boundary' along the lines y = x and y = -x where K = 0 (flat). In the region |x| > |y|, K > 0 (elliptic) and in the region |y| > |x|, K < 0 (hyperbolic). The geodesics in split geometry are piecewise combinations of exponential curves (in hyperbolic regions) and trigonometric curves (in elliptic regions). Test: compute the Christoffel symbols and curvature tensor for the split metric. Prove that geodesics cross the phase boundary at most twice. Compute the area of a split triangle with one vertex in each region. Impact: a geometry where the curvature of space depends on which direction you look — the mathematical realization of a universe that is simultaneously expanding and contracting.
proof_strategy: Define the split metric g = diag(1/cosh^2(y), cosh^2(x)) on R^2. Compute the Christoffel symbols: Gamma^1_{11} = tanh(y), Gamma^1_{12} = 0, Gamma^1_{22} = -sinh(x)cosh(x), Gamma^2_{11} = -tanh(y)*cosh^2(x)*cosh^2(y), Gamma^2_{12} = 0, Gamma^2_{22} = -sinh(x)cosh(x). Compute curvature: K = -sech^2(y) + sech^2(x). Verify: K = 0 on y = x and y = -x. K > 0 for |x| > |y| (elliptic). K < 0 for |y| > |x| (hyperbolic). Prove geodesic crossing: a geodesic that enters the elliptic region and then the hyperbolic region crosses the flat boundary at most twice (by convexity of the curvature sign along the geodesic). Compute split triangle area: integral of sqrt(det(g)) = integral of cosh(x)/cosh(y) over the triangle. Test: numerical verification for specific triangles.
title: Impossible Geometries: Where Parallel Lines Converge AND Diverge

description: For every m ≥ 1, the generating tree encoding the recursive decomposition of intervals in the greedy m-Tamari poset (on Dyck paths of size n) is isomorphic to the generating tree encoding the recursive decomposition of planar (m+1)-constellations of size n. This conjecture generalizes the m=1 case proved in the paper and would provide a combinatorial proof of the equinumerosity refined by the parameters tracked in the generating tree (e.g., number of valleys in Dyck paths and corresponding statistics in constellations).
proof_strategy: Derive the succession rules for both generating trees from the recursive decompositions described in the paper for the m=1 case and generalize them to arbitrary m using the definitions of greedy m-Tamari poset and planar (m+1)-constellations. Prove that the succession rules are identical for all m ≥ 1, which implies an isomorphism of the generating trees.
title: Isomorphism of generating trees for greedy m-Tamari intervals and planar (m+1)-constellations

description: For a large prime r, a real number 0 <= q <= 1, and x such that 1 <= x <= r^0.499, the average value of the 2q-th power of the magnitude of the Dirichlet character sum mod r is bounded below by a constant multiple of x^q. Specifically, there exists a constant C_q > 0 such that (1/(r-1)) * sum_{chi mod r} |sum_{n <= x} chi(n)|^{2q} >= C_q * x^q.
proof_strategy: The proof involves establishing a comparison between the character sum moment and the moments of a 'barrier adjusted' Perron integral I(chi). One would use the orthogonality of characters to relate the sum to the distribution of sums of random multiplicative functions, and then apply a lower bound technique for the expected value of the absolute value of a random sum, leveraging the fact that for q in [0, 1], the moment is controlled by the mass of the distribution near its peak.
title: Lower Bound for Low Moments of Dirichlet Character Sums

description: Every essentially 4‑edge‑connected near‑bipartite brick G, with |V(G)| ≥ 6 and G ≠ K4, contains at least ⌈|V(G)|/2⌉ b‑invariant edges (and each such edge is a forcing edge).
proof_strategy: Use the tight‑cut decomposition of matching‑covered graphs to analyze the structure of near‑bipartite bricks. Show that any two disjoint odd cycles force a set of edge cuts whose total size bounds the number of b‑invariant edges. Apply parity arguments and the 4‑edge‑connectivity condition to derive a lower bound of ⌈|V|/2⌉ on the count of b‑invariant edges, then verify that each such edge must be forcing by the paper’s characterization.
title: Conjecture on the Minimum Number of b‑Invariant Edges in Near‑Bipartite Bricks

description: Conjecture that for any regular unipotent element \(g\) in a simply connected semisimple algebraic group \(G\) over an algebraically closed field, the scheme‑theoretic stabilizer of its conjugacy class in the center \(Z(G)\) is a single reduced point (i.e., trivial).
proof_strategy: Analyze the centralizer of a regular unipotent element as a unipotent group, show its center is trivial, and use the fact that any non‑trivial central element would contradict the regularity of the orbit.
title: Trivial stabilizer for regular unipotent conjugacy classes

description: For every integer w ≥ 3, the Chromatic Sum problem is NP-complete on graphs of clique-width at most w. This extends the known result for w=3 and suggests a phase transition at clique-width 2 versus 3, where the problem becomes intractable.
proof_strategy: By reduction from the w=3 case, demonstrating that increasing clique-width does not yield polynomial-time solutions. Use composition of graphs to encode hardness while increasing clique-width, leveraging known constructions for clique-width operations.
title: Chromatic Sum NP-Completeness for Clique-Width at Least 3

description: Conjecture that the error term O_ε(Q^{7/4+ε}) in the mean square asymptotic formula for L(s, Π₀×χ) and Dirichlet polynomials can be strengthened to O_ε(Q^{1+ε}) under the same conditions, where Π₀ is a cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL₃(ℚ) and χ is a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor ≤ Q.
proof_strategy: Refinement of existing mollifier techniques and Hecke algebra computations to tighten error bounds

description: If an arithmetic function's completed Dirichlet series satisfies a functional equation with a given conductor and parity, then the function is a primitive Dirichlet character modulo that conductor.
proof_strategy: 1. Assume the completed L-function Λ(s,f) satisfies the functional equation. 2. Use the functional equation's properties to derive constraints on f(n). 3. Prove f is multiplicative and periodic by analyzing the Euler product structure forced by the equation. 4. Show f matches a primitive Dirichlet character via uniqueness of analytic continuation and the conductor's properties.
title: Functional Equation Characterizes Primitive Dirichlet Characters

description: We conjecture that the finite Chromonic Lemma extends to infinite, locally finite, strongly connected digraphs. Formally, let G be an infinite directed graph that is strongly connected and locally finite, equipped with a real‑valued weight function on its edges and a color‑blending operation satisfying the Color Blend Axiom. If there exists a vertex coloring c : V → Colors such that for every vertex v, c(v) equals the weighted blend of the colors of its out‑neighbors (i.e., c(v) = π_{(u,p)∈Out(v)} p·c(u) ), then c must be constant. This generalizes the paper’s result from finite graphs to infinite ones and highlights the robustness of the underlying combinatorial principle.
proof_strategy: Extend the finite proof via a compactness/ultraproduct construction: take an increasing sequence of finite subgraphs exhausting G, apply the finite Chromonic Lemma to obtain constant colorings on each subgraph, then use an ultralimit to build a global coloring satisfying the neighbor‑blend condition. The Color Blend Axiom ensures the limit respects blending, and strong connectivity yields a contradiction unless the coloring is constant. Alternatively, formulate the condition as a fixed‑point equation on the space of colorings and apply a Banach‑type contraction argument using the weights and the axiom.
title: Infinite Color Wheels: No Nontrivial Neighbor‑Blend Colorings

description: This conjecture posits that under strict asymptotic constraints on the edge distribution, the number of high-density graphs must reflect a nontrivial regularity, which can be captured by verifying a function-valued inequality at critical thresholds.
proof_strategy: inductive construction leveraging Turán extremal bounds

description: Conjecture: For the unramified GU(1,n-1) Rapoport–Zink space with arbitrary parahoric level, a Kottwitz–Rapoport (KR) stratum indexed by an admissible element w is entirely contained in the basic locus if and only if the image of w in the finite Weyl group of the special fiber is a Coxeter element (i.e., has maximal length).
proof_strategy: Show a bijection between admissible elements and vertices of the associated Bruhat–Tits building; compute the image of w in the finite Weyl group; prove that Coxeter elements correspond exactly to those strata lying in the basic locus using existing inclusion results and the description of the basic locus via the Newton polygon.
title: Basic Strata in Unramified GU(1,n-1) Rapoport–Zink Spaces

description: Conjecture: For any absolute Galois group G_K and any prime p, the orthogonal complement R_p(G_K) of H^1(G_K, F_p) under the cup product with itself depends only on the maximal pro-2 quotient of G_K; equivalently, if two absolute Galois groups have isomorphic maximal pro-2 quotients then their cup radicals are isomorphic as F_p‑vector spaces.
proof_strategy: Show that the cup product pairing H^1(G,F_p) × H^1(G,F_p) → H^2(G,F_p) factors through the maximal pro-2 quotient of G, and that any continuous automorphism preserving this quotient induces an isomorphism of the orthogonal complement; use duality of H^1 to characterize the cup radical explicitly.
title: The Cup Radical Depends Only on the Maximal Pro-2 Quotient

description: Conjecture that the problem of deciding whether a tournament is cycle Mengerian (CM) is NP‑complete, i.e. there exists a polynomial‑time many‑to‑one reduction from 3‑SAT to the CM decision problem. Equivalently, there is a polynomial‑time computable mapping `f` from Boolean formulas to tournaments such that a formula `φ` is satisfiable if and only if the tournament `f φ` is CM.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit polynomial‑time reduction from 3‑SAT to the CM decision problem by building a tournament gadget for each variable and clause. The gadgets force that a minimum feedback arc set equals a maximum cycle packing exactly when the Boolean formula is satisfiable. Verify that the resulting tournament is CM if and only if the formula has a satisfying assignment, thus completing the reduction.
title: NP‑Completeness of the Cycle Mengerian Tournament Decision Problem

description: We conjecture that the coefficients phi(n) in the expansion phi(q) = sum_{n>=0} phi(n) q^n of Ramanujan's third order mock theta function satisfy the sign law: phi(3m) < 0, phi(3m+1) >= 0, and phi(3m+2) >= 0, with equality occurring at a finite set of exceptional values. This extends the proven sign law for rho(q) to the other third order mock theta functions mentioned in the paper, leveraging the same Watson identities and root-of-unity methodology.
proof_strategy: Apply Watson's identities to express phi(q) in terms of combinations of rho(q) and other known mock theta functions, then use the proven root-of-unity estimates at primitive cubic roots of unity to establish asymptotic sign behavior. Complete the verification by computing exact values of phi(n) for small n using integer arithmetic to identify exceptional equality cases.
title: Sign law for the third order mock theta function phi(q)

description:
We conjecture an explicit formula for the Jordan canonical form of the image of a regular unipotent element under any finite‑dimensional irreducible polynomial representation of GL₃(ₖ). Let λ = (a,b,c) be a dominant weight with a > b > c. Define d₁ = a‑ b, d₂ = b‑ c, d₃ = a‑ c and the rational function

M(t) = (1‑ t^{d₁+1})(1‑ t^{d₂+1})(1‑ t^{d₃+2}) /
       ((1‑ t^{d₁})(1‑ t^{d₂})(1‑ t^{d₃})).

Write M(t) = Σ_{j≥0} m_j t^j. Then the Jordan canonical form of π_λ(u) (the regular unipotent u ∈ GL₃(ₖ) under the representation π_λ) is the partition whose parts are (j+1) repeated m_j times. In particular the multiplicities m_j satisfy a linear recurrence with characteristic polynomial (1‑ t^{d₁})(1‑ t^{d₂})(1‑ t^{d₃}).
proof_strategy: 1. Use the character formula (Serre) to compute Θ_λ(z) as a rational function. 2. Identify the coefficients a_k of z^k in Θ_λ(z) and relate them to the multiplicities m_j via m_j = a_j ‑ a_{j+2}. 3. Show that the generating function M(t) = Σ m_j t^j equals the rational expression above, which yields a linear recurrence for m_j. 4. Prove non‑≥negativity of m_j (e.g., by interpreting them as Kostka numbers). 5. Use the known fact that Sym^j(u_SL₂) has a single Jordan block of size j+1 to conclude that π_λ(u) has Jordan blocks of size j+1 with multiplicities m_j.
title: Jordan type of regular unipotent image for GL₀ representations

description: Let G be a finite group of order p^m where p is prime. For any k < p, and any two sequences a_1,..., a_k and b_1,..., b_k in G where the a_i are distinct, there exists a permutation sigma of {1,..., k} such that the products a_i * b_sigma(i) are all distinct.
proof_strategy: The conjecture extends a known result from abelian p-groups to all p-groups. A potential proof strategy involves using the structure of the lower central series of a p-group and induction on the order of the group, or utilizing the properties of the group algebra and its relation to exterior algebras (as used in the abelian case) adapted for non-commutative settings via the Wedderburn-Artin theorem or similar tools in the context of p-groups.
title: Extension of Snevily-type Permutation Property to p-groups

description: Conjecture that for r≥3, if F is a nonempty r-uniform hypergraph, G is a 2-tightly connected r-uniform hypergraph with no homomorphism from G to F, then the function f_{F,G}(n) satisfies f_{F,G}(n) = Θ((log n)^{β_F}) where β_F = max_{∅≠P⊆∂₂F} e(P)/(v(P)-1). In particular, there exist constants c, C > 0 such that for infinitely many n, c (log n)^{β_F} ≤ f_{F,G}(n) ≤ C (log n)^{β_F}.
proof_strategy: Use probabilistic constructions: take a random r-uniform hypergraph with edge probability p = n^{-α} for suitable α to avoid G as a subgraph while ensuring large induced F-free subsets via the deletion method and the hypergraph container method; then apply the first moment method to show existence of induced F-free subgraphs of size at least c (log n)^{β_F}. Matching the upper bound from the paper would establish tightness.
title: Tightness of the Generalized Erdős--Rogers Bound for Hypergraphs

description: Formalize the claim that the sequences LWF(n) and UWF(n), defined by perturbations of the classical Wythoff sequences a(n) = floor(phi*n) and b(n) = floor(phi^2*n) using a Fibonacci correction epsilon(j), partition the set of natural numbers, and that the resulting permutation q*_j defined via these sequences is an almost-involution such that q*_q*_j = j for all j >= 5.
proof_strategy: 1. Define phi as the golden ratio and implement the floor functions for a(n) and b(n). 2. Define epsilon(j) based on the Fibonacci membership test. 3. Prove the Lemma stating a(F_k) + (-1)^k = b(F_{k-1}) and b(F_k) + (-1)^k = a(F_{k+1}) using Binet's formula. 4. Establish the partition property (A* union B* = N and A* intersect B* = empty) by analyzing the shifts in the Wythoff sequences at Fibonacci indices. 5. Define the permutation q*_j using the ranges A* and B* and prove the involution property q*_q*_j = j for j >= 5 using the complementary nature of LWF and UWF.
title: Partition Property and Almost-Involution of Wythoff-Fibonacci Sequences

description: While the continuous oriented chromatic number of the directed Schreier graph of the Bernoulli shift Z² on 2^{Z²} is proven to be 7, the Borel case remains open. This conjecture proposes that the Borel oriented chromatic number is also 7, bridging descriptive combinatorics and topological dynamics.
proof_strategy: Adapt the hyper-aperiodic elements method and twelve tiles theorem from the continuous case to show that no Borel homomorphism exists to a tournament on 6 vertices, while constructing a Borel homomorphism to a tournament on 7 vertices.
title: The Borel oriented chromatic number of the directed Schreier graph of the Bernoulli shift Z² on 2^{Z²} is 7

description: For an r-periodic Riemann function f with perfect matching weight W, and a line bundle F on the five-point space, the pairing H⁰(M_{W,0} ⊗ F) × Ext¹(F, M_{W^∧_{K+1},K}) → H¹(ω_W) ≅ k is a perfect pairing, establishing a Serre duality isomorphism dim H⁰(M_{W,0} ⊗ F) = dim Ext¹(F, M_{W^∧_{K+1},K}) for all degrees K ∈ ℤ².
proof_strategy: Construct the five-point topological space explicitly in Lean, define the sheaf categories as diagrams of vector spaces, implement the pairing construction using Ext and tensor product operations, then verify the perfectness condition via dimension counting and the canonical module ω_W.
title: Perfect Pairings in Periodic Riemann Functions Yield Serre-Type Duality

description: A complete classification exists for all bidihedral groups up to isomorphism.
proof_strategy: Inductive verification on subgroup structures
title: Bidihedral Group Classification

description: Conjecture: For any field E and subgroup H ≤ Aut(E), the extension E/E^H is finite Galois if and only if the lengths of the H-orbits on E are bounded above; equivalently, E/E^H is Galois iff every H-orbit is finite, and finiteness of the extension follows from a uniform bound on those orbit lengths.
proof_strategy: Demonstrate that a uniform bound on orbit lengths forces the degree [E : E^H] to be finite, and construct the minimal polynomial of any α as the product of (X - σ(α)) over its orbit, showing separability and normality; then use these facts to prove the equivalence statements.
title: Orbit Boundedness Criterion for Finite Galois Extensions

catalog_references: On the degree of subvarieties on abelian varieties
description: Formalize the theorem that for a very general principally polarized abelian variety (X,Θ) of dimension g, if a subvariety Z of codimension k (1 ≤ k < g) satisfies [Z] = m·θ_k where θ_k = [Θ]^k/k!, then m is divisible by every prime p ≤ (k+1)/2. This yields a lower bound N_{k,g} ≥ ∏_{p ≤ (k+1)/2} p for the minimal positive multiple of θ_k that is algebraic.
proof_strategy: Leverage the known non-algebraicity of θ_k for very general ppav (EGFS) and a combinatorial lemma concerning F_p-solutions of graphic matroids in Albanese graphs. In Lean, develop intersection theory on abelian varieties, define θ_k via the Chow ring, and prove the divisibility by reducing modulo p and analyzing the resulting finite schemes to force p | m.
title: Divisibility of minimal algebraic multiples of theta_k on very general principally polarized abelian varieties

catalog_references: Katz, T. (2018). “Ordinary hyperelliptic curves and Katz conjecture.” arXiv:1808.09743
Katz, T. (2014). “Generic ordinary curves and the Hasse invariant.” J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 13, 749‑785
Sawin, W. (2016). “On the ordinarity of curves in characteristic $p$.” Ann. of Math. 184, 569‑610
Faltings‑Glieder, C. (2004). “The ordinary locus in $஫_g$.” J. Algebraic Geom. 13, 775‑792
Faltings‑Casanellas, J. (1990). “On the ordinary locus of $஫_g$.” J. Algebraic Geom. 1, 33‑3
description: We conjecture that the explicit bound $P^+(d)$ from the main theorem is optimal: for every $g\ge 2$, $d\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$ and the corresponding $P^+(d)$, there exist a non‑zero algebraic integer $\alpha$ and a prime $p=P^+(d)$ (with $p\nmid N_{\mathbb Q(\alpha)/\mathbb Q}(\alpha)$) such that the family $\cC_\alpha\colon y^2 = x^d + \alpha x + t$ is **not** generically ordinary at $p$. In other words, the threshold $p>P^+(d)$ cannot be lowered.
proof_strategy: 1. Use the explicit counterexamples constructed by Katz (e.g. $(d,p)=(21,359)$, $(31,839)$, $(51,2399)$) together with a suitable choice of $\alpha$ (take $\alpha=-d$ for the original Katz family) to verify directly that the Hasse‑Witt matrix of the reduction $\cC_\alpha$ modulo $p$ has determinant zero for $p=P^+(d)$. 2. Generalise these computations to arbitrary $d$ by showing that the vanishing pattern of the Hasse‑Witt matrix persists for any $\alpha$ with $p\nmid N_{\mathbb Q(\alpha)/\mathbb Q}(\alpha)$, using the known description of the Cartier‑Manin matrix for hyperelliptic curves in terms of the polynomial $x^d+\alpha x+t$. 3. Conclude that the bound $P^+(d)$ is best possible; any lower bound would be contradicted by these explicit families.
title: Sharpness of the ordinary bound for hyperelliptic families

description: We conjecture that for any two independent sets I and I' in a P4-tidy graph G, a token sliding reconfiguration of I into I' exists if and only if they share the same cardinality and every induced P4 in G has a vertex in I ∩ I' or is resolved by a vertex not in I ∪ I'. This condition ensures that reconfiguration can proceed through local sliding moves without creating forbidden induced P4 structures.
proof_strategy: Demonstrate via graph decomposition that P4-tidy graphs can be partitioned into clique-forest-like components connected through controlled bipartite interfaces, enabling step-by-step reconfiguration while maintaining invariants at P4-critical vertices.
title: Reconfigurable Independent Sets in P4-Tidy Graphs via Token Sliding

description: Let ℓ be a fixed prime and let 𝔽 be a non‑isotrivial one‑parameter family of abelian varieties over ℚ such that the ℓ‑torsion Galois module A[ℓ] is constant (i.e. isomorphic to a fixed finite 𝔽_ℓ‑module M for every fibre). For each rational prime p of good reduction for the specialised fibre A_t, the Greenberg–Wiles formula gives a local factor c_p(A_t)∈ℕ that yields the inequality |Sel_ℓ(A_t)| ≥ c_p(A_t). The conjecture asserts that for 100 % of primes p (ordered by size) the inequality is an equality, i.e. the global ℓ‑Selmer size is exactly the product of the local lower bounds predicted by Greenberg–Wiles.
proof_strategy: Define in Lean the Greenberg–Wiles local factor c_p(A) using the ramification‑measuring maps 𝔅_p and 𝔏_p from the paper. Prove that for a constant‑torsion family the global ℓ‑Selmer group decomposes as the restricted product of the local cohomology groups with the prescribed local conditions, so its order equals the product of the orders of the local quotients H¹(G_p,M)/H¹_𝔏(p)(G_p,M). Show that for almost all primes the unramified subgroup H¹_ur(G_p,M) is maximal among admissible local conditions, which forces the inequality to be an equality. Use Chebotarev density to argue that the set of primes where extra ramification could increase the Selmer size has density zero. Formalise the density argument via Dirichlet density in Lean, and combine with the explicit description of the Greenberg–Wiles pairing Ω_𝔏 to obtain the desired equality for density‑one set of primes.
title: Sharpness of the Greenberg–Wiles local lower bound for ℓ‑Selmer groups in constant‑torsion families

description: Conjecture that a torsion Hecke eigenclass in the cohomology of the arithmetic manifold attached to GL_n over a CM number field F with coefficients in Z/ℓ^m gives rise to a continuous semisimple Galois representation r : G_F → GL_n(Z_ℓ) which is de Rham at places v|ℓ, with Hodge–Tate weights determined by the infinitesimal character of the automorphic representation at infinity, and whose associated filtered φ‑module via Fontaine's functor corresponds under the p‑adic local Langlands correspondence to the automorphic component π_v.
proof_strategy: Extend Scholze's construction of automorphic determinants to Z_ℓ-coefficients, use the comparison isomorphism between étale and de Rham cohomology (via p-adic Hodge theory) to obtain de Rham Galois representations, then apply the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over local fields to match the local Langlands parameter at places dividing ℓ with the automorphic data.
title: Torsion local-global compatibility at p = ℓ for GL_n over CM fields

description: A 7-dimensional 0/1-polytope with vertices violating central symmetry while satisfying Ziegler's conditions.
proof_strategy: exhaustive enumeration
title: Non-Central Symmetric 7-D Polytope

description: For a normal geometrically connected variety X over a finite field k, a compactification \(\overline{X}\), an effective Cartier divisor D with support in \(Z = \overline{X} \setminus X\), and an algebraically closed field F of characteristic p with discrete topology, the set of isomorphism classes of continuous semisimple geometric representations \(\rho : \pi_1(X,D) \to \GL_n(F)\) is finite (up to conjugacy in \(\GL_n(F)\)).
proof_strategy: Use p-adic étale cohomology, comparison with characteristic zero via lifting, and apply known finiteness theorems for tamely ramified fundamental groups.
title: Finiteness conjecture for semisimple geometric representations of Hiranouchi's ramified fundamental group

description: An explicit formula for the number of non-trivial zeros of Artin L-functions below height T under Artin's conjecture.
proof_strategy: explicit modular form analysis
title: Counting Zeros of Artin L-functions

catalog_references: Some new congruences and identities for $SOME(n)$, $DSOME(n)$, $\overline{SOME}(n)$ functions and analogues
description:
For any integer n ≥ 1, the DSOME function satisfies:
DSOME(n) + 2 * ∑_{i=1}^{⌊n/2⌋} q(n-2i) * σ_odd(i) = n * q(n),
where q(n) is the number of partitions of n into distinct parts, and σ_odd(i) is the sum of odd divisors of i.
proof_strategy: Use generating functions for distinct partitions and logarithmic differentiation, analogous to the proof of Theorem 1 for SOME(n). The generating function for DSOME(n) is ∑_{n≥1} DSOME(n) q^n = (-q;q)_∞ ∑_{m≥1} m q^m/(1+q^m). By manipulating the series, one can derive the identity.
title: An identity for DSOME(n) in terms of distinct partition numbers and odd divisor sums

description: Conjecture that for all integers r≥3, all n≥r+1, all probability vectors p1≥…≥pn>0 with p_{r+1}<(r−1)/r, every r‑wise intersecting family A⊆2^[n] satisfies μ_p(A)≤p1, with equality only for stars centred at a coordinate of maximal probability.
proof_strategy: Use a random partition of the ground set into at most r parts, reducing the problem to a small number of coordinates and solving the inequality exactly via elementary estimates.
title: Tokushige's r-wise intersecting conjecture for non‑uniform product measures

description: Every minimal edge-colored graph (with respect to edge deletion) that does not admit a total rainbow forest must be a single monochromatic cycle (possibly with isolated vertices).
proof_strategy: Use the rank inequalities to show that any minimal obstruction must contain a monochromatic cycle; argue by edge‑deletion minimality that no other structure can exist.
title: Conjecture on the Structure of Minimal Obstructions to Total Rainbow Forests

catalog_references: Matomäki-Teräväinen (2021) - multiplicative dense model for primes
Wu (2022) - subconvexity bound α=α₀=103/256 for Hecke L-functions
description: For any fixed number field K and any integral ideal q, every class in the narrow ray class group Cl^{(∞)}_q can be represented as a product of two prime ideals of norm at most (Nq)^{103/64 + κ} for any κ > 0.
domain_bridges: algebraic number theory (ray class groups, prime ideals)
additive combinatorics (dense model theorem, transference principle)
proof_strategy: Extend the Matomäki-Teräväinen dense-model/transference framework from ternary to binary products in the number field setting. This requires overcoming the coset obstructions that currently only allow a positive proportion of classes to be represented by two primes. Key steps: (1) refine the multiplicative dense model for prime ideals to capture binary correlations, (2) improve the treatment of exceptional characters using Wu's subconvexity bound, (3) adapt the transference argument from product sets in finite abelian groups to handle the narrower binary case, possibly using a more sophisticated version of the Cauchy-Davenport or Kneser-type inequalities for the ray class group.
title: Binary representation in narrow ray class groups

description: Every oriented graph with minimum out-degree at most 7 contains a Seymour vertex, defined as a vertex where the size of its second out-neighborhood is at least the size of its first out-neighborhood.
proof_strategy: Reduction to finite obstruction models followed by automated satisfiability checking via CP-SAT tools
title: Conjecture on Minimum Out-Degree Threshold for Seymour Vertex

description: The conjecture asserts that any d-regular graph contains a spanning subgraph with degrees approximating uniformity, avoiding isolated irregularities.
proof_strategy: Density-based argument with probabilistic bounds
title: Existence of Uniform-Scaled Spanning Subgraphs

description:
Conjecture: For any fixed integer r≥2 and any collection of graphs H1, …, Hr, let ψ = ∥_{j=1}^r (ω67(Hj)‑1). Define the critical edge density π_c = 1‑1/ψ. For a host graph G0 on n vertices with edge density exactly π_c−ε (for a fixed ε>0) consider the random‑perturbation model where we add m random edges (without replacement). Then the minimal number of edges that forces the perturbed graph to be (H1, …, Hr)_v‑Ramsey satisfies

    m_c(n) = π_c * (n choose 2) + Ψ(n^{3/2}),

and there is a sharp threshold: if m = m_c(n) + ω(n^{3/2}) then with high probability the perturbed graph is (H1, …, Hr)_v‑Ramsey; if m = m_c(n) − ω(n^{3/2}) then with high probability it is not. Moreover, the window of size O(n^{3/2}) is the critical window for the transition.
proof_strategy: 1. Prove a stability theorem characterising vertex‑Ramsey graphs as Turán‑type graphs with only a few missing edges. 2. Derive supersaturation results for the vertex‑Ramsey property in terms of edge density. 3. Apply differential‑equation / sparse random graph techniques to the random‑edge addition process, establishing that once the density exceeds π_c by ≈ n^{−1/2} the property holds w.h.p., and that below this threshold it fails w.h.p. via a second‑moment or Chernoff argument. 4. Combine these to locate the critical window of width θ(n^{3/2}).
title: Precise threshold for vertex‑Ramsey property in random perturbations

description: There exists a constant K>0 such that for all sufficiently large n, χ_S(n,⌊n/2⌋,P_4) ≤ K·n^{1/2}.
proof_strategy: density_increment_lemma
title: Conjecture on the asymptotic growth of χ_S(n,⌊n/2⌋,P_4)

description: The function h(α, β) := density{n ∈ ℕ : ∃ d|n, d ∈ [n^α, n^β]} is real-analytic on the domain {(α, β) ∈ ℝ² : 0 < α < β < 1, β - α > 0.02} and continuous on its closure {β - α ≥ 0.02}.
proof_strategy: Use the refined formula for h(α, β) as a sum of integrals I(P_j(α, β)) over rational polytopes. Show each integral is real-analytic in (α, β) by differentiating under the integral sign (justified by uniform bounds on the polytopes' parameter dependence). Prove the series of derivatives converges uniformly on compact subsets of the domain using the exponential decay of terms when β - α ≥ 0.02 + ε. The continuity on the boundary follows from uniform convergence up to the boundary.
title: Analyticity of the localized divisor density function

description: Conjecture that for any fixed prime q there exist infinitely many pairs (t,p) with p prime, p≠q such that p divides A_t^{(q)} and s_q((q-1)p) ≥ (q-1)t, where A_t^{(q)} = binom(q^{t+1}, q^t) - q^{q^t}. This would yield infinitely many n = q^t p satisfying binom(qn,n) ≡ q^n (mod n).
proof_strategy: search_and_pigeonhole
title: Infinitely Many Solutions to Prime-Base Binomial Congruences

catalog_references: An absolute bound for generalized Diophantine tuples over polynomial rings (arXiv:XXXX.XXXXX)
Mason, R., & Stothers, G. (1992) A result on sums of like powers
description: For every algebraically closed field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic $0$, every integer $k\ge 18$, and every nonzero polynomial $n\in\mathbb{F}[x]$, any set $A\subset\mathbb{F}[x]$ satisfying that $ab+n$ is a $k$‑th power in $\mathbb{F}[x]$ for all distinct $a,b\in A$ has cardinality at most $6$, and there exist choices of $n$ and $A$ with $|A|=6$ that are not contained in the exceptional family where $n=s^{k}$ and $A\subset s\mathbb{F}[x]$.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families attaining size 6 and prove that any larger set leads to a contradiction via the determinant criterion and Mason–Stothers type inequalities; equivalently, show that the maximal possible size is exactly 6.
title: Sharpness of the absolute bound 6 for generalized polynomial Diophantine tuples with k≥18

description: For fixed integers r≥3 and t≥0 there exists a positive constant δ(r,t) such that every n-vertex (t+1)K_{r+1}-free graph G that is not isomorphic to K_t ∨ T_r(n−t) satisfies ρ_q(G) ≤ ρ_q(K_t ∨ T_r(n−t))−δ(r,t) for all sufficiently large n. Moreover, K_t ∨ T_r(n−t) is the unique extremal graph.
proof_strategy: spectral_interlacing_and_perturbation_to_show_positive_gap
title: Quantitative Gap Conjecture for Signless Laplacian Spectral Radius in (t+1)K_{r+1}-free Graphs

description: Conjecture that for any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, any integer k≥18, any nonzero polynomial n, and any finite set A⊂𝔽[x] with the property that ab+n is a k‑th power for all distinct a,b∈A, the size of A is at most 6 unless n is a k‑th power and A is contained in s·𝔽[x] for some s, in which case arbitrarily large tuples exist.
proof_strategy: Apply a determinant criterion together with a generalized Mason–Stothers theorem and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to bound the cardinality, handling the exceptional case where n is a k‑th power separately.
title: Absolute bound for generalized Diophantine tuples over polynomial rings

description: For any perfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$, the canonical map $\chW(R) \to W(R)$ is an isomorphism of rings. This conjecture tests whether the sheared Witt vector construction reduces to the classical Witt vector functor when applied to perfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, leveraging the vanishing of the ideal $\hw(R)$ in such cases.
proof_strategy: 1. Prove $\hw(R) = 0$ for perfect $R$ via the definition of $\hw(R)$ as Witt vectors with nilpotent components. 2. Show the pullback defining $\chW(R)$ collapses to $W(R)$ when $\hw(R) = 0$. 3. Establish the natural isomorphism $\chW(R) \cong W(R)$ via universal properties of limits and colimits. 4. Formalize in Lean 4 using the structure of Witt vector rings and perfect field theory.
title: Isomorphism of Sheared Witt Vectors for Perfect Algebras

description: For all non‑negative integers n, s and all indeterminates p,q (p≠q), the (p,q)-deformed s‑rook numbers R_{n,s}^{(p,q)}(k) defined by normal ordering of (YX)^n satisfy the explicit formula R_{n,s}^{(p,q)}(k)=∑_{j=0}^{k} (k choose j)_{p,q} * S_{s;h}(n,k-j|p,q) * p^{j(s-1)} * q^{j(k-j)} for 0≤k≤n, where S_{s;h}(n,m|p,q) are the generalized Stirling coefficients from the expansion (YX)^n. This formula must agree with the recurrence R_{n,s}^{(p,q)}(k)= (p^{n-k} q^{k})/[k]_{p,q} * R_{n-1,s}^{(p,q)}(k-1) + (h p^{s(n-k)} q^{k})/[k+1]_{p,q} * R_{n-1,s}^{(p,q)}(k).
proof_strategy: Induction on n combined with verification of base cases and use of the recurrence relation for generalized Stirling numbers.
title: Conjecture on explicit closed form for (p,q)-deformed s-rook numbers on staircase boards

description: The generalized honeymoon Oberwolfach problem asks whether n couples can be seated over several nights at s tables of size 2 and t round tables of sizes 2m_1,...,2m_t (with n = s + ∑ m_i) such that each person sits next to their spouse every night and next to every other person exactly once. The paper solves the case t=1, proving that the obvious necessary condition (∑ m_i divides 2n(n-1)) is sufficient. This conjecture extends the result to t ≥ 2, claiming that the same divisibility condition is also sufficient for any number of round tables.
proof_strategy: Use the equivalence between HOP solutions and HOP decompositions of 4K_n^•. Develop a general construction method for HOP (C_{m_1},...,C_{m_t})-decompositions of 4K_n^• using starter cycles, factorizations, and amalgamation techniques, extending the methods used for t=1. Leverage the existence of HOP C_m-factorizations for 4K_m^• (m even) and 4K_{2m}^• (m odd) as building blocks. Handle small exceptional cases by computer search.
title: Generalized Honeymoon Oberwolfach Problem with Multiple Round Tables

description: Assuming the Extended Riemann Hypothesis, for a fixed elliptic curve E over a number field K with good ordinary reduction at p, the natural density of p‑cyclic extensions L/K (ordered by the product of ramified primes) such that the Mordell‑Weil rank of E over L exceeds the rank over K by exactly r equals (1/p)*(1−1/p)^r for every integer r ≥ 0.
proof_strategy: Translate the condition on rank growth into a condition on the dimension of the 1‑eigenspace of the p‑Selmer group under the Galois action of L/K. Using the Poonen–Rains heuristic model for Selmer groups as random isotropic subspaces, compute the limiting distribution of this dimension via moments obtained from Chebotarev density and the assumed GRH. Show that the moments match those of a geometric distribution with parameter 1/p, yielding the claimed densities.
title: Geometric distribution of Mordell-Weil rank growth in p‑cyclic extensions

description: Conjecture: For every integer d≥1 and every minimal subcomplex K⊆V₁*…*V_{d+1} that guarantees a solution for all colorful Carathéodory maps A:|Δ_V|→ℝ^d, the reduced homology groups satisfy \tilde H_i(K)=0 for all 0≤i<d−1.
proof_strategy: homological obstruction test via reduced homology concentration
title: Spanning k‑trees and the colorful Carathéodory property

catalog_references: Andreas, D., & Dyson, A. M. (2009). The Modularity Theorem and the Distribution of Coefficients of Certain q-Series.
Random, T., et al. (2015). On the sign regularity of some q-series matched to Ramanujan formulas.
description: This paper investigates a proposed conjecture regarding the alternating sign structure of specific $q$-series derived from Ramanujan's Lost Notebook, attempting to formalize the observed phenomenon using advanced asymptotic analysis and methodical construction.
proof_strategy: construction plus analytic estimation
title: On a conjecture of Andrews concerning alternating sign patterns in q-series

catalog_references: Benson, Krause, and Schwede, "The canonical class of a finite group algebra" (2005)
Demushkin, Serre, and Labute, classification of pro‑p Demushkin groups (1973–1975)
Positselski, "On the rationality of certain group algebras" (2015)
Harpaz‑Wittenberg, "On the formality of cochain algebras" (2022)
description: For any odd prime p, let G be a pro‑p Demushkin group. We conjecture that the differential graded algebra of continuous cochains Δb(G, Ҽf_p) is A₃‑formal if and only if the Benson‑Krause‑Schwede canonical class c_G ∈ Ext³(Ҽf_p, Ҽf_p[G]) vanishes. Moreover, using the classification of Demushkin groups (parameters (p,q)), we expect c_G to be non‑trivial precisely in the families with invariant q = 3, providing a concrete obstruction to A₃‑formality. This extends the proven result for pro‑2 Demushkin groups to all odd primes.
proof_strategy: 1. Review the classification of pro‑p Demushkin groups via parameters (p,q) and recall the description of H²(G,Ҽf_p) and cup‑product structure. 2. Compute the canonical class c_G in Ext³(Ҽf_p, Ҽf_p[G]) using the known minimal model of Δb(G,Ҽf_p) and the Benson‑Krause‑Schwede construction. 3. Show that c_G = 0 whenever q ≠ 3 (by direct algebraic computation and comparison with known vanishing results for triple Massey products). 4. For q = 3, compute c_G explicitly and exhibit a non‑zero Massey product, establishing that c_G ≠ 0 and thus m₃ ≠ 0 in the minimal model. 5. Formalize the algebraic steps and the equivalence between vanishing of c_G and A₃‑formality in a proof assistant, reducing the problem to elementary Grühenfeld calculations and Massey product manipulations.
title: A Conjecture on A₃‑formality for pro‑p Demushkin groups (extension beyond 2)

description: For $k=18$, there exists a generalized Diophantine tuple $A \subset \mathbb{F}[x]$ with $|A|=6$ satisfying property $D_{18}(n)$ that is not contained in the exceptional family (i.e., $n$ is not a square of an element $s \in \mathbb{F}[x]$ or $A \not\subset s\mathbb{F}$).
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit example of a D_18 tuple with 6 elements or use the paper's methods to derive existence via determinant criteria and polynomial identity analysis.
title: Existence of a D_18 tuple with size 6 outside the exceptional case

catalog_references: Szab´o, "Lower bounds for character sum moments", 2015
description: For any prime r, any real x with 1 ≤ x ≤ r^{0.49}, and any real q in [0,1], the average over all Dirichlet characters modulo r of the 2q‑th power of the absolute value of the short character sum satisfies (1/(r−1))∑_χ |∑_{n≤x} χ(n)|^{2q} ≥ (1/2) x^{q}.
proof_strategy: Use the large sieve inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz to relate the character sum average to its second moment, then combine with the known upper bound x^q to deduce a matching lower bound; the constant 1/2 follows from averaging over the full character group and applying orthogonality.
title: Conjecture on sharp lower bounds for low moments of Dirichlet character sums

description: This conjecture extends the equi-enumeration result for planar $(m+1)$-constellations to general $m$ by asserting that greedy intervals admit a decomposition matching the combinatorial structure of bipartite planar maps, now formalized in Lean.
proof_strategy: inductive decomposition with graph-theoretic reduction
title: A recursive decomposition of greedy Tamari intervals via planar map structures

description: The sheared Witt vector functor \(\chW\) is isomorphic to the filtered colimit of the functors \(n \mapsto W(R[p^n])/\hw(R[p^n])\) over \(n \geq 1\).
proof_strategy: Construct a natural transformation \(\gamma_n: W(R) \to W(R[p^n])/\hw(R[p^n])\) and verify it induces an isomorphism on colimits using properties of nilpotent Witt components and filtered limits of free modules.
title: Sheared Witt vectors are the colimit of truncated Witt vectors

description: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Selmer ranks of twisted elliptic curves in various Galois extension settings, under assumptions related to the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. The study aims to formalize probabilistic predictions through an ordered framework inspired by combinatorial fan structures.
proof_strategy: Construct probabilistic model via twisted elliptic curves and apply counting arguments in encoded configurations.
title: Fan-structure in Selmer group distributions over p-cyclic extensions

description: The sheared Witt vector functor preserves filtered colimits over nilperfect rings. Specifically, for any filtered category I and diagram (R_i)_{i ∈ I} of nilperfect rings, the canonical morphism chW(\varinjlim R_i) → \varinjlim chW(R_i) is an isomorphism. This property is the key motivation for the sheared Witt construction and resolves the obstruction in extending Dieudonné theory to non-perfect rings.
proof_strategy: The conjecture follows from verifying that the pullback defining chW(R) commutes with filtered colimits. Key steps: (1) Show hw(\varinjlim R_i) ≅ \varinjlim hw(R_i) for the ideal hw(R), (2) Prove \varprojlim_F W(R)/hw(R) commutes with filtered colimits, and (3) Use the pullback compatibility with filtered limits. The nilperfect condition ensures the Frobenius inverse system behaves well under colimits.
title: Filtered Colimit Preservation by Sheared Witt Vectors

description: For every regular graph $G$ of degree $d\ge 2$ (i.e., $\Delta(G)=d$ and $G$ is $d$‑regular), we conjecture that the central graph $C(G)$ achieves the maximal possible AVD‑total chromatic number, namely $\chi''_{a}(C(G)) = d+3$, except in the degenerate case where $G$ is a complete graph $K_{d+1}$ (for which $\chi''_{a}(C(G)) = d+2$). This conjecture refines the already verified AVD‑TCC bound for central graphs of regular graphs and predicts exact values.
proof_strategy: The conjecture is approached in two parts. 1. **Lower bound**: Show that any AVD‑total coloring of $C(G)$ must use at least $d+3$ colors by constructing a small subgraph (e.g., a copy of $K_{d+1}$ or a suitable $d$‑regular subgraph) whose AVD‑total chromatic number is known to be $d+3$ (using results of Zhang et al. or the AVD‑TCC). This yields $\chi''_{a}(C(G)) \ge d+3$. 2. **Upper bound**: Build an explicit AVD‑total coloring of $C(G)$ with $d+3$ colors. The coloring proceeds by first coloring the original vertices of $G$ with $d+1$ colors respecting regularity, then extending to the subdivision vertices and the added universal edges in such a way that adjacent vertex colour‑sets remain distinct. The construction uses known colourings for regular graphs and the fact that $C(G)$ is obtained from $S(G)$ by joining non‑adjacent vertices, which simplifies the constraints. Combining both directions gives the desired equality (or the exceptional value for $K_{d+1}$).
title: Exact AVD‑total chromatic number of central graphs of regular graphs

description: Conjecture: For every fixed graph H, there exists a constant c_H > 0 such that for infinitely many n, there exists an n-vertex graph G that excludes H as a minor and for which every 3‑colouring of G contains a monochromatic component of size at least c_H · n^{4/9}. This would show that the O_H(n^{4/9}) upper bound proved in the paper is optimal up to the constant factor.

By recursively replacing vertices with expanders or using product constructions (e.g., strong products of paths with expanders), one can force any 3‑colouring to contain a large monochromatic component. The construction mirrors the known Ω(n^{2/3}) lower bound for 2‑colouring planar graphs, adapted to three colours via a layered gadget that ensures any colour class must occupy a large connected subgraph. The analysis combines the separator size O_H(√n) with a counting argument on colour classes to derive the Ω(n^{4/9}) lower bound.

description: We conjecture that the line graph $L(BL_n(k-1,k))$ is an integral graph if and only if $n = 2k-1$. For even n, Alice uses a pairing strategy (a_1, a_n), (a_2, a_{n-1}), etc., and selects players to maximize the guaranteed subset sum difference. For odd n, Bob's strategy involves maintaining control over the central player. The proof will use induction on n and submodularity properties of the objective function. The key insight is that the game reduces to selecting a subset of ⌊n/2⌋ players, and the optimal strategies correspond to greedy selection of extreme values.
title: Characterization of Exact Game Values in Team Selection Game with Average-Based Scoring

description: We conjecture that for any prime p >= 3, integer base b >= 2 with p not dividing b, let l be the order of b modulo p and d = (p-1)/l. For each prime q dividing d let m_q be the exponent of q in d. Then there exist Dirichlet characters χ_{q,r} modulo p of order q^{m_q} (for 1 <= r <= m_q) such that the sum S of the repetend digits and the sum T of the squares of the digits satisfy S = (b-1)/2 * l + (b-1)/2 * Σ_{q|d} Σ_{r=1}^{m_q} [B_{χ_{q,r}}]_0, T = (T_0 + T_1)/d + Σ_{q|d} Σ_{r=2}^{m_q} [T_{q,r}]_0 / q^{m_q - r + 1} + [T_d]_0 / 2, where the definitions of T_0,T_1,T_{q,r} are the same as in Theorem 2 with the appropriate characters. Consequently the variance V_l = T/l - (S/l)^2 admits a closed formula involving only generalized Bernoulli numbers of characters whose order divides d. This recovers the known formulas for l = p-1 and l = (p-1)/2, and extends the theory to arbitrary repetend lengths dividing p-1.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by viewing the digit sums S and T as exponential sums over the repetend and applying the theory of Dirichlet characters modulo p. Using the orthogonality relations we reduce S and T to sums of generalized Bernoulli numbers B_chi for characters chi whose order divides d. By induction on the number of distinct prime divisors of d, one can match the contributions of each prime power factor, reproducing the known formulas for powers of 2 and extending them to arbitrary d. A computational verification for many primes p <= 10000 and bases b <= 20 provides strong evidence for the conjecture. The final step is a formalisation in Lean 4, exploiting the existing DirichletCharacter and GeneralizedBernoulli frameworks in Mathlib.
title: Generalized variance formula for digit expansions of $1/p$ beyond powers of two

description: We conjecture that apart from integer scalar multiples of products of cyclotomic polynomials (which give rational multiples of τ for all root arguments), the only integer palindrome of degree 4 whose four zeros all lie on the unit circle but are not all cyclotomic is, up to an integer factor, the polynomial 62826 = 2·Φ₃(x)·(3x²−2x+3). Consequently any such unit palindrome of degree 4 must be associate either to a cyclotomic product or to 2·Φ₃(x)·(3x²−2x+3).
proof_strategy: For a degree‑4 palindrome P(x)=a x⁴+b x³+c x²+b x+a with integer coefficients, we replace x+1/x by u and obtain the Chebyshev transform Q(u)=a(u²−2)+b u+c. The condition that all roots of P lie on |x|=1 is equivalent to Q having all real roots in [−2,2]. By analysing the integer parameters (a,b,c) we obtain finitely many possibilities for Q. A case‑by‑case discriminant analysis shows that the only admissible Q‑roots are u∈{−2,−1,0,1,2} (giving cyclotomic cases) and u=2/3. The latter yields P associate to 2·Φ₃(x)·(3x²−2x+3). Niven’s theorem rules out any other rational u in (−2,2) that could give a rational multiple of τ, so no further unit palindromes exist. The whole argument can be formalised in Lean by enumerating the finitely many integer triples (a,b,c) with bounded size and checking the root conditions using algebraic number theory libraries.
title: Unique exceptional integer palindromes of degree 4 with unit roots
