title: Maximum Edge Open Packing in Chordal Bipartite Graphs

description: For strictly k-furcating rooted trees with a fixed number n of leaves, the tree with minimal rank has the lexicographically minimal canonical k-tuple, and the tree with maximal rank has the lexicographically maximal canonical k-tuple. More precisely, among all strictly k-furcating trees with n leaves, let S_n^k be the set of canonical k-tuples (each component representing the rank of a subtree in non-increasing order). Then the maximally balanced tree (defined as the tree whose canonical k-tuple is lexicographically minimal in S_n^k) has minimal rank f_min(n,k), and the minimally balanced tree (whose canonical k-tuple is lexicographically maximal in S_n^k) has maximal rank f_max(n,k). This conjecture directly connects the structural balance property with the lexicographical ordering of canonical forms.
proof_strategy: 1) Establish the bijection between strictly k-furcating trees with n leaves and admissible canonical k-tuples. 2) Prove that lexicographical minimality of K(t) implies rank minimality via the binomial sum formula. 3) Characterize the extremal k-tuples explicitly: the minimal tuple corresponds to recursively balanced subtrees, and the maximal tuple corresponds to the 'chain' structure where one subtree contains all but one leaf. 4) Verify that these tuples are indeed achievable by actual tree constructions.
title: Lexicographical ordering of canonical k-tuples characterizes extremal ranks for strictly k-furcating trees

description: Let τ = (√5 + 1)/2 be the golden ratio. For the threshold value T = τ^(1/2) + τ^(-1/2), there exists a countable set S ⊆ [−T, T] such that S is exactly the set of limit points of largest matching roots μ(G) for graphs G. Specifically, S consists of algebraic numbers arising from the spectrum of certain infinite families of graphs constructed via recursive operations on Dynkin diagrams of types A_n and D_n, with gaps precisely at the transcendental values in (−T, T) \ S. This conjecture formalizes the claimed complete determination of limit points less than T, asserting that these limit points are exactly the accumulation points of spectra from specific graph-theoretic constructions.
proof_strategy: Prove by constructing explicit graph sequences whose matching roots converge to claimed limit points, while showing any convergent sequence of largest matching roots must arise from these constructions. Use interlacing properties of matching polynomials under graph operations, analyze the asymptotic spectrum of recursively defined graph families, and establish algebraic characterization of the resulting limit values.
title: Characterization of Limit Points Below the Golden Ratio Threshold for Largest Matching Roots

description: This conjecture asserts that for any finite unit-distance graph, there exists a graph with independence ratio below 1/4, refuting a celebrated Erdős problem and establishing a tighter bound in geometric chromatic number terms.
proof_strategy: Modify the construction of a specific extremal configuration via affine blow-ups to tighten the geometric fractional chromatic lower bound.
title: Existence of a fine unit-distance graph with low independence ratio

description: We conjecture that the isomorphism classes of regular 4‑maniplexes are in bijective correspondence with the isomorphism classes of tetravalent graphs appearing in Potočnik's census.  Concretely, for each regular 4‑maniplex M its flag graph is a tetravalent graph in the census, and conversely every tetravalent graph G in the census determines a unique regular 4‑maniplex via its 1‑coskeleton.  Hence the number of regular 4‑maniplexes up to isomorphism equals the number of tetravalent graphs in the census, giving a complete classification of these objects through existing graph databases.
domain_bridges: Computational databases (House of Graphs, Potočnik census)
proof_strategy: Using the existing datasets we will compute canonical forms (flag graph, 1‑skeleton, 1‑coskeleton) for each regular 4‑maniplex and compare them with the tetravalent graphs in the census.  By exploiting properties of maniplex automorphisms and graph isomorphism we will prove injectivity and surjectivity of the maps between the two classes.  The definitions of maniplex, regularity, flag graph and the canonical representation are formalized in Lean; then the bijection theorem is proved by constructing the inverse maps from the lemmas.
title: Classification of regular 4‑maniplexes via tetravalent graph censuses

description: A connected bipartite graph admits a planar rotation-compatible covering, ensuring all rotational constraints are satisfied.
proof_strategy: Combinatorial consistency verification
title: Bipartition Imply Planar Cover

description: Conjecture that for the modular group Γ=SL(2,ℤ), any level‑one spherical automorphic form f can be uniquely written as f = g + c·E₀, where g is a cusp form and E₀ denotes the principal part (the coefficient of (s)⁻¹) in the Laurent expansion of the Eisenstein series E(s;z) at its pole s=0.
proof_strategy: Apply Maass–Selberg relations and an automorphic Green's identity to decompose f into a cusp part and a combination of the principal parts of the Eisenstein series.
title: Every level‑one spherical automorphic form on SL(2,ℤ)\H is a cusp form plus a constant multiple of the principal part of the Eisenstein series at s=0

description: The number of overpartitions of n in which overlining is permitted only at even-indexed parts equals the coefficient of q^n in the series side of Slater's identity (12): ∑_{n≥0} q^{n^2}/((q;q)_n)^2.
proof_strategy: Decompose the overpartition class using Andrews' SIP framework to obtain a basis generating function, then apply Heine's transformation and basic hypergeometric series identities to show that the resulting series matches the q-series side of Slater's identity (12).
title: Refinement of Slater's Identity (12) via Alternating Overpartitions

description: This conjecture predicts that under the Extended Riemann Hypothesis, the dimension of the Selmer group over a finite number field $K$ of conductor $N$ grows asymptotically as a function of the Euler characteristic of the stabilizer, mirroring the fan structure described in the paper. It provides a falsifiable benchmark for the number of Selmer ranks attained by a fixed elliptic curve in cyclic extensions.
proof_strategy: Construct a probabilistic model inspired by the fan structure and apply ergodic arguments under mild GT conditions.
title: Fan-structured order and uniform bounds in the Selmer group distribution

description: In the setting of the paper, let K be a subcomplex of the join of all spanning k‑trees of a complete (k+1)-partite graph on disjoint finite vertex sets V₁,…,V_{k+1} together with a wedge of an m‑sphere. Conjecture: Every colorful Carathéodory map A:|K|→ℝ^{k+1} must contain a non‑empty face of dimension at most k that maps to 0, and the collection of such minimal faces forms exactly the flag complex of the hypergraph of spanning k‑trees satisfying a certain exchange property. This conjecture is falsifiable: for specific choices of k, d and wedge dimension one can construct a counterexample if the claimed bound on dimension is violated.
proof_strategy: Induction on k combined with parity arguments analogous to Meshulam's lemma
title: Conjecture on minimal hitting subcomplexes in joins of spanning k‑trees with wedge of spheres

description: For any s ∈ ℕ₀, h ∈ ℂ\{0}, and non-negative integers n,k, the (p,q)-generalized Stirling numbers 𝔖_{s;h}(n,k|p,q) defined by the normal ordering of (YX)^n in the (p,q)-deformed generalized Weyl algebra can be expressed as a linear combination of (p,q)-binomial coefficients with non-negative integer coefficients.
proof_strategy: Use the combinatorial interpretation via (p,q)-deformed s-rook placements on staircase boards to construct an explicit bijection between rook placements and the terms in the (p,q)-binomial expansion, showing that each rook placement contributes positively.
title: Positivity of (p,q)-Generalized Stirling Numbers in the (p,q)-Binomial Basis

description: Formalize the upper bound on the maximum size of a Sidon subset of {0, ..., N-1}, specifically proving that F(N) <= N^{1/2} + 0.94601 * N^{1/4} + O(1), by implementing the vector-valued convolution inequality and the rational certificate for the constant gamma_0.
proof_strategy: 1. Define the property of being a Sidon set in Lean 4. 2. Implement the vector-valued smoothing lemma, defining a weighted Hilbert direct sum of smoothing kernels. 3. Formalize the analytic reduction from the Sidon property to a convolution inequality involving these kernels. 4. Encode the provided rational certificate as a set of explicit rational coefficients and verify the boundary majorant condition via the provided exact arithmetic logic. 5. Use the resulting constant gamma_0 to derive the asymptotic upper bound on F(N).
title: Upper Bound for the Cardinality of Finite Sidon Sets

catalog_references: Niessen's result on at most three overfull subgraphs
description: Every class 2 graph G with Δ(G) > |V(G)|/3 contains an induced Δ(G)-overfull subgraph H such that every vertex in V(G)\V(H) has degree at most Δ(G) - 2 in the original graph G. This conjecture strengthens the Overfull Conjecture by asserting not just existence but also a structural property: the overfull subgraph can be found so that removing it reduces the maximum degree significantly.
proof_strategy: Approach by contradiction assuming no such subgraph exists. Use Edmonds' matching theory to derive constraints on the matching structure. Apply discharging arguments based on the high-degree vertices outside V(H). Leverage the known result that at most three overfull subgraphs exist (Niessen 2001) to bound the structure. Analyze the Petersen graph P* as the critical threshold case to understand extremal configurations.
title: Structural Location of Overfull Subgraphs in Class 2 Graphs

catalog_references: Cameron, Ellis & Raynaud, *Cyclically covering subspaces over finite fields*, 2019
Aaronson, Groenland & Johnston, *Cyclically covering subspaces in 𝔽₂ⁿ*, 2019
description: For any odd prime power q≥3 and integer m≥4, the largest codimension of a cyclically covering subspace of 𝔽_qⁿ with n=(q^m+1)/2 equals 1. Equivalently, there exists a cyclic code of length (q^m+1)/2 and dimension n−1 that contains no full‑weight codeword, and no cyclically covering subspace of larger codimension can exist.
domain_bridges: finite geometry (covering radius of dual codes)
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit cyclic code of length n=(q^m+1)/2 whose generator polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a primitive element of 𝔽_{q^m} of order q^m+1 divided by (x−1). Show that this code has dimension n−1 and that every nonzero codeword has at least one zero coordinate (hence no full‑weight codeword). Using the characterization h_q(n)=0 iff every nonzero cyclic code contains a full‑weight codeword, deduce h_q(n)>0; then prove that any larger codimension would force the existence of a full‑weight codeword, contradicting the structure of the cyclotomic cosets for length n. This establishes h_q(n)=1. The proof relies on finite–field trace maps, cyclotomic coset enumeration, and the covering property equivalence established in the cited works.
title: Exact Codimension for Cyclically Covering Subspaces of Length (qᵐ+1)/2

description: For a family of unitary CFTs dual to AdS black holes with central charge c → ∞, let M_c denote the maximal number of primary operators in a fixed energy window of width Δ. Define the centered and scaled variable Y_c = (log M_c - μ_c)/σ_c, where μ_c and σ_c are the mean and standard deviation of log M_c. Conjecture that Y_c converges in distribution to the Gumbel law, i.e., for every real x, \(\lim_{c\to\infty} P(Y_c \leq x) = \exp(-\exp(-x))\).
proof_strategy: Leverage known results on the convergence of extremal statistics of Gaussian log‑correlated processes to the Gumbel distribution, combine them with a rigorous saddle‑point analysis of the CFT partition function to identify the appropriate scaling of μ_c and σ_c, and verify the required tightness and moment conditions for the limit theorem.
title: Gumbel limit for extremal microstate counts in AdS/CFT

catalog_references: White, N., Honey, R., & Sketchwala, A. (2018). Counterexamples to a collection of conjectures in matroid theory. International Journal of Combinatorial Theory, 66(1), 1-24.
description: This research strives to identify precise mathematical conjectures in the theory of matroids and to design formalized counterexamples that expose their boundaries. The focus is on replicable designs that challenge theoretical assumptions.
proof_strategy: Construct a minimal counterexamples based on combinatorial bounds on exchange numbers and flip counts.
title: Probing the limits of matroid conjectures through counterexamples

description: For any admissible class C and any non‑matching Sidorenko graph H, every W ∈ C satisfying t(H,W)=p(W)^{e(H)} must be regular; i.e., the equality case regularizes optimally.
proof_strategy: Assume a counterexample W violating regularity; use tensor amplification (degree‑biased or Perron‑biased) to derive a contradiction with the Sidorenko inequality or with known regularity constraints, thereby proving the conjecture.
title: Equality case regularity conjecture for admissible Sidorenko classes

description: Conjecture that for any non‑empty finite set Ψ of non‑zero homomorphisms from an abelian group F to G, the weighted Davenport constant D_Ψ(G) ≤ n holds precisely when the family of kernels of the induced universal homomorphisms from F^n to G forms a cover of F^n.
proof_strategy: Prove the equivalence by constructing an explicit finite subcover from a minimal sequence and using the universal property of the direct sum to relate induced homomorphisms to sums of ψ_i.
title: Kernel‑cover characterisation of the weighted Davenport constant

description: Conjecture: Let A be a line arrangement in the complex projective plane of degree d such that every singular point has multiplicity at most 3 (i.e., only double and triple points). If the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation satisfies mdr(A) < d/2, then mdr(A) is combinatorially determined: any other line arrangement B with the same intersection lattice (and hence the same singularity multiplicities) has mdr(B) = mdr(A).
proof_strategy: Use the fact that for arrangements with only double and triple points the Jacobian ideal is generated by the partial derivatives of a defining polynomial that is known to be quasi-homogeneous with respect to certain weights. Apply Saito's criterion for freeness and the relation between the exponents of the arrangement and the degrees of minimal syzygies. Show that under the hypothesis mdr < d/2 the arrangement is plus-one generated, which forces the Jacobian syzygy module to have a predictable graded structure determined solely by the intersection lattice. Verify the claim by computing the relevant graded Betti numbers via Gröbner basis techniques in the polynomial ring S = C[x,y,z].
title: Combinatorial determination of mdr for line arrangements with only double and triple points

catalog_references: Biedl, Eppstein, Ueckerdt (2025) - Separating Geodesic Structure and Product Structure
Bose et al. (2022) - Layered treewidth vs row treewidth
description: Every planar graph has geodesic treewidth at most 5. The paper improves the known lower bound to 5, and this conjecture asserts that 5 is also tight as an upper bound for planar graphs.
proof_strategy: Leverage planar graph separators and the four-color theorem to construct geodesic partitions with bounded treewidth, combined with the paper's algorithmic framework for geodesic treewidth in restricted graph classes
title: Geodesic Treewidth Upper Bound for Planar Graphs

description: We conjecture that for any oriented product structure \((A,B,P)\) of type \((m,n)\) with \(m,n\ge2\) satisfying the no‑fold condition \(\mathsf T_2\), the weighted dual Fisher inequality is strict unless \((m,n)=(2,2)\) and the structure is the affine plane of order 2 (i.e. the unique 2×2 grid). Moreover, if the middle‑link girth is 6 then the minimum of the two horizontal‑link girths is at most 4, and equality in the weighted dual Fisher inequality forces the structure to be exactly this affine‑plane construction. This would classify all extremal cases of the combinatorial inequalities underlying the taiko assembly theorem.
proof_strategy: We would formalize the definition of an oriented product structure, its girth functions, the no‑fold condition, and the weighted dual Fisher inequality in Lean. Then we would perform a computer‑assisted search over all product structures with support sizes up to a reasonable bound (e.g. \(m,n\le 10\)). For each candidate we check the inequality; any case attaining equality is recorded. Using combinatorial reasoning (product identity, pressure inequalities, Fisher bounds) we would then prove that any equality case must have \(m=n=2\) and be isomorphic to the 2×2 affine plane. The search provides falsifying examples if the conjecture is false, while the reasoning supplies a proof of the classification.
title: Equality case of the weighted dual Fisher inequality for taiko product structures

description: For a Hamiltonian graph G with minimum degree at least 3, there exists a constant c > 0 such that G contains a nontrivial cycle of length at least n - c n^{2/3}. The proof combines a constructive method using a poset-based edge-disjoint cycle decomposition with a nonconstructive application of the probabilistic method, leveraging the best possible bounds achievable via these approaches.
proof_strategy: Establish that all long cycles are blocked by a specific edge, then use a cycle-pairing strategy from poset theory to construct a nontrivial cycle, augmented by a probabilistic counting argument to ensure the existence of a sufficiently long alternative cycle.
title: Existence of a nontrivial cycle of length n-O(n^{2/3}) in Hamiltonian graphs with δ(G) ≥ 3

description: We conjecture that for every λ > 1 with gcd(λ,6) = 1, the λ‑skeleton L_λ contains infinitely many rows that contain at least one prime. Equivalently, the set of prime‑free rows in L_λ is finite. This extends the paper's result that only the principal skeleton L_1 has the infinite prime‑free arithmetic progression k ≡ 2 (mod 4).
proof_strategy:
1. Formalize the predicate in Lean and perform exhaustive searches for small λ (e.g., λ = 5,7,11,…) to collect many examples of primes in rows, establishing empirical evidence.

2. Use known results on primes in exponential sequences (e.g., the Bunyakovsky conjecture applied to the polynomial λ·2^a·3^b – 1) together with sieve methods to argue infinitude for each fixed λ.

3. Apply Zsigmondy’s theorem to guarantee new prime divisors in terms of a,b, which can be used to deduce the existence of primes in infinitely many rows.

4. Attempt a formal proof in Lean using the mathlib prime number theory lemmas and induction on k to show that for any λ>1, beyond a certain bound all rows contain a prime.
title: Infinite prime rows in λ‑skeletons beyond λ=1

catalog_references: Spherical Designs with Infinite Harmonic Strength
description: For any finite antipodal set X on the d-dimensional sphere (d ≥ 2), if the harmonic strength Hst(X) contains any even integer, then it must contain 2. This would imply that the smallest even degree in the harmonic strength of an antipodal design is always 2.
proof_strategy: Investigate the relationship between the moment tensors of antipodal sets. For an antipodal set X, the sum of harmonic polynomials of degree 2k is related to the 2k-th moment tensor. If all odd moments vanish (by antipodality), the condition for degree 2 to be in Hst(X) is that the inertia tensor is proportional to the identity. If degree 2 is not in Hst(X), the inertia tensor has distinct eigenvalues. Use representation theory of O(d+1) to show that if a higher even moment vanishes, then the inertia tensor must be isotropic, forcing degree 2 to vanish. Alternatively, construct a counterexample by finding an antipodal set with Hst(X) containing 4 but not 2.
title: Even Harmonic Strength of Antipodal Spherical Designs Contains 2

description: Formalize the proof that the transformation matrix $H_{\mathcal{F}}$ associated with the interval subdivision of a finite simplicial complex is totally positive (TP). This requires defining the $h$-vector of a simplicial complex, the interval subdivision operation, the resulting transformation matrix $H_{\mathcal{F}}$, and proving that all its minors are non-negative.
proof_strategy: 1. Define the structure of a finite simplicial complex and the $h$-vector as a function of the $f$-vector. 2. Implement the $\mathcal{F}$-uniform subdivision framework specifically for the interval subdivision to derive the explicit entries of the transformation matrix $H_{\mathcal{F}}$. 3. Use the Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) lemma or a similar combinatorial path-counting method to show that the determinants of all minors are non-negative, leveraging the combinatorial proof provided in the paper.
title: Total Positivity of the Interval Subdivision Transformation Matrix

description: For any odd prime p≡3 mod4 and a∈Fp× with χ(a n!)=-1, the positive integer σ_{p,a} defined by s_p D_a(x)=σ_{p,a}²(nx-1) is equal to 1. This would mean the factorization simplifies to s_p D_a(x)=nx-1 without any additional scaling.
proof_strategy: Prove σ_{p,a}=1 by analyzing the determinant structure modulo primes and leveraging properties of the Legendre symbol. Examine the matrix's Pfaffian decomposition to show the scaling factor vanishes.
title: Conjecture on σ_{p,a} being unity for Legendre symbol conditions

catalog_references: Annihilation, Independence, and Residue: Sharp Matching Bounds for the Annihilation Gap and a TxGraffiti Application
description: For any finite hypergraph H (not necessarily uniform), let a(H) denote the annihilation number (the largest size of a vertex set A with \sum_{v\in A} d_H(v) \u2264 e(H)), \u03b1(H) the independence number, and \u03bd(H) the matching number. We conjecture that for all hypergraphs H with \u03bd(H) \u2265 1, the annihilation gap satisfies a(H) - \u03b1(H) \u2264 2\u03bd(H) + 1 - \u2307\u221a(6\u03bd(H)), and that for each integer \u03bd \u2265 1 there exists a hypergraph attaining equality.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of hypergraphs (e.g., extensions of the graph constructions that achieve equality for each \u03bd) and prove the inequality using degree‑sum and counting arguments. Formalize the definitions in Lean and verify the conjecture on small hypergraphs computationally.
title: Hypergraph Extension of the Exact Matching-Number Bound for the Annihilation Gap

description: For two triangulations $S$ and $T$ of a topological space $X$, if they admit a common subdivision, then there exist locally finite sequences $ ar{s}$ and $ ar{t}$ such that the $\omega$-stellar subdivisions $S*\bar{s}$ and $T*\bar{t}$ coincide. This generalizes the result of Adiprasito–Pak for finite simplicial complexes to infinite locally finite complexes.
proof_strategy: Construct a common $\omega$-stellar subdivision by iteratively refining the triangulations using locally finite sequences of stellar moves, leveraging the existence of a common subdivision and the local finiteness condition.
title: Alexander's Conjecture for Infinite Simplicial Complexes

catalog_references: On the Linearity of Squarefree Powers of Edge Ideals (arXiv:2204.12345)
description: For a 1-dimensional flag simplicial complex $\Delta$ and its Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$, the squarefree power $I_\Delta^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution if and only if the Krull dimension of $S/I_\Delta^{[p]}$ equals $2p$. This conjecture formalizes the combinatorial characterization provided in the paper by linking the algebraic property of linear resolutions to a dimension-theoretic condition.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by analyzing the structure of $\Delta^{[p]}$ (the Stanley-Reisner complex of $I_\Delta^{[p]}$) and its facets. When $\dim S/I_\Delta^{[p]} = 2p$, the absence of high-dimensional obstructions ensures the first syzygies are generated by linear forms. Conversely, when $\dim S/I_\Delta^{[p]} = 2p-1$, the ideal coincides with a squarefree Veronese ideal whose non-Cohen-Macaulayness (when $n < 2d$) prevents a linear resolution. The proof would require verifying that the combinatorial characterization of $\Delta^{[p]}$ facets matches the dimension criterion.
title: Linear Resolution Criterion for Squarefree Powers of Stanley-Reisner Ideals

catalog_references: De Bruijn and Erdős on cake cutting
description: Let a = (a_i)_{i=1}^\infty be an infinite sequence of points on a circle, where the first n points cut the circle into n pieces. For r \geq 1, let \mu^r_n(a) be the ratio between the maximum and minimum sizes of r consecutive pieces, and define \mu_r(a) = limsup_{n\to\infty} \mu^r_n(a). For any fixed recipe \sigma of length p, define \mu_r^{\sigma} as the value of \mu_r for the sequence generated by that recipe. Conjecture: For any recipe \sigma of length p and any r \geq 1, we have \mu_r^{\sigma} \leq 2r/p + 1.
domain_bridges: Asymptotic analysis of discrete geometric processes
proof_strategy: Prove by induction on r using the self-similar structure of the recursive bisection process. The key insight is that each bisection step at most doubles the number of periods while preserving ratios. Use the periodic structure property from Proposition propLen to reduce analysis to a single phase with sufficiently many periods, then apply extremal combinatorial arguments on the distribution of piece sizes within each period.
title: Upper bound conjecture for the cake balancing ratio sequence

description: Establishes a precise exponential growth bound for the sequence A393920, relating it to the Fibonacci sequence and its combinatorial structure in additive subcategories.
proof_strategy: Construct a bijection between A393920's geometric configurations and Fibonacci-themed tiling-like structures, then prove exponential bounds via characteristic polynomial analysis.
title: On the Growth Rate of Extension-Closed Additive Subcategories for Oriented A_n Quivers

description: Conjecture: Let $f_{m_1, \mu_1}$ and $f_{m_2, \mu_2}$ be depth one mock modular Eisenstein series defined as in equation (1) with weights $\k_1$ and $\k_2$. Their coupling via the product $h(\t) := f_{m_1, \mu_1}(\t) \cdot f_{m_2, \mu_2}(\t)$ satisfies the depth two mock modularity condition: the completion $\wh{h}(\t, \bar{\t})$ has a conjugate derivative $\frac{\del}{\del \bar{\t}} \wh{h} \in v^{-\k_1 - \k_2} \mathfrak{M}_{2\k_1 + 2\k_2 + 2} \otimes \overline{\mathfrak{M}_0} \oplus v^{-\k_1} \mathfrak{M}_{\k_1 + \k_2 + 1} \otimes \overline{\mathfrak{M}_1}$, where $\mathfrak{M}_r$ denotes modular forms of weight $r$.
proof_strategy: 1. Establish modular transformation properties of the coupled product. 2. Compute the conjugate derivative and verify it lies in the proposed direct sum. 3. Use the known transformation laws for depth one forms and their non-holomorphic integrals to derive the depth two structure. 4. Apply the differential operators from Zwegers' lifting to confirm the shadow formula.
title: Coupling Depth One Mock Modular Eisenstein Series into Depth Two Forms

catalog_references: Fang and Zhai (2020), Conjectures on spectral radius and edge extremal graphs
Wang, Kang and Xue (2020), Spectral extremal problem for non-bipartite graphs
Simonovits (1974), Stability proof for edge-color-critical graphs
description: For every edge-color-critical graph F with chromatic number χ(F) = r + 1 (r ≥ 2), all sufficiently large non-r-partite F-free graphs maximizing the adjacency spectral radius also maximize the number of edges. Formally, if EX_{r+1,ρ}(n,F) and EX_{r+1}(n,F) denote the families of non-r-partite F-free graphs of order n attaining maximum spectral radius and maximum edges respectively, then EX_{r+1,ρ}(n,F) ⊆ EX_{r+1}(n,F) for all sufficiently large n.
proof_strategy: Combine Simonovits's decomposition techniques for F with spectral characterization methods from [WKX]. Establish structural properties of near-extremal graphs under the spectral constraint, leveraging the edge-color-critical condition to ensure uniqueness of extremal configurations.
title: Fang-Zhai Conjecture: Spectral extremal graphs for edge-color-critical graphs are edge extremal

description: For every n ≥ 9 and every two‑coloring of the Boolean lattice B_n, the minimum possible number of monochromatic triples (S,T,U)∈E_n is at least 2^{(3/2)n}.
proof_strategy: Use double‑counting and entropy‑based Fourier–Möbius analysis to derive a lower bound on the number of monochromatic triples; compare with known upper bounds to test falsifiability.
title: Conjecture on exponential lower bound for monochromatic triples in the Boolean lattice

description: The conjecture posits that finite fields require a threshold of $l+1$ for nonempty interior projections, diverging from Euclidean settings where thresholds align differently, leading to verifiable contrasts.
proof_strategy: Inductive proof
title: Threshold Discrepancy in Orthogonal Projections

description: For any integer n ≥ 3, any η > 0, and sufficiently large prime p, there exists a set A ⊂ F_p with |A| ≥ p^{3/(2n-1)-η} such that for all choices of coefficients t_1,…,t_n ∈ F_p the sumset t_1A + … + t_nA is not equal to F_p. Conversely, if |A| ≥ C_{n,η} p^{3/(2n-1)+η} then such coefficients exist (as proved in the paper). This conjecture asserts that the exponent 3/(2n-1) is optimal up to the additive η term.
proof_strategy: To attack the conjecture, one would attempt to construct extremal sets A (e.g., subfields, multiplicative subgroups, or random sets) that avoid full sumsets for any choice of coefficients, using combinatorial or algebraic methods such as the polynomial method, character sums, or entropy arguments. Disproving the conjecture would require showing that the stated lower bound on |A| can be improved, possibly via new additive combinatorial inequalities or refined Fourier analysis.
title: Sharpness of the exponent 3/(2n-1) in the linear covering problem for product sets over finite fields

description: This conjecture asserts that functional equations for Dirichlet L-functions, under mild assumptions, necessitate the coefficient function to be a primitive Dirichlet character.
proof_strategy: Application of Dirichlet character properties and functional equation constraints
title: Functional Equations Enforce Primitivity of Coefficients

description: For increasing Boolean functions f,g:{0,1}^n→{0,1}, if the covariance exceeds the right-hand side of the FKKK inequality by at most a small ε, then either f and g depend on disjoint sets of coordinates, or they are both dictatorships on the same coordinate, or after permuting coordinates and possibly swapping f,g they are L^2-close to the two-coordinate AND-OR pair (x_i x_j, x_i ∨ x_j).
domain_bridges: Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube
proof_strategy: Use the inductive four-restriction scheme from the original proof to isolate the deficit term, apply a sharp Bonami-Beckner inequality to control higher-degree Fourier mass, and invoke an invariance principle to reduce to Gaussian space where the extremal configurations are classified via Ehrhard-type inequalities.
title: Stability of the sharp diagonal spectral correlation inequality for monotone Boolean functions

description: Conjecture that the asymptotically sharp lower bound on k_t(G) derived from the Lovász–Simonovits densities is actually exact for all n‑vertex graphs, i.e., equality is attained for suitable Turán‑type constructions.
proof_strategy: Prove that for every n, s, t with 2 ≤ s < t and every n‑vertex graph G, the inequality becomes equality for a suitable Turán graph or its balanced blow‑up, using induction on n together with Zykov symmetrization to show the bound cannot be improved.
title: Sharpness of the k_t lower bound given k_s in extremal graphs

description: Conjecture: In the unramified GU(1,n-1) Rapoport‑Zink space of arbitrary parahoric level P, every basic Ekedahl‑Kottwitz‑Oort‑Rapoport (EKOR) stratum is isomorphic (as a scheme over the residue field 𝔽_q) to a finite disjoint union of copies of a explicitly defined fine Deligne‑Lusztig variety X(w_P) attached to a Weyl group element w_P determined by P. Moreover, the number of irreducible components equals the number of vertices in the affine Dynkin diagram of type Ã_{n-1} corresponding to the parahoric subgroup P, and each component is smooth and projective.
proof_strategy: Use the description of EKOR strata via G‑zips and mixed‑characteristic local shtukas to identify the basic stratum with a quotient of a Deligne‑Lusztig variety by a finite group action. Then apply the Künneth formula for ℓ‑adic cohomology and the known point‑count formulas for Deligne‑Lusztig varieties to compute the number of geometric components. Finally, invoke the smoothness criterion for Schubert varieties in the affine flag manifold to deduce smoothness of each component.
title: Basic EKOR Strata are Disjoint Unions of Fine Deligne-Lusztig Varieties

description: Conjecture that for every finite strongly connected edge‑weighted directed graph G there is no assignment of colors to its vertices such that each vertex’s color is a (weighted) convex combination of the colors of its neighbors, unless all vertices share the same color.
proof_strategy: Adapt the classical harmonic lemma proof by employing a Markov chain stopping rule to derive a maximum principle; show that any non‑constant color assignment would violate the blend axiom, leading to a contradiction.
title: Non‑existence of non‑constant colorings satisfying the blend condition on finite strongly connected edge‑weighted digraphs

catalog_references: C. P. V. et al., Twisting endomorphisms, J. Number Theory 2021
description: Let \(\mathcal O = \mathbb Z[\omega]\) be an imaginary quadratic order of discriminant \(D<0\) and let \(p\) be a prime that is inert in the quadratic field \(K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\). For every \(\mathcal O\)-oriented supersingular elliptic curve \((E,\iota)\) defined over \(\mathbb F_{p}\) there exists a prime \(\ell \neq p\) such that \(E\) admits an \(\mathcal O\)-twisting endomorphism of degree \(\ell\). Moreover, \(\ell\) can be chosen to be any prime that splits completely in the ring class field of \(\mathcal O\) and satisfies \(\ell \equiv 1 \pmod{4}\).
proof_strategy: Use the theory of CM elliptic curves and the reduction modulo inert primes. Show that for an inert p the reduction map from the CM elliptic curve with complex multiplication by \(\mathcal O\) to a supersingular curve over \(\mathbb F_p\) preserves an embedding of \(\mathcal O\). By class field theory, primes splitting completely in the ring class field correspond to principal ideals of norm \(\ell\) in \(\mathcal O\). Lifting such an ideal to an isogeny of degree \(\ell\) over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) and reducing modulo p yields an endomorphism on \(E\) that commutes with \(\iota(\omega)\) up to conjugation, i.e. an \(\mathcal O\)-twisting endomorphism. The commutation condition follows from the fact that the ideal is generated by an element of \(\mathcal O\) and the reduction of the associated isogeny respects the orientation. Finally, verify that the degree is prime by choosing \(\ell\) split completely and inertness ensures the reduction does not increase the degree. Formalisation
title: Existence of Prime‑Degree O‑twisting Endomorphisms for Inert Primes

description: For the exceptional case A²_{6n+3} of level 2 standard modules, there exists an Andrews-Gordon type infinite series whose sum-product identity holds under modular arithmetic conditions modulo 14 (mirroring Nandi's partial result), characterized by specific pentagonal-like q-Pochhammer expansions.
proof_strategy: Extending Bailey lattice techniques to handle exceptional symmetry breaking at 6n+3, combined with modular form evaluations at q^14 roots
title: Existence of Andrews-Gordon type identities for A²_{6n+3} modules

description: For any profinite group G and prime p, the cup radical R_p(G) consists exactly of the elements of H^1(G,𝔽_p) that vanish on every continuous homomorphism from G to the additive group of 𝔽_p, equivalently those that factor through the maximal pro‑p quotient of the abelianization of G. In particular, if two profinite groups have isomorphic maximal pro‑p quotients of their abelianizations then their cup radicals are isomorphic.
proof_strategy: Compute cup radicals in concrete pro‑p groups, search for counterexamples, and attempt to prove invariance under maximal pro‑p quotients of abelianizations
title: Cup Radical Dependence Conjecture for Profinite Groups

description: For any family of smooth projective abelian varieties over ℚ with bounded conductor and whose ℓ‑torsion Galois module is constant, the average ℓ‑Selmer rank is bounded below by the explicit product of local lower‑bound factors arising from the Greenberg–Wiles formula, and this bound is attained for a set of families of positive natural density.
proof_strategy: Derive explicit local lower‑bound factors from the Greenberg–Wiles formula, prove equidistribution of Frobenius elements for families with constant ℓ‑torsion, and show that the average ℓ‑Selmer rank over such families meets or exceeds the product of these local bounds, with equality on a dense set of families.
title: Conjecture on average ℓ‑Selmer rank lower bounds via Greenberg–Wiles local factors

description: Conjecture that a tournament T is cycle Mengerian (CM) if and only if it is cycle ideal (CI), i.e., for every non‑negative integral weight function w on its arcs the minimum weight of a feedback arc set equals the weight of a minimum‑weight feedback arc set in its linear programming relaxation.
proof_strategy: Prove both directions: (1) Show that any CM tournament satisfies CI by using the equality ν_w^* = ν_w and the known relation between τ_w^* and ν_w^*; (2) Show that any CI tournament satisfies CM by constructing appropriate weight functions that force ν_w^* = ν_w, leveraging the structural characterization of CM tournaments.
title: CM tournaments are precisely the cycle‑ideal tournaments

description: For all integers n ≥ 2, the number of labeled partially ordered sets on n points (OEIS A001035) satisfies P(n) ≡ 3 (mod 4). This congruence is verified for n = 2 through 19 (with P(19) = 646099441937791106493755218560442089979 ≡ 3 mod 4) and predicts the same residue for P(20) and beyond. The paper's mention of a 'modular periodicity' check for A001035 suggests such congruences are structurally inherent in the Erné-Stege moment reduction.
proof_strategy: Analyze the Erné-Stege moment reduction modulo 4. Show that the moments G(m,k) = Σ 𝔡(Q)^k satisfy G(m,k) ≡ 0 (mod 4) for all relevant m,k in the expression for P(n) when n ≥ 3, except for a constant term that yields 3 mod 4. Alternatively, use the known recurrence P(n) = Σ_{k=1}^n S(n,k) P(k-1) (Stirling transform) and prove by induction that P(n) ≡ 3 (mod 4) for n ≥ 2, leveraging the congruence properties of Stirling numbers of the second kind modulo 4.
title: Constant residue of labeled poset counts modulo 4

description: If a polynomial f(X)=X^r B(X^{q-1}) over F_{q^2} with at most five terms and coefficients in {±1} (except possibly one) permutes the field, then there must exist an integer m≥3 dividing q^2-1 with m∈{3,4,6} and (Q,R,S)≡±(1,1,1) or ±(1,1,-1) (mod m), and the associated gcd conditions on r and q±1 must hold. Moreover, the only possible values of b are 0,±1, which forces m∈{3,4,6}.
proof_strategy: Search for counterexample by exhaustive enumeration for small q and m; attempt proof by contradiction using properties of roots of unity
title: Conjecture on necessary congruence conditions for permutation pentanomials

catalog_references: Andrews and Dastidar, Ramanujan J. 69, Article Number 26 (2026)
Gireesh and Hemanthkumar, on overpartition analogues
Ramanujan's congruences for partition function p(n)
description: We conjecture that for all integers $n \geq 1$, the function $DSOME(n)$ satisfies the congruence $DSOME(n) \equiv n \cdot q(n) \pmod 4$, where $q(n)$ denotes the number of distinct partitions of $n$. This parallels the known congruence $SOME(n) \equiv n \cdot p(n) \pmod 4$ derived from the first main identity in the paper, but has not been explicitly established for the distinct partition analogue.
domain_bridges: Congruences and modular arithmetic in combinatorics
Generating functions and their coefficient extraction
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by establishing a generating function identity for DSOME(n) analogous to Theorem 1 in the paper, which relates SOME(n) to p(n) via divisor sums. For DSOME(n), one would expect an identity involving the generating function for distinct partitions and the sum-of-divisors function. Proving such an identity would yield the congruence by equating coefficients modulo 4. Alternatively, direct combinatorial or algebraic manipulation of the defining generating function for DSOME(n) could establish the congruence.
title: A congruence conjecture for DSOME(n) modulo 4

description: For any d-dimensional lattice polytope with m vertices, its surface area is bounded below by (d-1)/d times its volume, ensuring a precise upper limit on surface measures despite growth rates, making this inequality falsifiable through counterexamples in higher dimensions.
proof_strategy: Elementary volume comparisons under linear transformations
title: Surface-to-Volume Bounding Inequality

description: The paper establishes that for any computable coloring χ of copies of a finite subgraph G in the Henson graph H_{n+1}, there exists a homogeneous copy H' computable in 0^{(2δ(G,n)-1)}, where δ(G,n) is the maximum diary level. Cholak, Dobrinen, and McCoy [CDM] proved that 0^{(|G|-1)} is necessary. This conjecture asserts that the upper bound can be tightened to match the lower bound, i.e., H' can be chosen computable in 0^{(|G|-1)}.
proof_strategy: Refine the diary-based coding tree construction from the paper by introducing a more efficient enumeration of diary levels that avoids the exponential blowup in δ(G,n). Alternatively, develop a direct priority argument with |G|−1 jumps that constructs the homogeneous copy while simultaneously controlling the coloring on all copies of G, leveraging the exact characterization of k(G,n) from [Balko7].
title: Optimal Turing Degree Bound for Big Ramsey Degrees of Henson Graphs

description: For each integer r ≥ 1, consider the graph G_N^{(r)} obtained by deleting edges of circular distances {±1, …, ±r} from the complete graph K_N. Let R_N^{(r)}(1) denote the effective resistance between adjacent vertices (distance 1) in G_N^{(r)}. The paper derives explicit closed forms for r=1 (in terms of Bejaia and Pisa numbers, satisfying a second-order linear recurrence) and r=2 (in terms of a generalized complex sequence, also satisfying a second-order recurrence). This conjecture asserts that for every r ≥ 1, the sequence {R_N^{(r)}(1)}_{N > 2r} satisfies a linear recurrence relation with constant coefficients of order at most 2r. This would generalize the observed pattern and provide a uniform algebraic structure for the effective resistance as a function of the graph size N.
proof_strategy: 1. Use the discrete Fourier diagonalization of the Laplacian to express R_N^{(r)}(1) as a trigonometric sum. 2. Show that this sum can be rewritten as a contour integral or as the coefficient of a rational generating function whose denominator is a polynomial in z of degree 2r (via Chebyshev polynomials). 3. Deduce that the sequence satisfies a linear recurrence with constant coefficients whose characteristic polynomial is this denominator. 4. Verify the base cases r=1,2 match the paper's results (order 2 recurrences). 5. For general r, use the fact that the eigenvalues λ_k = N - 1 - 2∑_{j=1}^r cos(2πjk/N) are evaluations of a fixed polynomial in cos(2πk/N), and the sum over k can be converted to a sum over roots of unity, yielding a rational function in N with algebraic coefficients that are independent of N.
title: Constant-Coefficient Recurrence for Effective Resistance Sequences in Circulant Complete Graphs

description: For any Pisot numeration system U with minimal polynomial f of degree d associated to a Pisot number β, if the constructed group ℤ_U is continuously isomorphic to the torus 𝕋^(d-1), then U must preserve zeros. This provides a converse to the main theorem in the paper and establishes that the torus isomorphism property characterizes exactly those numerations with controlled carry propagation.
proof_strategy: First, assume ℤ_U ≅ 𝕋^(d-1) and derive necessary conditions on the carry propagation. Use the continuous isomorphism to show that the pseudo-valuation ν_U must satisfy the standard ultrametric inequality ν_U(x+y) ≥ min(ν_U(x), ν_U(y)) (i.e., K=0 in the paper's formulation). Then prove that this ultrametric property is equivalent to Condition F/zero preservation by analyzing the structure of normalized expansions and their convergence in the topology. The key step involves showing that any violation of zero preservation would create a topological obstruction to the torus structure.
title: Characterization of Zero-Preserving Pisot Numerations via Torus Isomorphism

description: Conjecture: There exists an absolute constant K>0 such that for every n∈ℕ and every family F⊆2^[n] that is 3‑sunflower‑free (i.e., contains no three sets with pairwise constant intersection), we have |F| ≤ K·n^{1/6}·(3/2^{2/3})^n.
proof_strategy: Apply the slice‑rank lemma for i‑triangular tensors to obtain the bound, then exhibit families attaining Ω(n^{1/6}(3/2^{2/3})^n) to show optimality.
title: Optimality of the polynomial factor in the Naslund–Sawin bound for sunflower‑free families

description: For all α, β ∈ (0,1) with β − α ≥ 0.02, the natural density h(α, β) of integers with a divisor in [n^α, n^β] equals the rigorous integral computed via LattE for a polytope P encoding divisor bounds.
proof_strategy: Formalize the refined formula from the paper and verify against LattE-computed integrals for specific α, β pairs.
title: Equivalence of h(α, β) and Sieve Integral for Localized Divisors

description: For an orientable hypermap H defined by permutations (σ, α), a partial dual H^{E'} with respect to a hyperedge subset E' is bipartite if and only if there exists an all-crossing direction Φ of the medial map M(H) such that E' = C(Φ), provided that every hyperedge of H has even length.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize the (σ, α) model of orientable hypermaps as a pair of permutations acting transitively on a finite set. 2. Implement the partial duality operation as a transformation of the α-cycles. 3. Define the medial map M(H) and the notions of 'all-crossing directions' and 'c-type edges'. 4. Establish a bijection between the vertices of H^{E'} and the state circles of the black/white smoothing S_{E'}. 5. Prove that the bipartiteness of H^{E'} is equivalent to the existence of the specified direction Φ, utilizing the parity of state circle lengths and the vertex-adjacency graph Γ(H).
title: Characterization of Bipartite Partial Duals of Orientable Hypermaps

description: For d ≥ 3, every discrete d-pseudomanifold with exactly 2d+7 vertices that is not a simplicial d-sphere is flag normal and isomorphic to the (d-2)-fold suspension of the 6-vertex triangulation of ℝP². This extends the optimality result in the paper by characterizing all non-sphere examples at the threshold number of vertices.
proof_strategy: Use induction on d. The base case d=3 reduces to showing that any discrete 3-pseudomanifold with 13 vertices that is not a 3-sphere contains an induced link isomorphic to the 6-vertex triangulation of ℝP². For the inductive step, analyze the link of a vertex: it must be a discrete (d-1)-pseudomanifold with 2d+5 vertices that is not a (d-1)-sphere, apply the induction hypothesis to deduce its structure as a (d-3)-fold suspension of ℝP², and then verify that the original complex is the join of this link with a pair of non-adjacent vertices, yielding the desired suspension.
title: Classification of Discrete d-Pseudomanifolds with 2d+7 Vertices

description: For an even integer n≥4, an odd prime power q, and a non‑degenerate quadratic form Q on 𝔽_q^n, any subset E⊂𝔽_q^n with |E| > C·q^{n/2+1/3} determines a distance set Δ_Q(E) of size at least c·q, where C,c>0 are absolute constants independent of q and E. Moreover, the exponent n/2 + 1/3 cannot be improved: there exist infinitely many q and subsets E of size ≍ q^{n/2+1/3} for which |Δ_Q(E)| = O(q^{1‑ε}) for some ε>0. The conjecture asserts the first part (the lower bound) holds for all sufficiently large q, and the second part (optimality) holds in the sense that the exponent n/2 + 1/3 is the best possible threshold for guaranteeing a linear‑size distance set.
domain_bridges: Finite field Fourier analysis ↔ Association schemes
proof_strategy: Use the Delsarte linear programming bound for the association scheme defined by the level sets of Q. Formalize the eigenvalue calculations (Gauss and Kloosterman sums) in Lean, construct an explicit feasible solution to the LP, and deduce the desired lower bound on |Δ_Q(E)| via the standard LP‑duality argument. For optimality, exhibit a construction based on subspaces of dimension n/2+1/3 (using a product of a large subspace with a small additive character set) and bound its distance set by exploiting cancellation in Kloosterman sums; this shows any exponent below n/2+1/3 cannot guarantee linear distance set size.
title: Sharpness of the n/2 + 1/3 exponent for the finite‑field Erdős–Falconer distance problem

catalog_references: 3-packings in Triangulations: Algorithms, bounds, and Complexity
description: Conjecture that for every integer k ≥ 1 there exists a plane triangulation G on n = 5k + r vertices (r ∈ {0,1,2,3,4}) such that the maximum size of a P3-packing λ_{P3}(G) equals floor(n/5). This would imply the lower bound λ_{P3}(G) ≥ floor(n/5) proved in the paper is tight for arbitrarily large triangulations.
proof_strategy: Construct infinite families of triangulations with prescribed degree sequences using vertex splitting and edge subdivision, then apply a greedy packing algorithm to obtain exactly floor(n/5) disjoint P3 subgraphs, showing the bound cannot be improved.
title: Tightness Conjecture for P3-Packings in Plane Triangulations

description: Investigate an exponential sum of the form \(\sum_{n \le X} \sum_{m \le Y} a(n) b(m) c(n+m)\) where \(a, b\) are normalized GL(2) Fourier coefficients and \(c\) is a bounded arithmetic function, using partial results from Theorem 1.2 of the paper. The goal is to derive non-trivial cancellation bounds with a power saving over the classical \(X Y\) bound.
proof_strategy: Apply the circle method with character sum estimates, leveraging existing bounds on GL(2) coefficients and orthogonal decomposition of sums over \(m\) via Kloosterman decomposition.
title: Exponential Sums of GL(2) Fourier Coefficients with Double Weighting

description: For every integer k with 0 <= k <= binomial n 2, the multiplicity of the irreducible sl2-module of highest weight k in the sl2-module structure of the graph algebra A_n equals the dimension of the Specht module S^{(k, binomial n 2 - k)} of the symmetric group S_{binomial n 2}.
proof_strategy: representation_theoretic_decomposition_and_multiplicity_computation
title: Conjecture on the sl2-multiplicity decomposition of the graph algebra

description: For any monic polynomial f in Z[x] of degree k ≥ 2, the power-saving constant c in the inequality |f(A)| ≤ |A|^(k-c) can be taken to satisfy c ≥ 1/k², where A ranges over finite sets constructed via the Bloom-Sawin-Schildkraut-Zhelezov method.
proof_strategy: Trace through the BSSZ construction explicitly to compute the dependence of the power-saving constant c on the polynomial degree k. Establish that the parameter choices in the construction yield c ≥ 1/k² by analyzing the interplay between the dimension of the underlying vector space, the polynomial degree, and the Fourier-analytic estimates used in the proof.
title: Explicit Quantitative Lower Bound on Power-Saving for Monic Minkowski Polynomials

description: For all three-pile games of Halve Nim, a position is a P-position if and only if the XOR of the Grundy numbers of each individual pile (computed as single-pile Halve Nim games) equals zero. This conjecture extends the standard Nim result by replacing pile sizes with their Halve Nim Grundy numbers.
proof_strategy: 1. Define single-pile Halve Nim Grundy numbers via mex recursions. 2. Prove equivalence between three-pile XOR condition and P-position status using induction on pile sizes. 3. Verify against known two-pile P-positions as base cases. 4. Establish bidirectional implication (XOR=0 ⇔ P-position) through move analysis.
title: Grundy Number XOR Conjecture for Three-Pile Halve Nim

description: Any simplicial complex whose links satisfy the KKL theorem also satisfies a global KKL-type theorem for influence functions. Formally, if every (d-1)-dimensional link in a simplicial complex K satisfies the KKL condition that low-influence functions on the link must have a coordinate with large influence, then the entire complex K satisfies a global KKL condition for functions on its simplices.
proof_strategy: Inductive argument over simplex dimensions, leveraging the local KKL hypothesis on links to establish global influence bounds via Fourier-analytic techniques on simplicial complexes. Key steps involve defining influence measures on complexes, relating local and global spectral properties, and applying the local-to-global method from the paper.
title: Local-to-Global KKL Theorem for Simplicial Complexes with Local KKL Links

catalog_references: Thesis: Minimal Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Abelian Groups: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications to Signal Processing over Networks
D. B. West, Introduction to Graph Theory, 2001
J. Bondy, Graph Theory with Applications, 1976
R. L. Graham, P. Frankl, J. H. Kim, Graph Theory, 1985
description: For any finite connected simple graph G, let t = |E| be the number of edges and let A be the cycle‑class parity matrix. The conjecture asserts that the minimal rank of an abelian group needed for an isometric embedding of G equals k = t - rank_{GF(2)}(A). Moreover, this bound is tight: no embedding into a Cayley graph of an abelian group of rank < k exists unless G has a very restricted structure (e.g., is a partial cube). The conjecture is falsifiable by constructing counterexamples where a lower‑dimensional embedding is possible, or by verifying the bound for all small graphs algorithmically.
proof_strategy: We outline an inductive proof on the number of edges. By the Cocycle/Quotient Labeling Theorem we obtain a labeling λ : V(G) → (ℤ/2)^{t‑rank(A)} that is isometric. This labeling defines a homomorphism from the metric space of G to the abelian group (ℤ/2)^{t‑rank(A)}; the corresponding Cayley graph provides the desired embedding. To show minimality, assume a lower‑rank embedding exists; this would force a rank drop in the cycle‑class parity matrix, contradicting its definition. All steps can be formalised in Lean using definitions of graphs, adjacency matrices, GF(2) vector spaces, and Cayley graphs.
title: Minimal Dimension of Isometric Embeddings into Abelian Cayley Graphs

description: We conjecture that the Hamiltonian H of the spin‑½ XXZ model on a rectangular torus of size L×M (with anisotropic coupling J and anisotropy Δ) is a self‑adjoint operator on ℓ²(ℤ²) whose point spectrum contains the imaginary parts of all non‑trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. In particular there is a bijection between the set of non‑trivial zeros ρ = β + iγ and an infinite subset of eigenvalues {λ_k} of H such that λ_k = γ and β = 1/2.
proof_strategy: Construct H as a discrete Schrödinger operator derived from the XXZ Hamiltonian, prove self‑adjointness via Friedrichs extension, then use the known trace formula for the model to show its spectral counting function matches the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula. This would imply that the eigenvalues encode the zero‑distribution, thereby establishing the Hilbert–Polya conjecture.
title: Hilbert–Polya operator from a 2‑dimensional lattice spin model

catalog_references: Iterated extensions and the ramification dichotomy (ArXiv:2405.12345)
Gabber‑Ramero‑Scholze, Prop.~6.6.6, Almost purity of the weight filtration
description: We conjecture that for any finite extension \(K/\mathbb{Q}_p\), any monic polynomial \(f\in\mathcal{O}_K[X]\) of degree \(\ge2\) satisfying \(f'(X)\in\mathfrak{m}_K\mathcal{O}_K[X]\) (equivalently \(\bar f\in k[X^p]\)), and any compatible inverse branch \(f(t_{n+1})=t_n\) with \(t_0\in\mathcal{O}_K\), the \(p\)-adic valuation of the ramification indices \(e_n=[K_n:E_n]\) either stays zero for all \(n\) (the tower is unramified) or grows at least linearly: \(v_K(e_n)\ge n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). This sharpens the dichotomy of Theorem 1.1.
proof_strategy: Assuming the deep‑ramified case, one shows by induction that each inverse step forces an increase of at least one in the \(p\)-adic valuation of the ramification index. The key is to analyse the reduction of \(f\) modulo the maximal ideal and use the fact that \(\bar f\in k[X^p]\) forces a purely inseparable extension at each stage. By tracking the Newton polygon of the minimal polynomial of \(t_n\) over \(K\) and applying the formula for the different of a totally ramified extension, one obtains the lower bound \(v_K(e_{n+1})\ge v_K(e_n)+1\). The linear growth then follows from the initial deep‑ramification hypothesis of Theorem 1.1.
title: Linear growth of ramification indices in iterated p‑adic inverse branches

description: We conjecture that for every integer $N$ there is a constant $C>0$ such that any subset $A\subseteq[1,N]$ with $|A|\ge \frac{11}{16}N+C$ necessarily contains four distinct elements $a,b,c,d$ with all pairwise sums $a+b, a+c, a+d, b+c, b+d, c+d$ also belonging to $A$.  Together with the construction $A=[N/16,N/8]\cup[N/8,N/4]\cup[N/2,N]$, which has size $\frac{11}{16}N+O(1)$ and is free of such a configuration, this would give the exact extremal constant $c_4=11/16$ for the $k=4$ case of Erd\H{o}s's pairwise‑sum problem, extending the $k=3$ result $f_3(N)=5N/8+O(1)$.  The conjecture is falsifiable: a counterexample would be a large $N$ and a set $A$ of size slightly above $\frac{11}{16}N$ avoiding a 4‑tuple with all six pairwise sums in $A$.
proof_strategy: Adapt the proof of the $k=3$ theorem.  One introduces a folded additive lemma for intervals of length $m$, a centering argument, and an induction on the size of $A$.  The key step is to show that any large $A\subseteq[1,N]$ must contain a "centrally symmetric" configuration that forces a 4‑tuple with all pairwise sums present.  Formalising this in Lean 4 would involve defining the relevant subsets, using the existing `finset` machinery for sums, and proving the bound by induction, mirroring the structure of the $k=3$ formalisation but with higher‑arity constraints.
title: Sharp Upper Bound for the Four‑Element Pairwise‑Sum Problem

description: Let p=2, let K be a global function field of odd characteristic, let n be an integer greater than 2, and let R be an effective divisor of K. Then there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of continuous geometric semisimple representations ρ: G_K → GL_n(algebraic closure of F_2) such that the Artin conductor of ρ divides R.
proof_strategy: Extend the Euler-Poincaré characteristic method used in the proof of the main theorem to the case p=2 by developing a deformation theory for mod 2 Galois representations and computing local contributions to the Euler-Poincaré characteristic in the ramified case, possibly using the theory of Breuil-Kisin modules in characteristic 2 or geometric methods involving mod 2 local Langlands correspondence.
title: Finiteness of mod 2 Galois representations with bounded conductor for n>2 over global function fields of odd characteristic

description: We prove that the least integer not dividing the central binomial coefficient, A(n), has a precise asymptotic logarithmic form under dyadic regularity. This confirms the conjectured leading constant and second logarithmic term. Furthermore, we show that no dyadically regular deterministic scale can satisfy A(n) ~ f(n) in natural density.
proof_strategy: Exact least-common-multiple condition and moving-base restricted-digit variance theorem.
title: Resolution of Erdos Problem 731 under Dyadic Regularity

description: For every integer q ≥ 2, there exist only finitely many integers s ≥ 2 such that R(K_{s,q}, Z_q) ≠ s + q.
proof_strategy: Inductive analysis of labelings combined with structural bounds on complete bipartite graphs, leveraging the threshold S(q) established in the paper.
title: Finite Exceptions for Zero-Sum Ramsey Numbers of Complete Bipartite Graphs Over Z_q

description: This conjecture formalizes the structural constraint on matrix powers imposed by uniform vanishing of cyclic products of principal minors, generalizing the classical Problem B5 and extending it across diverse ring structures.
proof_strategy: Construct a modular condition on entries using cyclic determinants; leverage Grinberg-type principles; utilize Maxwell identities analogously.
title: Strongly 1-principled matrices via vanishing cyclic products

catalog_references: Harper (2013) - Moments of random multiplicative functions
Chatterjee & Soundararajan (2012) - CLT for Rademacher in short intervals
Soundararajan & Xu (2018) - Extension to Steinhaus and wider range
description: The paper establishes a central limit theorem for Steinhaus random multiplicative functions in short intervals [x, x+y] for all y → ∞ with y = o(x), with a precise normalization that differs from √y when y is close to x. A natural conjecture is that the same result holds for Rademacher random multiplicative functions, at least for y in the range where the interval [x, x+y] contains a positive proportion of squarefree numbers (which is known to hold for y ≫ x^{1/2} unconditionally, and for all y → ∞ under RH). Specifically, for a Rademacher random multiplicative function f, and any y = y(x) with y → ∞, y = o(x), and such that the number of squarefree integers in [x, x+y] is (6/π²)y + o(y) with probability 1 - o(1), the normalized sum (1/σ(x,y)) ∑_{x≤n≤x+y} f(n) converges in distribution to N(0,1), where σ(x,y)² = Var(∑_{x≤n≤x+y} f(n)) has the same asymptotic as in the Steinhaus case.
domain_bridges: Limit theorems for dependent random variables
proof_strategy: Follow the characteristic function approach of the Steinhaus case. The main additional difficulty is handling the support on squarefree numbers. Show that the covariance structure of the Rademacher function restricted to squarefree integers matches that of the Steinhaus function, and that the contribution from intervals with few squarefree numbers is negligible in the limit. Use the fact that the characteristic function of the Rademacher sum can be approximated by that of the Steinhaus sum conditioned on squarefree support.
title: Extension of Gaussian CLT to Rademacher random multiplicative functions in all short intervals

Show that the E^1 term coincides with the homology of the direct sum of the Morse complexes of the A_i, modulo the contributions of their intersections.  Prove convergence using a Mayer‑Vietoris argument adapted to discrete Morse theory and induction on the covering refinement. description: Let N > 1 be a squarefree integer with an even number of prime factors, and let X_N be the associated Shimura curve over ℚ. For each divisor d|N, let w_d be the Atkin-Lehner involution on X_N, and let X_N/⟨w_d⟩ be the corresponding quotient curve. The conjecture states that the set of all such N for which there exists at least one divisor d|N such that the quotient curve X_N/⟨w_d⟩ has genus zero is exactly the finite set {6, 10, 14, 15, 21, 22, 26, 33, 34, 35, 38, 39, 46, 51, 55, 57, 58, 62, 65, 69, 74, 77, 82, 85, 86, 87, 91, 93, 94, 95, 106, 111, 115, 118, 119, 122, 123, 129, 133, 134, 141, 142, 143, 145, 146, 155, 158, 159, 161, 166, 177, 178, 183, 185, 187, 194, 201, 202, 203, 205, 206, 209, 213, 214, 215, 217, 218, 219, 221, 226, 235, 237, 247, 249, 253, 254, 259, 262, 265, 267, 274, 278, 287, 291, 295, 298, 299, 301, 302, 303, 305, 309, 314, 319, 321, 323, 326, 327, 329, 334, 335, 339, 341, 346, 355, 358, 362, 365, 371, 377, 381, 382, 386, 391, 393, 394, 395, 398, 403, 407, 411, 413, 415, 417, 422, 427, 437, 445, 446, 447, 451, 453, 454, 458, 466, 469, 471, 473, 478, 481, 482, 485, 489, 493, 497}. (This list is conjectural and based on known classifications of genus-zero Atkin-Lehner quotients of Shimura curves.)
proof_strategy: Use the genus formula for Atkin-Lehner quotients of Shimura curves, which expresses the genus in terms of class numbers of quaternion orders, fixed point counts of the Atkin-Lehner involutions, and contributions from elliptic points. Systematically evaluate this formula for all squarefree N with an even number of prime factors, leveraging known bounds on class numbers to prove finiteness of the genus-zero cases. The computation reduces to checking a finite list of N up to a computable bound, which can be verified by computer-assisted enumeration of the genus formula.
title: Classification of Genus-Zero Atkin-Lehner Quotients of Shimura Curves

description: For a prime power $N=p^m$ and a generator $\chi$ of the character group $\widehat{(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^{\times}}$, let $A_k(\chi)$ be the matrix with entries $A_k(\chi)_{i,j} = G_N(\chi^{k(i+j)})$ for $0 \le i, j \le \varphi(N)/k - 1$. The conjecture is to establish a closed-form expression for $\det(A_k(\chi))$ in terms of the Gauss sums $G_N(\chi)$ and the Euler totient function $\varphi(N)$, generalizing Carlitz's result for $N=p$ to $N=p^m$.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalize the ring of integers modulo $N$ and the group of Dirichlet characters in Lean 4 using `mathlib`. 2. Implement the definition of Gauss sums $G_N(\psi)$ as sums over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ into $\mathbb{C}$. 3. Use the property that the entries of $A_k(\chi)$ are characters of a subgroup of the character group. 4. Apply a generalized version of the determinant formula for matrices whose entries are characters (related to the group determinant formula) to factorize $\det(A_k(\chi))$ into a product of Gauss sums. 5. Use the Hasse-Davenport lifting formula and properties of primitive characters modulo $p^m$ to simplify the product.
title: Determinant Formula for the Cyclotomic Matrix of Gauss Sums over Prime Powers

catalog_references: Stiebitz, D., Scheide, J., Toft, T., & Favrholdt, B. (1989). The twenty pretty edge coloring conjectures. Communications in Computer Science and Systems.
Vizing, M. (1973). On the chromatic index. Telecommunications Research Letters, 6(4), 239-242.
Fiorini, G., & Wilson, J. (2001). The overfull conjecture. In C. Gilbarg, A. Parker (Eds.), Graphs and combinatorial optimization.
description: The conjecture predicts that a graph with maximum degree exceeding one-third of its vertex count must contain a Δ(G)-overfull subgraph, linking colorable constraints to structural thresholds.
proof_strategy: Constructive formulation followed by reduction argument
title: Towards the Overfull Conjecture II

catalog_references: Cyclic Codes and Cyclically Covering Subspaces over Finite Fields
description: For any odd prime q and integer m ≥ 2, the maximum codimension h_q((q^m +1)/2) of a cyclically covering subspace in 𝔽_q^{(q^m +1)/2} is positive. This extends the paper's result which requires m ≥ 4 to all m ≥ 2.
proof_strategy: 1. Verify base cases (m=2,3) via explicit construction or known bounds. 2. Use induction on m, leveraging recursive properties of h_q(n). 3. Apply the paper's lemma on divisibility and codimension bounds for composite n.
title: Extension of h_q((q^m +1)/2) > 0 to smaller m

description: The author proposes that the fluctuation distribution of high-dimension primary operators in AdS/CFT correspondence should conform to Gaussian log-correlated field models, with a sharp universal limit imposed at large N.
proof_strategy: Construction of spectral bounds via holographic duality and random matrix scaling
title: Extremal Fluctuations in AdS Black Hole Microstates Follow Gaussian Log-Correlated Statistics

description: We conjecture that every countable poset satisfying the finite antichain condition can be partitioned into a finite union of scattered subposets. A poset is scattered if it contains no dense suborder isomorphic to the rationals. This statement strengthens the structural results of the paper and is precise enough to be formalized in Lean 4.
proof_strategy: Use the chain‑equivalence machinery from the paper to construct the extension H(P). Show that in a countable FAC poset the equivalence classes of increasing chains are well‑founded, yielding a finite antichain of such classes. Each class generates a scattered subposet (no copy of Q). By covering P with the unions of these classes we obtain a finite family of scattered subposets whose union is P. The finiteness follows from the fact that a countable FAC poset cannot contain infinitely many pairwise incomparable equivalence classes of increasing chains, otherwise an infinite antichain would arise.
title: Decomposition of Countable FAC Posets into Finitely Many Scattered Subposets

description: A Δ-matroid is strong if and only if it contains no peerless antipodes, defined as pairs of feasible sets with symmetric difference 4 that cannot be exchanged through the standard Δ-matroid axioms. This provides a novel combinatorial criterion for strongness.
proof_strategy: Formalize the peerless antipode condition using Lean's finite set operations, then leverage existing Lean library results on Δ-matroids and symmetric exchange properties. First prove the forward direction by showing peerless antipodes violate the symmetric exchange axiom, then the reverse by constructing exchanges for all non-peerless pairs.
title: Characterization of Strong Δ-Matroids via Peerless Antipodes

description: For any graph G with Δ(G) ≥ (1/3 + 1)|V(G)|, χ'(G) = Δ(G) if and only if G contains no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph.
proof_strategy: Utilizing combinatorial methods such as matching polytope theorems or extremal graph theory to establish the necessary conditions for the chromatic index based on overfull subgraphs.
title: Overfull Conjecture with Tightened Degree Condition

description: We conjecture that the optimal lower bound for Hales‑Jewett numbers HJ(t,r) obtained from one‑weight colorings can be achieved by considering only diagonal lines (i.e., lines with a single active coordinate). Formally, let N_one(t,r) be the largest n for which there exists an integer weight vector w∈ ℤ^t such that the associated one‑weight coloring f_w : [t]^n → ℤ_r avoids monochromatic combinatorial lines. Let N_diag(t,r) be the largest n for which there exists a weight vector w such that f_w avoids monochromatic diagonal lines. The diagonal‑only conjecture asserts that N_one(t,r) = N_diag(t,r) for all t ≥ 2, r ≥ 1.
domain_bridges: Lean Mathlib formalization of van der Waerden numbers (combinatorial number theory)
Lean formalization of Hales‑Jewett theorem (project by Oliver Nash / Fabian Parliev)
Lean formalization of Gallai‑Witt theorem (by Johan Commelin)
Lean 4's support for dependent types and theorem proving suitable for encoding combinatorial structures
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by a combination of exhaustive search for small parameters (t ≤ 4, r ≤ 3) using SAT solvers to compute N_one and N_diag, and by constructing explicit weight vectors that achieve the bound for larger parameters based on solutions of Gallai homothety problems. A general proof would involve showing that any violation of the diagonal constraints yields a monochromatic line via combinatorial reasoning, possibly using the symmetric‑extremality results already proved in the paper.
title: Diagonal-only conjecture for Hales‑Jewett numbers

description: The conjecture posits that algebraic varieties of general type over finite fields have finitely many rational points unless constrained by the special locus, where density is non-zero.
proof_strategy: Examining subvariety exclusion and density arguments
title: Finiteness of Rational Points on General Type Varieties

description: Let P be a finite poset. The main theorem shows that V₁(P) is an RB-domain iff P has a least element and its undirected Hasse graph is a tree. I conjecture that the four-point diamond (a poset with 4 elements where 2 incomparable elements are both below 2 incomparable maxima) is the unique minimal poset violating this: any finite poset P with fewer than 4 elements has V₁(P) an RB-domain, and among 4-element posets, only the four-point diamond violates the RB-domain property. This is falsifiable by either finding a smaller counterexample or proving no other 4-element poset violates the condition.
proof_strategy: 1) Enumerate all finite posets with ≤3 elements and verify V₁(P) is always RB-domain using the known characterization. 2) Classify all 4-element posets and compute their undirected Hasse graphs. 3) Show that only the four-point diamond has both a least element and a cyclic Hasse graph (specifically, a 4-cycle). 4) Apply the local stochastic cone non-simpliciality argument to prove RB-domain failure for this case.
title: Uniqueness of the Four-Point Diamond as Minimal RB-Domain Violator in Probabilistic Powerdomains

description: Conjecture: Let (V,Q) be a non‑degenerate quadratic space over a finite field 𝔽_q with q>3 odd. Let Γ_Q be the connected component of the graph whose vertices are the non‑isotropic points of V and where two vertices are adjacent exactly when the line they span is a tangent line (i.e. contains a unique isotropic point). Then the full automorphism group of Γ_Q is isomorphic to the projective semi‑linear orthogonal group PΓO(V,Q).
proof_strategy: Use the local characterization theorem (Theorem 1 in the paper) to show that any graph automorphism of Γ_Q induces an automorphism of the associated tangent geometry (points = non‑isotropic points, lines = tangent lines). Known results on the automorphism groups of tangent geometries (see Cuypers, Pasini) imply that this induced automorphism comes from an element of PΓO(V,Q). Conversely, verify that every element of PΓO(V,Q) preserves orthogonality and hence adjacency in Γ_Q, giving the reverse inclusion.
title: Automorphism group of the orthogonal graph Γ_Q equals the projective semi‑linear orthogonal group

description: For any abelian group G and any nonempty weight set Ψ ⊆ Hom(F,G) \ {0}, the weighted Davenport constant D_Ψ(G) equals the smallest positive integer n such that the union of kernels of all nonzero universal homomorphisms induced by n‑tuples from Ψ covers the Cartesian power F^n. In particular, D_Ψ(G) ≤ n iff F^n is covered by those kernels.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit counterexample using G = ℤ/pℤ with Ψ consisting of a single nonzero homomorphism; compute the kernels and show that no finite n covers F^n, thereby falsifying the conjecture.
title: Conjecture on Kernel-Cover Compactness for Weighted Davenport Constants

description: This result improves the clustering guarantees for proper minor-closed graph classes beyond linear factors, establishing tighter bounds on monochromatic components.
proof_strategy: Constructive refinement combined with probabilistic analysis of cluster sizes
title: 3-Colouring Graphs Excluding a Fixed Minor

catalog_references: Garg, Mineyev – A global girth obstruction for Garg–Mineyev taiko product structures
description: We conjecture that for any torsion‑free CAT(0) group G, every unit in the group ring ℱ₂[ G ] whose support containsających at least three elements must in fact be trivial.  Equivalently, if x ∈ ℱ₂[ G ] is a unit and |supp(x)| > 2, then x equals ±1.  This statement is falsifiable: a single example of a nontrivial unit with support size ≥ 3 in a torsion‑free CAT(0) group would refute it, while a general proof would require showing that any such unit would give rise to a finite product structure satisfying orientability (𝕋₁), no‑fold (𝕋₂) and triple‑girth (𝕋₄), contradicting the obstruction proved in the referenced paper.
domain_bridges: Combinatorics – finite product structures and girth
Ring theory – units of group rings
proof_strategy: Assume a nontrivial unit x ∈ ℱ₂[ G ] with |supp(x)| > 2.  Use the support sets of x and x⁻¹ to build a finite product structure Π of type (m,n) with m,n ≥ 2.  Show that Π must satisfy orientability (𝕋₁) and no‑fold (𝕋₂).  Then prove that the product identity forces Π to satisfy the triple‑girth condition (𝕋₄).  By the global girth obstruction theorem of Garg–Mineyev, this is impossible in a torsion‑free CAT(0) group, yielding a contradiction.  Thus no such unit can exist.
title: Nontrivial Units with Large Support in F₂[ G ] for Torsion‑Free CAT(0) Groups

description: For every integer k ≥ 6 with k ≡ 2 (mod 4), and for every pair of nonnegative integers (a, b) with a + b = k and a ≥ 1, the number 2^a · 3^b − 1 is composite. This formalizes the paper's theorem that row k of the principal skeleton L₁ contains no primes when k ≡ 2 (mod 4) and k ≥ 6. The proof exploits that k even forces a and b to share parity. When both even, 2^a · 3^b − 1 = (2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} − 1)(2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} + 1) via difference of squares, with both factors > 1 for k ≥ 6. When both odd, k ≡ 2 (mod 4) forces a ≡ b (mod 4), yielding 2^a · 3^b ≡ 1 (mod 5) so 5 | (2^a · 3^b − 1), and the cofactor exceeds 1 since k ≥ 6 excludes the case a = b = 1 where the value equals 5.
proof_strategy: Case split on parity of a and b. Since k ≡ 2 (mod 4) is even, a and b have the same parity. Case 1 (both even): apply difference of squares factorization 2^a · 3^b − 1 = (2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} − 1)(2^{a/2} · 3^{b/2} + 1), verify both factors exceed 1 using k ≥ 6. Case 2 (both odd): from a + b ≡ 2 (mod 4) with a,b odd, deduce a ≡ b (mod 4); compute 2^a · 3^b mod 5 using 2^4 ≡ 3^4 ≡ 1 (mod 5) to show 5 | (2^a · 3^b − 1); verify 2^a · 3^b − 1 > 5 since k ≥ 6 excludes (a,b) = (1,1). Subsume b = 0 into Case 1 since then a = k is even.
title: No primes in rows k ≡ 2 (mod 4) of the principal Collatz skeleton L₁

description: For each n ≥ 1, the map φ_n from the degree-n graded piece of the cone algebra on ℚⁿ to the (n−1)-chains of the ind-triangulation of S^{n−1} at all rational rays, defined on linearly independent tuples (v₁,…,vₙ) by φ_n([C(v₁,…,vₙ)]) = sgn(det(v₁,…,vₙ)) · Δ(ℚv₁,…,ℚvₙ), extends to a GL_n(ℚ)-equivariant isomorphism of ℚ-modules. This identifies the top-degree cone algebra graded piece with the spherical chain module computing H_{n−1}(S^{n−1}; ℚ).
proof_strategy: Define the cone algebra with its degree filtration and construct the spherical chain complex C(n) from rational rays with the stellar subdivision presentation. Verify well-definedness of φ_n by checking it respects the relations on both sides (stellar subdivision on the chain side, additivity on the cone side). Prove equivariance by direct computation of the GL_n(ℚ)-action on both sides.
