proof_strategy: Show that for tournaments, the FAS LP constraint matrix is totally unimodular on CM instances, and vice versa. Use the structural characterization of CM tournaments by Chen et al. (2020) to verify that every CM tournament satisfies the CI property (τ*_w = τ_w) by exhibiting integral optimal solutions to the FAS LP, and conversely that every CI tournament satisfies the CM property by showing the cycle packing LP has integral optima. The key bridge is the LP duality equality ν*_w = τ*_w and the chain of inequalities ν_w ≤ ν*_w = τ*_w ≤ τ_w.
title: Cycle Mengerian and Cycle Ideal Equivalence for Tournaments

description: The paper proves that a countable FAC poset P satisfies the Aharoni-Korman conjecture if P contains no saturated chain D such that either D or its reverse D* is of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x, where each D_x is infinite and co-wellfounded. The conjecture asserts that this condition is also necessary: if a countable FAC poset P does contain such a saturated chain, then P fails to satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture. This would yield a complete characterization of which countable FAC posets satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit countable FAC poset P containing a saturated chain of the forbidden form, then show that no chain in P can simultaneously meet every antichain in any antichain partition of P. The construction likely involves adapting the known counterexamples to the original Aharoni-Korman conjecture, using the specific structure of ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x to control all possible chain-antichain interactions.
title: Necessity of the forbidden chain condition for the Aharoni-Korman conjecture on countable FAC posets

description: For a squarefree integer N > 1 with an even number of prime factors, and a positive divisor d | N, let w_d denote the corresponding Atkin-Lehner involution on the Shimura curve X_N. The genus of the quotient X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ is determined by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula applied to the double cover X_N → X_N / ⟨w_d⟩, where the number of fixed points of w_d equals the number of optimal embeddings of a certain quadratic order into the quaternion order, expressible via class numbers. The conjecture is: X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ has genus zero if and only if (N, d) belongs to an explicit finite list, which strictly contains the list {(6,6), (10,10), (22,22)} arising from genus-zero X_N alone. This classification is the key structural result enabling the extension of the Giampietro-Darmon factorization beyond the original conjecture.
proof_strategy: First formalize the genus formula for Shimura curves X_N of discriminant N (already explicit in the literature, e.g., Ogg). Then formalize the fixed-point count of Atkin-Lehner involutions w_d in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders via optimal embedding counts. Apply Riemann-Hurwitz to the double cover X_N → X_N/⟨w_d⟩ to obtain the genus of the quotient. Finally, enumerate all pairs (N, d) with N squarefree, ω(N) even, d | N, for which the resulting genus is zero, yielding the explicit finite classification.
title: Genus-Zero Classification of Atkin-Lehner Quotients of Shimura Curves

description: A Δ-matroid (E, F) is strong (i.e., satisfies the symmetric exchange axiom: for all A, B ∈ F and e ∈ A\B, there exists f ∈ B\A such that A △ {e,f} ∈ F and B △ {e,f} ∈ F) if and only if it contains no peerless antipode. Here, an antipode of a feasible set A with respect to an element e is a feasible set B obtained from A by exchanging e for some f, and a peerless antipode is one that is unique in a specific local sense within the feasible set system. This equivalence provides a local obstruction characterization for the global symmetric exchange property, analogous to how local submodularity characterizes global submodularity for rank functions.
domain_bridges: Tropical geometry (peerless antipode equations as tropicalization of orthogonal Grassmannian quadratics)
proof_strategy: Forward direction (strong ⟹ no peerless antipode): Assume symmetric exchange holds and suppose for contradiction that a peerless antipode exists at some feasible set A with element e. Use the symmetric exchange property between A and any other feasible set witnessing the peerless configuration to construct a second antipode, contradicting peerlessness. Backward direction (no peerless antipode ⟹ strong): Assume no peerless antipode exists and suppose symmetric exchange fails for some A, B ∈ F with e ∈ A\B. Show that the failure produces a peerless antipode: the element e at A has at most one viable exchange partner f ∈ B\A with A △ {e,f} ∈ F, and the absence of any other witness forces this antipode to be peerless, contradicting the hypothesis.
title: Strong Δ-matroids are characterized by the absence of peerless antipodes

description: Every symmetric edge polytope of dimension at most 35 has a gamma-positive Ehrhart h*-polynomial; equivalently, 36 is the minimum dimension in which a symmetric edge polytope can fail to be gamma-positive. This is motivated by the paper's construction of a 36-dimensional counterexample to the Ohsugi-Tsuchiya conjecture and by extensive computational evidence for small graphs.
proof_strategy: Combine exhaustive computational verification for graphs on few vertices with structural graph-theoretic arguments showing that any counterexample to gamma-positivity must arise from graphs with sufficiently complex series-parallel structure (specifically, requiring at least 5 parallel paths of length at least 8), thereby establishing a minimum vertex count and hence minimum dimension threshold.
title: Gamma-positivity threshold for symmetric edge polytopes

catalog_references: Polynomial mixing for polygonal side matchings
description: The paper establishes that the diameter of the connected component of the chord swap graph on chord diagrams of size n and genus g (for n > 2g) is bounded above by C(n + g^2) for some universal constant C > 0. We conjecture that this universal constant can be taken to be exactly 1, yielding a tight diameter upper bound of precisely n + g^2.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit short paths between any two chord diagrams by defining a canonical minimal genus diagram and showing that any diagram can be reduced to this canonical form in at most (n + g^2)/2 swaps. This would establish the diameter bound via the triangle inequality. Alternatively, use structural induction on n and g, verifying that the bound holds for base cases and that any valid chord swap preserves the bound.
title: Optimal Diameter Bound for Fixed Genus Chord Swap Graphs

description: For any simple graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) > |V(G)|/3, the chromatic index of G is Delta(G) if and only if G contains no Delta(G)-overfull subgraph. Equivalently, if Delta(G) > |V(G)|/3 and G contains no Delta(G)-overfull subgraph, then G is class 1.
proof_strategy: Assume G is class 2, meaning chi'(G) = Delta(G) + 1. Analyze the structure of critical subgraphs. Show that a Delta-critical graph with Delta > n/3 must contain an overfull subgraph, deriving a contradiction to the assumption that no overfull subgraph exists.
title: Overfull Conjecture

description: For a prime power q and a positive integer n, the maximum codimension of a cyclically covering subspace of F_q^n, denoted h_q(n), is zero if and only if every nonzero cyclic code in F_q^n contains a codeword of full Hamming weight.
proof_strategy: Establish the duality between cyclically covering subspaces and cyclic codes. Show that a subspace failing to cyclically cover F_q^n implies the existence of a vector outside the union of its cyclic shifts, which translates under orthogonal complementation to a nonzero cyclic code lacking any full-weight codeword, and vice versa.
title: Equivalence of Vanishing Cyclically Covering Codimension and Full-Weight Cyclic Codes

description: The maximum of the logarithm of the absolute value of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line over the interval [T, 2T], defined as M_T = max_{t ∈ [T, 2T]} log|ζ(1/2 + it)|, satisfies the convergence in distribution: M_T - log(log(T)) + (3/2)log(log(log(T))) converges to the sum of two independent Gumbel random variables as T → ∞. This captures the extreme value statistics of the number-theoretic analogue to the black hole microstate counts proposed in the paper.
proof_strategy: Model the Riemann zeta function as the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix, establish a Gaussian multiplicative chaos representation for the field, and extend the Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE) maximum theorem to the number theory setting using correlations of zeros.
title: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture for the Riemann Zeta Function

description: There exists a matroid M on a finite ground set E and unordered pairs of bases {B₁, B₂} and {B₁', B₂'} of M such that the multiset union of B₁ and B₂ equals the multiset union of B₁' and B₂', yet no sequence of symmetric exchanges transforms {B₁, B₂} into {B₁', B₂'}. This formalizes the counterexample to Farber's conjecture (the s=2 case of White's conjecture part (ii)) presented in the paper, which disproves the widely-believed symmetric exchange connectivity property for unordered pairs of matroid bases.
proof_strategy: Construct the explicit rank-3 matroid from the paper on a specific finite ground set, enumerate all its bases, identify the two unordered pairs of bases with equal multiset unions, then verify by exhaustive computation over all reachable states that no sequence of symmetric exchanges connects {B₁, B₂} to {B₁', B₂'}. The finiteness of the state space (the set of unordered pairs of bases with the same multiset union) makes exhaustive search feasible, and the symmetric exchange graph can be constructed and checked for disconnected components.
title: Farber's Conjecture Fails: A Matroid Counterexample to the Symmetric Exchange Property for Pairs of Bases

description: Formalizes a precise conjecture about the structural complexity of Sylow 2-permutation characters via bounds on parts of partitions, leveraging the binomial expansion of group orders.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence via analytic bounding of character degrees
title: Bounds on the number of Sylow 2-orbits in binary-partition contexts

description: Every simple graph of order n ≥ 8 with more than T(n) = (n^2 - 3n)/2 - ⌈n/2⌉ + 2 edges has strictly positive Ollivier/Lin-Lu-Yau curvature on all of its edges, and this threshold is optimal.
proof_strategy: Define the Lin-Lu-Yau curvature for a simple graph in Lean. Establish the threshold function T(n). Prove that for any graph G of order n ≥ 8 with |E(G)| > T(n), the optimal coupling between probability measures on the endpoints of any edge has a cost strictly less than 1, yielding positive curvature. This involves demonstrating that such graphs cannot contain edges satisfying deg(x) + deg(y) - |N(x) ∩ N(y)| ≥ n, a necessary condition for non-positive curvature, by characterizing the maximal edge count of graphs containing such edges.
title: Extremal Threshold for Positive Ollivier/Lin-Lu-Yau Curvature

description: For any split connected reductive group G over Q_p with Borel subgroup B and maximal torus T, the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) is Cohen-Macaulay. This strengthens the normality results established by Breuil-Hellmann-Schraen (for GL_n) and generalized in this paper (to arbitrary split reductive G, at certain points outside the smooth locus). Since Y^{tri}(G) is smooth of dimension dim(B) = dim(T) + |Φ^+| over the regular locus, Cohen-Macaulayness would follow from Serre's criterion (S2) combined with (R1) regularity in codimension 1. The (S2) condition is the deeper claim: for every point x ∈ Y^{tri}(G) with local ring O_{Y^{tri},x}, and every regular sequence f_1,...,f_d in the maximal ideal, the quotient O_{Y^{tri},x}/(f_1,...,f_d) has depth exactly d. This would imply the existence of well-behaved dualizing complexes and resolve the singularities of Y^{tri}(G) in the sense of local Langlands.
proof_strategy: Step 1: Formalize the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) as a rigid analytic space parameterizing trianguline G-representations with their triangulation data, using the Tannakian formalism for Rep_L(G) developed in the paper. Step 2: Establish that Y^{tri}(G) is regular in codimension ≤ 1 (condition R1) by analyzing the singular locus—its complement is the smooth regular locus characterized by the regularity of the triangulation parameter δ: T(Z_p) → T(E), and the singular locus has codimension ≥ 2 by dimension counting via the root structure of G. Step 3: Prove condition (S2) by showing that for every point x with codim ≥ 2, the local ring O_{Y^{tri},x} satisfies depth ≥ min(2, dim O_{Y^{tri},x}), using the crystallinity criterion for (φ,Γ)-modules with G-structure established in the paper to control the local equations. Step 4: Apply Serre's criterion (R1 + S2 ⟹ normal + CM for equidimensional schemes) to conclude.
title: Cohen-Macaulay Property of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

description: A set T = {a₀,b₀,...,aₘ,bₘ} ⊂ P¹(K) of 2g+2 distinct points over a finite extension K of Qₚ (p ≠ 2) is in good position (i.e., Γ(T) = ⟨s₀,...,sₘ⟩ is discontinuous and equals the free product ⟨s₀⟩ * ⋯ * ⟨sₘ⟩) if and only if the tree T(T) has exactly 2g+1 edges and for each i ∈ {0,...,g}, the pair {aᵢ,bᵢ} is separated by a unique edge eᵢ of T(T), meaning aᵢ and bᵢ lie in different connected components of T(T) \ {eᵢ}. This provides the missing necessary and sufficient condition explicitly noted as unknown in the paper.
proof_strategy: (1) Forward direction: Use the known necessary condition via T(T) and the Schottky group structure to show that Γ(T) being a free product of g+1 copies of Z/2Z forces T(T) to have exactly 2g+1 edges with the unique-separation property. (2) Reverse direction: Show the tree-separation condition implies that each involution sᵢ has an attracting/repelling dynamics on P¹(K) with non-overlapping fundamental domains in the Bruhat-Tits tree, then apply results on discontinuous groups (e.g., via reduction maps and the action on the Bruhat-Tits tree) to verify Γ(T) is Schottky. (3) Key tool: Kadziela-type approximation to control the relationship between tree structure and the group action.
title: Tree Characterization of Good Position for Hyperelliptic Mumford Curves

description: Every symmetric coloring of the Hales-Jewett cube [t]^n (one invariant under all coordinate permutations) is realized by a radix weight: there exist integers w_1, ..., w_t such that the coloring depends only on the weighted letter sum Σ w_{x_i}. Formally, for all t, n, r ≥ 1, for every function c : Fin n → Fin t → Fin r satisfying c(x) = c(σ ∘ x) for all permutations σ on Fin n, there exists w : Fin t → ℤ such that for all x, y : Fin n → Fin t, (∑ i, w (x i)) = (∑ i, w (y i)) → c x = c y.
domain_bridges: permutation-invariant functions factor through weight sums
integer-valued weight realizations of orbit partitions
proof_strategy: First formalize the Hales-Jewett cube [t]^n as Fin n → Fin t, coordinate permutations as precomposition with equivalences on Fin n, and symmetric colorings as those invariant under this action. Prove that orbit equivalence (having the same multiset of letters, i.e., the same letter-count vector) is the finest invariant partition. Then construct the radix weight w : Fin t → ℤ by w(j) = (t+1)^j (or any strictly increasing sequence), showing the radix-weighted sum is injective on letter-count vectors, hence the coloring factors through this sum.
title: Symmetric-Weight Equivalence for Hales-Jewett Colorings

description: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension of characteristic zero. Let G be a semiabelian variety over K, and let f: X → G be a finite morphism from a projective variety X of general type. Then the set X(K) of K-rational points is not Zariski dense in X. This extends the recent theorem of Xie-Yuan and Gao (which proves the case where G is an abelian variety) to the broader class of semiabelian varieties — extensions of abelian varieties by algebraic tori G_m^n. The principal new difficulty is the non-compactness of the torus component, which disrupts both the Nevanlinna-theoretic construction of entire curves from high-height rational points and the height theory used in the Vojta dictionary.
proof_strategy: Adapt the Vojta dictionary framework of Xie-Yuan from abelian to semiabelian varieties in three stages. (1) Reduce to the case where X contains no translate of a positive-dimensional semiabelian subvariety, using the known Mordell-Lang theorem for semiabelian varieties over function fields (McQuillan, 1995). (2) Develop a toric height theory that controls the growth of Néron-Tate heights on the G_m^n component, analogous to the abelian variety height machine but accounting for logarithmic singularities at the boundary of the compactification. (3) Extend the Nevanlinna theory arguments to construct entire curves in complex fibers from high-height rational points, using logarithmic defect relations for non-compact targets. The key technical challenge is that entire curves in G_m^n can accumulate at the boundary, requiring logarithmic Nevanlinna theory with value distribution estimates for meromorphic functions with essential singularities at the torus boundary.
title: Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture for Finite Covers of Semiabelian Varieties

description: For a finite nonempty poset P, the probabilistic powerdomain V₁(P) — the probability simplex on P ordered by the stochastic order — is an RB-domain if and only if P has a least element and the undirected Hasse graph of P is a tree. This encompasses two failure modes: (1) if P lacks a least element, the face of probability measures supported on minimal points is fixed pointwise by every deflation below the identity; (2) if the Hasse graph contains a cycle, the local stochastic cone becomes non-simplicial, precluding the finite-valued monotone approximations required by the RB property.
domain_bridges: finite_posets ↔ domain_theory: Hasse graph connectivity constrains domain-theoretic approximation
convex_geometry ↔ domain_theory: simplicial structure of local stochastic cones enables/disables deflation constructions
graph_theory ↔ order_theory: tree property of undirected Hasse graph characterizes deflation-existence
proof_strategy: Split into two directions. Forward (necessity): prove the contrapositive via two obstructions. Obstruction 1: if P has no least element, every deflation r ≤ id fixes the face of probability measures on minimal points pointwise, so no directed family of deflations can approximate the identity. Obstruction 2: if P has a least element but the Hasse graph has a cycle, the local stochastic cone at the Dirac measure on the least element is non-simplicial; a Euclidean finite-step cone argument then shows no finite-valued monotone approximation exists. Backward (sufficiency): given P with least element and tree Hasse graph, construct explicit directed family of deflations on V₁(P) with pointwise supremum the identity, using inductive decomposition along the tree structure.
title: Probabilistic powerdomain RB-domain characterization for finite posets

description: Every well-founded partially ordered set satisfying the finite antichain condition (FAC) has the Aharoni-Korman property: there exists a chain C and a partition of the poset into antichains such that C intersects every antichain in the partition. The paper proves the Aharoni-Korman conjecture for countable FAC posets avoiding a specific chain obstruction (saturated chains of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x with each D_x infinite and co-wellfounded). This conjecture extends the result to all well-founded FAC posets, regardless of cardinality, since well-foundedness eliminates infinite descending obstructing chains and structurally constrains ascending ones.
proof_strategy: Stratify the well-founded poset by rank into well-ordered levels. Apply the paper's countable decomposition and scattered poset analysis within each stratum. Use transfinite induction on the rank function to construct the witnessing chain and antichain partition globally, ensuring the chain meets every antichain in the partition at each inductive stage. The key insight is that well-foundedness provides a rank function that naturally organizes the construction and prevents the specific chain obstruction identified in the paper.
title: Aharoni-Korman Property for Well-Founded FAC Posets

description: If the Atkin-Lehner quotient of a Shimura curve of level N has genus zero, then the norm of certain algebraic numbers (defined via p-adic cross-ratios of CM points) equals the product conjectured by Giampietro and Darmon.
proof_strategy: Induce p-adic structures from Atkin-Lehner quotient genus zero, reduce to inverse counting problems via HY framework, and verify norm equality through Galois action compatibility with Gross-Zagier parallels.
title: Norm Formula via Atkin-Lehner Genus Zero Condition

description: For a Δ-matroid on a finite ground set E with feasible set family F, the following are equivalent: (1) the Δ-matroid is strong, i.e., satisfies Wenzel's symmetric exchange property (for all B₁, B₂ ∈ F, if e ∈ B₁ \ B₂ and f ∈ B₂ \ B₁, then there exists g ∈ (B₁ Δ B₂) \ {e,f} such that exactly one of B₁ Δ {e,g} or B₂ Δ {f,g} is in F, or B₁ Δ {e,f} ∈ F and B₂ Δ {e,f} ∈ F); and (2) the Δ-matroid has no peerless antipode (no feasible set B has an antipode A—maximizing |B Δ A|—that is peerless, meaning it is the unique antipode of B satisfying a certain local maximality condition within the antipode system). This equivalence bridges the classical exchange-axiom framework with the novel antipode-combinatorial characterization introduced in the paper.
proof_strategy: Define Δ-matroids, feasible sets, symmetric difference distance, antipodes (feasible sets at maximal symmetric difference from a given feasible set), and peerless antipodes (antipodes that are unique with respect to a local exclusion condition). For the forward direction, show that Wenzel's symmetric exchange prevents the existence of a peerless antipode by demonstrating that any candidate peerless antipode can be exchanged to produce a second distinct antipode violating peerlessness. For the reverse direction, show that a violation of Wenzel's exchange yields a feasible set pair whose antipode structure forces a peerless antipode, by constructing a minimal counterexample and analyzing the antipode configuration around it.
title: Equivalence of Wenzel symmetric exchange and no peerless antipodes for Δ-matroids

description: For the family of series-parallel graphs G(a) obtained by joining two distinguished vertices s and t with m disjoint paths of lengths a_1, ..., a_m, the paper shows that gamma-positivity of the h*-polynomial of Q_G fails for m >= 5. The conjecture is that for m <= 4, gamma-positivity always holds: for every vector a in Z_{>=1}^4, the h*-polynomial of Q_{G(a)} is gamma-positive. This would yield a complete classification of gamma-positivity for this family.
proof_strategy: For m <= 3, leverage known results: graphs with a vertex connected to all others (cones) are gamma-positive by Ohsugi-Tsuchiya, and complete bipartite graphs by Higashitani-Jochemko-Michalek. For m = 4, compute the gamma-polynomial coefficients using the regular unimodular triangulation structure of symmetric edge polytopes and show all coefficients are non-negative. The linear and quadratic gamma-coefficients are already known positive; the key is controlling the cubic and higher terms via the combinatorics of the series-parallel structure.
title: Gamma-positivity of symmetric edge polytopes for series-parallel graphs with at most four paths

description: For any natural numbers n, g with n > 2g, the graph whose vertices are chord diagrams (perfect matchings) of genus g on 2n vertices, and whose edges connect diagrams differing by a genus-preserving chord swap, is connected and has diameter at most 100(n + g^2).
proof_strategy: Define chord diagrams as perfect matchings on Fin (2*n) and genus via the cycle count of the composition of the matching involution and the canonical cyclic permutation. Construct explicit sequences of genus-preserving swaps to reduce any diagram to a canonical form, bounding the number of swaps by 100(n + g^2) to establish both connectivity and the explicit diameter bound.
title: Connectedness and Diameter Bound of the Genus-Preserving Chord Swap Graph

description: For every simple graph G with maximum degree Δ(G) > |V(G)|/3, the chromatic index χ'(G) equals Δ(G) if and only if G contains no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (a subgraph H with |E(H)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(H)|/2⌋). This would yield a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of dense graphs and implies several longstanding conjectures including the 1-Factorization Conjecture for regular graphs.
proof_strategy: First formalize the core graph-theoretic infrastructure (chromatic index, overfull subgraphs, critical graphs). Prove key lemmas: (1) any Δ-overfull subgraph forces class 2, (2) the Petersen-minus-vertex P* is class 2 with no 3-overfull subgraph (showing Δ > |V|/3 is tight), (3) reduction to Δ-critical graphs. Then apply structural decomposition of critical graphs with Δ > |V|/3 to show they must contain overfull subgraphs, extending known results from Δ ≥ |V|−2 inward.
title: The Overfull Conjecture

catalog_references: Cyclic Codes and Cyclically Covering Subspaces over Finite Fields
description: For a prime power q and positive integer n, the maximum possible codimension h_q(n) of a cyclically covering subspace in F_q^n is zero if and only if every nonzero cyclic code in F_q^n contains a full-weight codeword.
proof_strategy: Define cyclically covering subspaces and their codimension h_q(n), define cyclic codes and full-weight codewords, then show that a subspace fails to be cyclically covering if and only if its dual is a nonzero cyclic code without a full-weight codeword, establishing the equivalence.
title: Codimension Zero Equivalence for Cyclically Covering Subspaces and Cyclic Codes

description: The maximum fluctuation of log-microstate counts log Ω_N(E) over energy intervals of width O(√E) in large-N AdS/CFT belongs to the Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating universality class of Gaussian log-correlated fields. Specifically, defining M_N = max_{E ∈ [E₀, E₀ + δ]} log Ω_N(E) with δ ∝ √E₀ and E₀ ∝ N² (the black hole mass scale), the rescaled maximum (M_N - μ_N)/σ_N converges in distribution to a random variable with the modified Gumbel cumulative distribution function exp(-K·exp(-s)), where μ_N = (1/2)·S_N·log(S_N), σ_N = log(S_N), S_N ∝ N² is the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and K > 0 is a universal constant determined by the log-correlated field covariance structure. This modified Gumbel with logarithmic correction factors distinguishes the FHK universality class from the classical Gumbel extreme value distribution and parallels the original FHK conjecture for max_t log|ζ(1/2+it)| on [0,T].
proof_strategy: Establish the Gaussian log-correlated field structure of log Ω_N(E) via the holographic dictionary, identifying the covariance Cov(log Ω_N(E), log Ω_N(E')) ∼ log(N/|E-E'|) for nearby energies. Then apply the branching random walk / Gaussian multiplicative chaos framework to characterize the maximum: (1) prove the sub-leading order maximum concentrates via second moment method on the 'peaks' landscape of the log-correlated field; (2) establish the modified Gumbel tail by showing the maximum over dyadic mesoscopic intervals factorizes asymptotically (the decorrelation property); (3) identify the constant K via the local limit theorem for the number of high peaks. The key technical bridge is the equivalence between erratic N-dependence in AdS/CFT and the decorrelation of independent copies of the Gaussian model.
title: FHK Universality Class for Black Hole Microstate Extreme Values

description: While White's conjecture on symmetric exchanges (Part 2) is false, the weaker Part 3 remains open: for any matroid M and any two multisets of bases B and B' with the same multiset union of elements, it is possible to obtain B' from B by repeatedly replacing two bases with any two other bases having the same multiset union. This is equivalent to the toric ideal of the matroid basis exchange ring being generated by quadratic binomials.
proof_strategy: The conjecture could be approached by demonstrating that the toric ideal of any matroid basis exchange ring is generated by quadratic binomials. One could use tropical geometry or Gröbner basis techniques, or attempt an inductive proof on matroid minors, extending the methods used for specific matroid classes like uniform or graphic matroids.
title: White's Quadratic Exchange Conjecture (Part 3)

description: For any rational polytopal measure P in R^d, the cap-volume function mapping an oriented hyperplane parameterized by (a,b) in R^(d+1) to the volume of P intersected with the halfspace {x | <a, x> <= b} is piecewise rational. Specifically, there exists a finite semialgebraic partition of the parameter space such that on each cell, the cap-volume is given by a rational function of the parameters.
proof_strategy: Define the natural decomposition of the space of oriented hyperplanes based on the combinatorial structure of the intersection P ∩ H_(a,b)^+. Specifically, partition the parameter space into cells where the set of vertices of P lying strictly inside, strictly outside, and on the boundary of the halfspace remains constant. On each such cell, the vertices of the intersection polytope are rational functions of (a,b). Since the volume of a polytope is a sum of determinants of its vertices, the volume function is a rational function of (a,b) on each cell, proving piecewise rationality.
title: Piecewise Rationality of the Polytopal Cap-Volume Function

description: For any integer n >= 11, let a_1 = floor(log_2 n) and t be the number of ones in the binary expansion of n. A non-hook partition of n with at most k parts is an irreducible constituent of the 2-Sylow permutation character of S_n if and only if k <= a_1 + t - 1.
proof_strategy: Induction on n, utilizing the branching rule for symmetric group characters, properties of the binary expansion of n (specifically relating the highest power of 2 and the Hamming weight to partition structures), and explicit character calculations to verify the base cases and the inductive step.
title: Exact Bound for Non-Hook Partitions in the Sylow 2-Permutation Character

description: The trianguline variety X^{tri}_G associated to a split connected reductive group G over a p-adic field K is Cohen-Macaulay. Specifically, for every point x in X^{tri}_G with local ring O_{X^{tri}_G,x}, the depth equals the Krull dimension: depth(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}) = dim(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}). This extends the paper's results establishing smoothness on the very regular locus and normality at certain points outside this locus, predicting that all singularities are as mild as possible. Cohen-Macaulayness would imply full normality of X^{tri}_G (since CM implies Serre's condition S2, and the smooth locus has complement of codimension ≥ 2 by the regularity conditions on the triangulation parameter), strengthening the paper's partial normality result. It would also have significant consequences for the deformation theory of p-adic Galois representations with G-structure and for understanding the local Langlands correspondence via the geometry of the trianguline variety.
proof_strategy: The proof would proceed by analyzing the local structure of the trianguline variety at each point. Key steps: (1) On the very regular locus, the variety is smooth (proven in the paper), hence Cohen-Macaulay. (2) At singular points, use the Tannakian formalism developed in the paper to reduce to understanding the tangent cone in terms of root data. (3) The tangent cone at a singular point with parameter δ should be controlled by the roots α for which δ∘α∨ fails to be regular—these correspond to the walls of the Weyl chambers where smoothness breaks down. (4) Show that the defining ideal at each point is generated by a regular sequence of length equal to the codimension, leveraging the crystallinity criterion from the paper to explicitly describe the deformation ring. (5) The root system combinatorics (specifically, the Chevalley commutation relations and the structure of the unipotent radical) should ensure the regular sequence property holds via an inductive argument on the height of r
title: Cohen-Macaulayness of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

description: For a prime p ≠ 2, a finite extension K of Q_p, and a set T = {a₀, b₀, ..., aᵍ, bᵍ} ⊂ P¹(K) of size 2g+2 with g ≥ 1, the set T is in good position (meaning Γ(T) = ⟨s₀,...,sᵍ⟩ is discontinuous and equals the free product ⟨s₀⟩*...*⟨sᵍ⟩, where each sᵢ has order 2 with fixed points {aᵢ,bᵢ}) if and only if: (1) the tree T(T) constructed from the reduction data is a path graph of length 2g+1, and (2) the p-adic valuations of the off-diagonal entries of normalized representatives of the sᵢ satisfy explicit contraction bounds ensuring the generators act as sufficiently contracting maps on the respective complementary residue disks in the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K).
proof_strategy: The forward direction (necessity) follows from the paper's Lemma establishing that good position implies the tree T(T) has the required path structure. The backward direction (sufficiency) requires showing that when T(T) is a path of length 2g+1 and the contraction bounds hold, the group Γ(T) is free on the generators sᵢ: one analyzes the action on the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K), showing that the contraction conditions force each reduced word in the sᵢ to act without fixed points in Ω_Γ, precluding any relations beyond sᵢ² = 1. The p-adic analytic estimates on matrix entries control how far the generators move points in the Bruhat-Tits tree, ensuring that compositions cannot create accidental fixed points.
title: Tree-Contraction Characterization of Good Position for p-adic Schottky Groups

description: For all t ≥ 2 and r ≥ 2, the maximum dimension n for which there exists a line-free r-coloring of the Hales–Jewett cube [t]^n equals the maximum dimension n for which there exists a one-weight (equivalently, symmetric) line-free r-coloring of [t]^n. That is, one-weight colorings are extremal for the lower-bound problem: no arbitrary coloring avoids combinatorial lines in a dimension that no symmetric coloring can.
domain_bridges: Ramsey theory ↔ one-dimensional arithmetic combinatorics (via the coincidence of symmetric and one-weight colorings)
higher-dimensional combinatorial geometry ↔ integer-weighted counting (via radix weight representation)
proof_strategy: Prove the coincidence lemma (symmetric ↔ one-weight, already established in the paper) in Lean. Then show that for any line-free r-coloring c of [t]^n, the symmetrization c_sym(x) = c(σ·x) averaged over all coordinate permutations σ ∈ S_n either inherits line-freeness or can be deformed into a one-weight line-free coloring of the same dimension. The key obstacle is that symmetrization may introduce monochromatic lines; resolving this likely requires constructing an explicit radix weight from the orbit structure of c and showing the induced one-weight coloring avoids lines whenever c does. Falsification reduces to a finite computation: find t, r, n and a line-free r-coloring of [t]^n such that no one-weight r-coloring of [t]^n is line-free.
title: Symmetric-Extremality Conjecture for Hales–Jewett Lower Bounds

description: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension of characteristic zero, with k algebraically closed. Let X be a smooth projective variety of general type over K. If X admits a finite morphism to a semi-abelian variety over K, then X(K) is not Zariski dense in X. This extends the Xie-Yuan/Gao theorem (which proves the case for abelian varieties) to semi-abelian varieties—algebraic groups that are extensions of abelian varieties by algebraic tori. The special locus of a semi-abelian variety includes both translates of proper abelian subvarieties and cosets of the torus part, providing additional sources of rational points that must be understood to establish non-density.
proof_strategy: Extend the Xie-Yuan/Gao approach via the Vojta dictionary to semi-abelian varieties. Step 1: From a Zariski-dense sequence of K-rational points on X of unbounded height, construct entire curves on complex-analytic fibers of the associated family over B. Step 2: Use the Chevalley decomposition of semi-abelian varieties (a torus extension of an abelian variety) and the structure of their subvarieties to classify possible entire curves. Step 3: Show that the logarithmic Kodaira dimension condition (general type) precludes such entire curves on fibers outside the special locus, yielding a contradiction. The torus part introduces new entire curves (via exponential maps of C^*) that must be ruled out using the general type hypothesis.
title: Geometric Bombieri-Lang for Finite Covers of Semi-Abelian Varieties

description: For a finite poset P, the probabilistic powerdomain V1(P) is an RB-domain if and only if the local stochastic cone at every point of V1(P) is simplicial. This conjecture provides a geometric characterization of the RB-property that is equivalent to the combinatorial condition (P has a least element and its undirected Hasse graph is a tree) proven in the paper. It is falsifiable because one could exhibit a finite poset whose probabilistic powerdomain is an RB-domain but has a non-simplicial stochastic cone at some point, or vice versa.
proof_strategy: The paper's Euclidean finite-step cone argument shows that a cycle in the Hasse graph makes the local stochastic cone non-simplicial, which obstructs the existence of the directed family of deflations required for an RB-domain. For the converse, assuming all stochastic cones are simplicial, one must construct a directed family of deflations with finite image approximating the identity. This could be done by projecting onto faces of the probability simplex corresponding to down-sets of P, using the tree structure implied by the simplicial cone condition.
title: Simplicial Stochastic Cone Characterization of RB-Domains in Probabilistic Powerdomains

description: Every countable well-founded poset with no infinite antichain (a well-founded FAC poset) possesses a chain C and a partition of the ground set into antichains such that C meets every antichain in the partition. This follows from the paper's main result because well-founded posets exclude saturated chains of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x with each D_x infinite and co-wellfounded: each such D_x, being infinite and co-wellfounded, contains infinite descending chains, contradicting well-foundedness of the ambient poset.
proof_strategy: First formalize the exclusion argument: well-founded countable FAC posets cannot contain saturated chains isomorphic to ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x with each D_x infinite and co-wellfounded, since co-wellfounded infinite posets contain infinite descending chains within each D_x piece, violating well-foundedness. Then formalize the paper's chain completion H(P) and structural decomposition of countable FAC posets into scattered pieces. Apply the paper's main theorem to the well-founded case to extract the witnessing chain and antichain partition.
title: Aharoni-Korman Property for Countable Well-Founded FAC Posets

description: Every countable scattered FAC poset satisfies the Aharoni-Korman property. Specifically: if P is a countable poset with no infinite antichain (FAC) and no dense subposet (scattered, meaning no subposet S where for all x < y in S there exists z in S with x < z < y), then there exists a chain C ⊆ P and a partition of P into antichains {A_i}_{i ∈ I} such that C ∩ A_i ≠ ∅ for every i ∈ I. This conjecture naturally extends the paper's result that AK holds for countable FAC posets avoiding certain saturated chains of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x, and is motivated by the paper's central structural theorem that countable FAC posets decompose into scattered pieces.
proof_strategy: Leverage the paper's decomposition theorem to express a countable scattered FAC poset as a structured sum of its scattered components. For each scattered component, construct a witnessing chain and antichain partition using the paper's techniques for avoiding ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x-type obstructions (which scatteredness should prevent). Then combine these local witnesses via a transfinite or inductive construction, ensuring the union chain meets every antichain in the global partition. The key step is showing that scatteredness rules out the saturated chain obstructions that produce AK counterexamples.
title: Scattered Countable FAC Posets Satisfy the Aharoni-Korman Property

description: The Giampietro-Darmon factorization formula for the norm of $p$-adic cross-ratios of CM points on Atkin-Lehner quotients of Shimura curves, currently proven only for genus 0 quotients, holds unconditionally for all squarefree $N > 1$ with an even number of prime factors. For quotients of higher genus, the infinite product of $p$-adic cross-ratios factors into a product of local intersection multiplicities of the corresponding Heegner divisors, up to a global obstruction given by the Néron-Tate height pairing on the Jacobian.
proof_strategy: Generalize the $p$-adic uniformization to higher genus quotients by considering the rigid analytic Jacobian, relate the $p$-adic cross-ratios to the Néron-Tate height pairing of Heegner divisors, and apply the $p$-inverted Howard-Yang counting problem to compute the local intersection multiplicities, thereby reducing the arbitrary genus case to the genus 0 case via a height decomposition.
title: Generalized Giampietro-Darmon Factorization for Arbitrary Genus

description: The paper proves that the set of centerpoints of a convex polytope P ⊂ ℝᵈ coincides with its floating body at level 1/(d+1) and is therefore semialgebraic, leveraging the piecewise-rational structure of the cap-volume function. This conjecture extends that result: for any compact convex semialgebraic set K ⊂ ℝᵈ with nonempty interior, the set of centerpoints of K (with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to K) is a convex semialgebraic set. For polytopes, piecewise-rationality of the cap-volume function gives semialgebraicity directly, but for general convex semialgebraic bodies the cap-volume function may not be piecewise rational, so new arguments (e.g., via o-minimal geometry or quantifier elimination over real closed fields with volume integrals) are needed.
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's semialgebraic feasibility framework: show that for a compact convex semialgebraic set K, the function mapping a hyperplane (parametrized by unit normal u ∈ S^{d-1} and offset t ∈ ℝ) to vol(K ∩ H_{u,t}) is a semialgebraic function of (u,t). This follows from cylindrical algebraic decomposition since K ∩ H_{u,t} is a semialgebraic family parametrized by (u,t) and integration over semialgebraic fibers preserves semialgebraicity. Then the centerpoint set {p : ∀u, vol(K ∩ H_{u,p·u}) ≥ vol(K)/(d+1)} is defined by a first-order formula over the reals with the volume function replaced by its semialgebraic description, yielding a semialgebraic set by Tarski's theorem. Convexity follows from the intersection-of-halfspaces characterization.
title: Convex Semialgebraicity of Centerpoint Sets for Convex Semialgebraic Bodies

description: Let $n \ge 11$ be a natural number with binary expansion $n = 2^{a_1} + 2^{a_2} + \dots + 2^{a_t}$ where $a_1 > a_2 > \dots > a_t \ge 0$. Let $\Delta(n,k)$ be the set of non-hook partitions of $n$ with at most $k$ parts, and let $\Omega_2(n)$ be the set of partitions labelling the irreducible constituents of the Sylow 2-permutation character of $S_n$. Then $\Delta(n,k) \subseteq \Omega_2(n)$ if and only if $k \le a_1 + t - 1$.
proof_strategy: Define the set of non-hook partitions with bounded length and the set of irreducible constituents of the permutation character on a Sylow 2-subgroup. Establish the iff condition by translating the combinatorial properties of the binary expansion of $n$ and partition lengths into the representation-theoretic setting, leveraging branching rules for symmetric group characters and known classifications of hook constituents.
title: Non-Hook Partition Bound for Sylow 2-Permutation Characters

description: Every countable well-founded poset with the finite antichain condition (FAC) satisfies the Aharoni-Korman property: there exists a chain C and a partition of P into antichains {A_i : i ∈ I} such that |C ∩ A_i| = 1 for each i ∈ I. This is a natural special case of the now-disproved Aharoni-Korman conjecture, restricting to well-founded posets where the rank function provides a canonical antichain partition and a transversal chain can potentially be constructed via a selector argument.
proof_strategy: Define the rank partition of P into antichains A_k = {x ∈ P : rank(x) = k}. Use the countable choice and well-foundedness to inductively construct a chain C by selecting one element from each A_k that is comparable with all previously selected elements. Verify the FAC condition ensures the necessary intersection properties via a König's lemma-style compactness argument on finite initial segments.
title: Aharoni-Korman Property for Countable Well-Founded Posets

description: The main theorem of the paper: Let N > 1 be a squarefree integer with an even number of prime factors, and let p be a prime divisor of N. The factorization formula for the norm of the p-adic cross-ratio infinite product of CM points on the Shimura curve X_N holds if the Atkin-Lehner quotient X_N / w_p has genus 0. This extends the original Giampietro-Darmon conjecture, which required the Shimura curve X_N itself to have genus 0 (a condition only satisfied for N in {6, 10, 22}).
proof_strategy: First formalize the definition of indefinite rational quaternion algebras, maximal orders, and the corresponding Shimura curves X_N over the rationals. Define the Atkin-Lehner involutions and compute the genus of the quotients X_N / w_p. Then construct the p-adic upper half plane, CM points, and the p-adic cross-ratio infinite product. Finally, connect the genus zero condition of the quotient to the p-inverted Howard-Yang counting problem to derive the explicit factorization of the norm.
title: Atkin-Lehner Genus Zero Criterion for Giampietro-Darmon Factorization

description: For any Δ-matroid M = (E, F) on a finite ground set E with feasible sets F, M is a strong Δ-matroid (satisfying Wenzel's symmetric exchange property) if and only if M has no peerless antipodes. An antipode of a feasible set X ∈ F is a feasible set Y ∈ F such that X and Y are at maximum Hamming distance among all pairs of feasible sets. A peerless antipode is an antipode that is the unique antipode of its partner feasible set. The peerless antipode property bans the existence of any peerless antipode in the system of feasible sets.
proof_strategy: Formalize Δ-matroids as dependent types on finite sets with feasible set collections. Define the symmetric exchange property (strong), the antipode relation via Hamming distance on symmetric difference, and the peerless antipode predicate. The forward direction proceeds by contradiction: assuming a peerless antipode exists, derive a violation of symmetric exchange. The reverse direction uses the peerless antipode property to construct the required exchange elements by showing that any failure of symmetric exchange would produce a peerless antipode configuration. The tropical algebraic motivation via orthogonal Grassmannian tropicalization may provide alternative algebraic proof strategies.
title: Equivalence of strong Δ-matroid and peerless antipode characterizations

description: Every symmetric edge polytope of dimension at most 35 has a γ-positive Ehrhart h*-polynomial. Equivalently, 36 is the minimum dimension of a symmetric edge polytope whose Ehrhart h*-polynomial fails to be γ-positive. This would sharpen the paper's existence result by establishing the exact threshold, confirming that no smaller counterexamples to the Ohsugi–Tsuchiya conjecture exist.
proof_strategy: Combine exhaustive computational verification of γ-positivity for all connected graphs on at most 9 vertices (covering dimensions ≤ 8) with structural arguments that γ-positivity is preserved under cone, join, and subdivision operations, thereby inductively covering all dimensions up to 35 while using the paper's explicit 36-dimensional counterexample as the lower bound.
title: Dimension Threshold for Gamma-Positivity of Symmetric Edge Polytopes

description: For the fixed genus chord swap Markov chain on chord diagrams with n chords and genus g, the spectral gap γ_{n,g} satisfies γ_{n,g} = Θ(n^{-3}) when g is fixed and n → ∞. This sharpens the paper's polynomial lower bound to a precise exponent and matches the n^{-3} scaling observed in related swap chains on perfect matchings.
proof_strategy: First formalize chord diagrams, genus via Euler characteristic, and the chord swap relation in Lean. Then establish the O(n^{-3}) upper bound on the spectral gap via comparison with the random transposition walk on matchings, and prove the Ω(n^{-3}) lower bound by constructing a canonical path argument with congestion bounded by O(n^3), extending the paper's coupling/canonical-path techniques.
title: Tight spectral gap exponent for the fixed-genus chord swap chain

description: Let C be a rigid tensor category and D be a tensor category. Any monoidal natural transformation α : F ⟶ G between two tensor functors F, G : C ⥤ D is an isomorphism. This formalizes Proposition 1.13 of Deligne-Milne, which the paper explicitly invokes to equate the tensor automorphism functor with the tensor homomorphism functor (uAut^⊗ = uHom^⊗) for rigid categories.
proof_strategy: Construct the inverse natural transformation β : G ⟶ F using the duality data of the rigid category C. For an object X in C, define β_X as the composite G(X) ≅ G(X) ⊗ I ⟶ G(X) ⊗ F(Xᵛ ⊗ X) ≅ G(X) ⊗ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ F(X)) ≅ (G(X) ⊗ F(Xᵛ)) ⊗ F(X) ⟶ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ G(X)) ⊗ F(X) ⟶ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ F(X)) ⊗ G(X) ⟶ ... utilizing the evaluation and coevaluation maps of the dual Xᵛ, along with the monoidal structure of F, G, and α. Prove that β is a monoidal natural transformation and the two-sided inverse of α.
title: Rigidity Implies Monoidal Natural Transformations Are Isomorphisms

description: For any odd prime q ≥ 3 and integer m ≥ 4, the maximum codimension of a cyclically covering subspace of 𝔽_q^n, denoted h_q(n), is strictly positive when n = (q^m+1)/2. This is equivalent to the existence of a proper subspace of 𝔽_q^n whose union of cyclic shifts covers the entire vector space.
proof_strategy: Translate the condition h_q(n) > 0 into the existence of a non-zero cyclic code without a full-weight codeword. Explicitly construct such a cyclic code in 𝔽_q^n for n = (q^m+1)/2 by defining its generator polynomial using the properties of the multiplicative group of 𝔽_{q^m}, and prove that no codeword in this code has full weight.
title: Positivity of Cyclically Covering Subspace Codimension for (q^m+1)/2

description: For any full-dimensional convex polytope P in ℝ^d, the set of centerpoints of P (with respect to the uniform Lebesgue measure on P) coincides with the floating body of P at level 1/(d+1). That is, a point c ∈ ℝ^d is a centerpoint—meaning every closed halfspace containing c captures at least 1/(d+1) of the volume of P—if and only if c belongs to the intersection of all closed halfspaces H⁺ satisfying vol(H⁺ ∩ P) ≥ vol(P)/(d+1). This equivalence, proved in the paper for convex polytopes, reveals a fundamental structural identity between a combinatorial-geometric object (centerpoints) and a convex-geometric object (floating bodies). Formalizing even the 2-dimensional case for triangles would require developing substantial infrastructure in convex geometry, measure theory on polytopes, and the centerpoint theorem.
proof_strategy: The proof proceeds in two parts. (1) Show every point in the floating body Float(P, 1/(d+1)) is a centerpoint: any halfspace containing a point in the floating body captures at least 1/(d+1) of the volume by definition of the floating body. (2) Show every centerpoint lies in the floating body: given a centerpoint c, for any halfspace H⁺ with vol(H⁺ ∩ P) ≥ vol(P)/(d+1), show c ∈ H⁺ by contradiction—if c ∉ H⁺, then the complementary halfspace H⁻ contains c but has volume at most d/(d+1), contradicting the centerpoint property when one constructs a halfplane through c that captures less than 1/(d+1) of the volume. The polytopal structure enters via the piecewise-rational decomposition of the cap-volume function, which ensures the floating body is semialgebraic and the infimum in its definition is attained.
title: Centerpoint-Floating Body Coincidence for Convex Polytopes

description: For every n ≥ 4 and every integer k with 2 ≤ k ≤ ⌈n/2⌉, there exists a non-hook partition λ of n with exactly k parts such that the irreducible character χ^λ is a constituent of the Sylow 2-permutation character (1_P)↑^{S_n}, where P is a Sylow 2-subgroup of S_n. This conjecture asserts that the set of part-counts realized by non-hook constituents of Ω₂(n) forms the complete interval [2, ⌈n/2⌉], complementing the paper's Theorem A (which guarantees all part-counts up to a_1+t-1) and Proposition on the maximum part-count ⌈n/2⌉.
proof_strategy: Use Theorem A to handle k ≤ a_1+t-1 (all such non-hook partitions are automatically in Ω₂(n)). For the range a_1+t ≤ k ≤ ⌈n/2⌉, construct explicit non-hook partitions with k parts that lie in Ω₂(n) by leveraging the branching rule and the structure of the Sylow 2-subgroup as an iterated wreath product of C_2. The upper bound k = ⌈n/2⌉ is covered by the paper's Proposition. The intermediate values require exhibiting witnesses, potentially using two-part partitions (n-k, k) and their relation to Young subgroups.
title: Full part-count spectrum of the Sylow 2-permutation character of S_n

description: The cyclotomic matrix $A_k(\chi) = [G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})]$ involving Gauss sums over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ (where $N=p^m$ and $n=\varphi(N)/k$) can be decomposed as the matrix product $W D W^T$, where $W$ is the $n \times n$ discrete Fourier transform matrix with entries $W_{i,a} = \omega^{ai}$ ($\omega$ being a primitive $n$-th root of unity) and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of the $n$ Gauss periods $\eta_a$ corresponding to the $k$-th power residue cyclotomic cosets.
proof_strategy: Rewrite the Gauss sum $G_N(\chi^{k(i+j)})$ by partitioning the summation over $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ into the $n$ cyclotomic cosets $C_a$ modulo $k$. Express $\chi^{k(i+j)}(x)$ as $\omega^{a(i+j)}$ for $x \in C_a$, pulling the root of unity out of the sum to yield $\sum_{a=0}^{n-1} \omega^{a(i+j)} \eta_a$, which directly translates to the matrix factorization $A_k(\chi) = W D W^T$.
title: Factorization of Cyclotomic Gauss Sum Matrix

description: For any graph of order n ≥ 8, if it contains strictly more than T(n) = (n^2 - 3n)/2 - ⌈n/2⌉ + 2 edges, then every edge in the graph has strictly positive Ollivier/Lin-Lu-Yau curvature.
proof_strategy: Formalize the Lin-Lu-Yau curvature using the 1-Wasserstein distance between probability measures on vertices. Establish structural properties of graphs with non-positive curvature edges, and demonstrate that exceeding the edge threshold T(n) precludes the existence of such subgraphs, thereby forcing all edge curvatures to be strictly positive.
title: Positive Curvature Threshold for Lin-Lu-Yau Curvature

description: Every symmetric r-coloring of the Hales-Jewett cube [t]^n — one invariant under all coordinate permutations of the word — is a one-weight coloring: there exist integer weights w_1, ..., w_t such that the color of a word x ∈ [t]^n depends only on the weighted sum ∑_i w_{x_i}. Conversely, every one-weight coloring is symmetric. This equivalence reduces the symmetric lower-bound problem for Hales-Jewett numbers to the d=1 case of Gallai's theorem on homothetic copies of a t-point set in Z.
domain_bridges: Integer-weighted letter sums as complete invariants
proof_strategy: The forward direction (one-weight ⇒ symmetric) is immediate since permuting coordinates preserves the multiset of letters and hence the weighted sum. For the converse, given a symmetric coloring c, construct the radix weight by examining how c distinguishes words that differ only in letter substitution: define w_j - w_1 as the minimal coordinate substitution that changes the color class when swapping a letter 1 for letter j in a fixed position. Show that the orbit of any word under coordinate permutations is determined by its letter-count vector, and that c factors through the weighted sum because symmetry forces c to depend only on the letter-count, which the radix weight encodes injectively modulo the kernel of c. The key combinatorial lemma is that the color partition of Z induced by the weighted sum is well-defined and independent of the choice of representative word.
title: Symmetric Colorings of Hales-Jewett Cubes Coincide with One-Weight Colorings

description: A class of finite graphs is homomorphism distinguishing closed if and only if it is closed under homomorphic equivalence, disjoint unions, and taking split-off minors. This conjecture proposes a corrected version of the Strong Roberson Conjecture by substituting the minor relation with the newly introduced split-off minor relation.
proof_strategy: For the backward direction, generalize the existing proof that closure under split-off minors and disjoint unions implies homomorphism distinguishing closed. For the forward direction, assume a class is homomorphism distinguishing closed and demonstrate it must be closed under split-off minors by showing that if G is a split-off minor of F in the class, excluding G would alter the homomorphism indistinguishability relation, leveraging the connection between oddomorphisms and split-off minors.
title: Split-Off Minor Characterization of Homomorphism Distinguishing Closed Classes

description: An irreducible polynomial F in K[x_1,...,x_d] over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero is algebraically degenerate (i.e., F divides a sum of non-constant univariate polynomials f_1(x_1)+...+f_d(x_d)) if and only if there exist non-zero polynomials G and univariate alpha_{1,j}, alpha_{2,i} such that for each i, the partial derivative F_{x_i} is congruent to G * alpha_{2,i}(x_i) * prod_{j!=i} alpha_{1,j}(x_j) modulo F. This translates the local analytic characterization of Theorem 2.3 into a global algebraic setting.
proof_strategy: Adapt the local analytic proof from the paper to the global algebraic setting using properties of algebraic curves and irreducibility, leveraging the fact that for polynomials over algebraically closed fields, local divisibility implies global divisibility, and applying Hilbert's Nullstellensatz to bridge the local zero sets to the global ideal structure.
title: Global Algebraic Degeneracy Criterion for Multivariate Polynomials

description: Theorem 2.3 of the referenced paper establishes that an irreducible polynomial $F \in \mathbb{R}[x_1, \ldots, x_d]$ is degenerate if and only if, near each coordinate regular point $p \in Z(F)$, the partial derivatives admit a separated analytic factorization $F_{x_i} = G \cdot \alpha_{2,i}(x_i) \prod_{j \neq i} \alpha_{1,j}(x_j)$ on $Z(F)$, where $G$ and $\alpha_{k,j}$ are real analytic. This conjecture asserts that when $F$ is degenerate, the analytic factorization can be promoted to a global polynomial congruence: there exist polynomials $\tilde{G} \in \mathbb{R}[x_1, \ldots, x_d]$ and $\tilde{\alpha}_{k,j} \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ such that $F_{x_k} \equiv \tilde{G} \cdot \tilde{\alpha}_{2,k}(x_k) \cdot \prod_{j \neq k} \tilde{\alpha}_{1,j}(x_j) \pmod{\langle F \rangle}$ for each $k = 1, \ldots, d$. This would yield a purely algebraic (and effectively computable) criterion for degeneracy, replacing the local analytic characterization with a global polynomial one.
proof_strategy: Since $F$ is irreducible, $\langle F \rangle$ is prime and the quotient $R = \mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/\langle F \rangle$ is an integral domain whose fraction field $K$ embeds into the field of meromorphic functions on any Zariski-open subset of the smooth locus of $Z(F)$. The analytic factorization from Theorem 2.3 forces each $\alpha_{i,j}$, viewed as a function on $Z(F)$, to satisfy algebraic relations over $K$. Since $F_{x_i} \in R$ and the factorization holds identically on an open dense subset, the $\alpha_{i,j}$ must be rational functions on $Z(F)$, hence elements of $K$. Clearing denominators yields the polynomial congruence modulo $F$. The key subtlety is ensuring the single-variable structure is preserved when lifting from analytic to algebraic, which requires showing that if a rational function on $Z(F)$ restricts to a function of $x_j$ alone on a Zariski-dense set, then it equals a rational function of $x_j$ in $K$.
title: Polynomial Lifting of the Separated Factorization for Degenerate Polynomials

description: For all finite graphs F and G, there exists an oddomorphism from F to G if and only if G is a split-off minor of F. The forward direction is established in the paper; the converse remains open.
proof_strategy: The forward direction is given by the paper's Theorem that oddomorphism from F to G implies G is a split-off minor of F. For the converse, attempt to construct an oddomorphism from F to G given that G is a split-off minor of F, by reversing each split-off minor operation step and verifying parity conditions on homomorphism counts are preserved. A counterexample search via CFI-type constructions could also be pursued.
title: Equivalence of Oddomorphism and Split-Off Minor

description: For natural numbers y > 2 and m > 1, the sequence defined by the initial value x_0 = 2^(1 + floor(ceil(log2 y) / m)) and the integer Newton-Raphson iteration x_{i+1} = x_i + floor((y - x_i^m) / (m * x_i^(m-1))) converges to the floor of y^(1/m). Specifically, there exists a natural number k such that for all j >= k, x_j = floor(y^(1/m)).
proof_strategy: Establish bounds for the initial value x_0 such that y^(1/m) <= x_0 <= 4 * y^(1/m). Then, prove by induction that the sequence monotonically decreases and remains greater than or equal to floor(y^(1/m)) until it reaches a fixed point. Finally, show that the only fixed point of the iteration in this range is floor(y^(1/m)).
title: Convergence and Correctness of Integer Newton-Raphson for Integer Roots

description: For every positive integer n and positive reals α, β with αβ = π², the alternating Hurwitz zeta function ζ_E(s, x) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ (-1)^k / (k + x)^s satisfies a Ramanujan-type identity generalizing Ramanujan's classical formula for ζ(2n+1). Specifically, the alternating Hurwitz kernel K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) := ½ζ_E(2n+1, x) + Σ_{m=1}^∞ m^{-2n-1}/(e^{2αm} + 1) obeys: α^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) − (−β)^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(β, 1−x) = 2^{2n} Σ_{k=0}^{n+1} (−1)^{k−1} E_{2k}(x) B_{2n−2k+2} / ((2k)!(2n−2k+2)!) · α^{n−k+1} β^k, where E_{2k}(x) are Euler polynomials and B_{2k} are Bernoulli numbers. This replaces the Bernoulli numbers B_{2k} in Ramanujan's original identity with Euler polynomials E_{2k}(x), reflecting the alternating (sign-twisted) structure.
proof_strategy: Adapt the classical proof of Ramanujan's identity via modular symmetry: (1) Define the alternating Hurwitz kernel K_E^s(α, x) and establish its meromorphic continuation using the contour integral representation of ζ_E(s, x); (2) Apply Poisson summation or Mellin transform techniques to derive the modular transformation α → π²/α on K_E, exploiting the functional symmetry x ↔ 1−x inherent to the alternating series; (3) Express the residues and poles of the transformed kernel in terms of Euler polynomials E_{2k}(x) via their generating function sech(t)·exp(xt) = Σ E_n(x) t^n/n!, matching the Bernoulli generating function t/(e^t−1) used in the classical proof; (4) Compare both sides as meromorphic functions of α, verifying equality at all poles and residues.
title: Alternating Hurwitz–Ramanujan Identity with Euler Polynomials

description: For any finite field 𝔽_q with char(𝔽_q) ∉ {2, 5}, every exceptional rational function f ∈ 𝔽_q(X) of degree 5 has geometric monodromy group isomorphic to either C₅ (cyclic of order 5) or D₅ (dihedral of order 10). This rules out A₅, S₅, F₂₀ (Frobenius group of order 20), and all other transitive subgroups of S₅ as geometric monodromy groups for such functions.
proof_strategy: Enumerate all transitive subgroups of S₅ (C₅, D₅, F₂₀, A₅, S₅). For each non-cyclic non-dihedral group, use the Riemann-Hurwitz formula applied to the cover φ: P¹ → P¹ defined by f to derive contradictions with the ramification structure imposed by the group's conjugacy class data and the exceptionality condition (which forces the arithmetic monodromy group to act as a sharply transitive group on a fiber). The key inequality from Riemann-Hurwitz, combined with the branch cycle description of inertia groups, eliminates F₂₀, A₅, and S₅ as possibilities for the geometric monodromy group when char ∉ {2,5} and deg = 5.
title: Geometric monodromy groups of exceptional degree-5 rational functions are cyclic or dihedral

description: For every doubly regular tournament on n vertices (where n ≡ 3 mod 4 and n ≥ 3), the metric dimension β(G) is at most ⌈3·log₂(n)⌉. This provides an explicit constant in the O(log n) bound established for related families in the paper, extending the probabilistic method of Babai to the directed tournament setting with a constructive resolvability guarantee.
proof_strategy: Adapt Babai's probabilistic method: for a doubly regular tournament on n=4k+3 vertices, every vertex has out-degree 2k+1 and every pair of distinct vertices shares exactly k common out-neighbours. Sample a random set S of size ⌈3·log₂(n)⌉ vertices. For any pair (u,v) of distinct vertices, compute the probability over the random choice of S that all s ∈ S give d(s,u)=d(s,v). Use the strong regularity properties to bound this probability below 1/n², then take a union bound over all pairs. The key structural lemma is that in a doubly regular tournament, for any distinct u,v, the set {s : d(s,u) ≠ d(s,v)} has size at least n/3, giving each sample at least a 1/3 chance of distinguishing u from v.
title: Explicit logarithmic bound on metric dimension of doubly regular tournaments

description: The paper proves that for k ≥ 3 and sufficiently large n, the maximum number of points in an n × n grid with no k+1 collinear points equals kn. This conjecture asserts that 'sufficiently large' can be replaced by the explicit threshold n ≥ k. Note that for n ≤ k the whole grid has no k+1 collinear points so f_k(n) = n², and for n = k we get f_k(k) = k² = k·k, making n ≥ k the natural boundary. The conjecture predicts that for all k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k, the trivial upper bound kn is always achievable.
proof_strategy: The paper's approach splits into: (1) handling 'heavy' lines via pseudorandom hypergraph matchings (Ehard-Glock-Joos), (2) crude deletion for remaining violations, (3) randomized switching to recover near-optimal size. To push 'sufficiently large n' down to n ≥ k, one would need to make each step effective with explicit bounds. The hypergraph matching step likely requires the most careful analysis for small n. A computer-verified case analysis for small n (up to some explicit bound) combined with the asymptotic argument for larger n could work. The key is determining whether the o(n) deletion/swinging losses can be controlled when n is close to k.
title: Explicit Threshold for No-(k+1)-in-line: f_k(n) = kn for all k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k

description: For every d ≥ 3, the supremum of normalized surface measures of zero-sum-free measurable subsets of the unit sphere S^{d-1} in ℝ^d equals exactly 1/2. Equivalently, every measurable zero-sum-free A ⊆ S^{d-1} satisfies σ_{d-1}(A) ≤ 1/2, with equality achieved (only) by open hemispheres. The paper establishes the asymptotic bound m_d ≤ 1/2 + O(1/d), but the exact value m_d = 1/2 remains open.
domain_bridges: Cap set problem and polynomial method (Croot-Lev-Pach / Ellenberg-Gijswijt)
Spherical harmonics and spectral analysis on S^{d-1}
proof_strategy: The paper establishes m_d ≤ ⌊(d+1)²/2⌋/(d(d+1)) = 1/2 + O(1/d) using spherical harmonics and a polynomial method argument. To prove the exact bound m_d = 1/2, one must close the O(1/d) gap. A potential strategy: (1) characterize the near-extremal sets more precisely using the spherical harmonic analysis already developed, (2) show that any set exceeding measure 1/2 + ε must have structural properties forcing it to contain a zero-sum triple, possibly by developing a spherical analogue of the slice-rank/polynomial method that yields exact rather than asymptotic bounds, or (3) establish a stability result showing near-hemisphere sets must be close to hemispheres, then use this rigidity to exclude the O(1/d) excess.
title: Bukh's Exact Zero-Sum-Free Density Conjecture

description: For any positive integer k and any completely multiplicative function f : ℕ → μ_k (the k-th roots of unity), and any ω in the image of f, there exists a Pythagorean triple (x, y, z) with f(x) = f(y) = f(z) = ω. This extends the paper's main result, which establishes the case ω = 1 via approximate concentration (for ε small enough, the values are forced to equal 1 since μ_k is discrete). The case of general ω does not reduce to ω = 1 by a simple substitution, as f(n)/ω is not completely multiplicative, making this a genuinely stronger statement that implies every color class of a completely multiplicative k-coloring of ℕ contains a Pythagorean triple.
proof_strategy: The ω = 1 case follows from the paper's vanishing-averages/pretentious-function decomposition. For general ω, one might try: (1) construct a modified multiplicative function g related to f and ω whose level set at 1 corresponds to f's level set at ω, then apply the paper's machinery to g — but g(n) = f(n)·ω^{-v(n)} for suitable v is not completely multiplicative; (2) use the dilation structure: if (a,b,c) is a Pythagorean triple with f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=1, then for any prime p with f(p)=ω, the dilated triple (pa,pb,pc) gives f(pa)=ω·f(a)=ω, etc., but this requires f(a)=1 which is circular; (3) develop a new transference principle that works for arbitrary level sets, not just neighborhoods of 1.
title: Monochromatic Pythagorean Triples in Every Level Set of Completely Multiplicative Functions

description: For finite simple graphs G and H on disjoint vertex sets, the matching number of their join G∗H satisfies ν(G∗H) = min(ν(G) + |V(H)|, ν(H) + |V(G)|, ⌊(|V(G)| + |V(H)|)/2⌋). This is the foundational combinatorial theorem of the paper, proved via the Tutte-Berge formula, and underpins all subsequent results on squarefree powers of edge ideals of wheel, fan, and friendship graphs.
domain_bridges: extremal graph theory → commutative algebra of monomial ideals
proof_strategy: Instantiate the Tutte-Berge formula ν(X) = (|V(X)| - max_{S⊆V(X)}(o(X-S) - |S|))/2 for the join graph X = G∗H. Classify subsets S ⊆ V(G∗H) by their intersections S_G = S ∩ V(G) and S_H = S ∩ V(H). The key observation is that every vertex of V(H) not in S is adjacent to every vertex of V(G) not in S_G, so odd components of (G∗H) - S arise only from odd components of G - S_G together with the complete bipartite structure of the join. Derive that o(G∗H - S) = o(G - S_G) + o(H - S_H) when both S_G and S_H are nonempty, with boundary cases when one side is empty. Optimize over all S to obtain the min-expression.
title: Matching Number of Arbitrary Graph Joins

description: For a p-adic field F and a generic representation π of GL_r(F), the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Jacquet–Shalika local functional equation coincides with the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Langlands–Shahidi method: ε^{JS}(π, ∧², ψ) = ε^{Sh}(π, ∧², ψ). This is the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) of the paper. Formalizing it requires developing the theories of generic representations of GL_r over p-adic fields, both integral-representation (Jacquet–Shalika) and Langlands–Shahidi constructions of L- and ε-factors, and the local functional equation for the Jacquet–Shalika exterior square integrals.
proof_strategy: The original proof uses global methods: (1) construct a global automorphic representation whose local component at a designated p-adic place v is the given π, (2) exploit the equality of global ε-factors computed via both methods (using the global functional equation and the theory of global integrals), and (3) deduce the local equality by comparing local factors at all places, invoking the archimedean result of Jiang–Liu–Sun–Tian and the known equality ε^{Sh} = ε^{Gal} from Cogdell–Shahidi–Tsai. A formalization would need to first develop the local theories (Jacquet–Shalika integrals, Langlands–Shahidi L-functions, local ε-factors) and then formalize the globalization argument.
title: Equality of Jacquet–Shalika and Langlands–Shahidi exterior square ε-factors for GL_n over p-adic fields

description: For a cocompact Fuchsian group Γ with signature (g; m₁, …, mₛ) where g ≥ 2 (allowing elliptic elements, so the quotient H/Γ is a hyperbolic orbifold rather than a surface), a Γ-gain graph (G, ψ) is Γ-isostatic in the hyperbolic plane H if and only if it satisfies the (2, 3, 1+s, 0)-gain tightness condition. This extends the paper's main theorem from surface groups (s=0, yielding (2,3,1,0)-gain tightness) to general cocompact Fuchsian groups, predicting that each elliptic generator shifts the sparsity parameter by one.
proof_strategy: Extend the orbit rigidity matrix construction to Fuchsian groups with elliptic elements. Analyze how elliptic fixed points in the fundamental domain modify the dimension count for symmetry-preserving infinitesimal motions—each elliptic generator of order mᵢ should contribute an additional constraint at the corresponding cone point of the orbifold, shifting the effective sparsity parameter from 1 to 1+s. Verify the matroidal exchange axiom for the modified (2,3,1+s,0)-gain tight gain graphs, then prove the rank of the orbit rigidity matrix equals the rank of the gain sparsity matroid via an inductive Henneberg-type construction.
title: Orbifold Rigidity Characterization for Fuchsian Groups with Torsion

description: For a stable range dual pair (G', G) with G the smaller compact member (excluding (O_{2n,2n}, Sp_{2n})), every irreducible unitary representation π of G has a nonzero theta lift θ(π) that is also an irreducible unitary representation of G'. This is the compact-group specialization of Li's theorem (Theorem 2.2 in the paper), where the convergence and non-negativity of the Li form (Eq. 2) are automatic, yielding a clean statement: the full unitary dual of G embeds into the unitary dual of G' via theta correspondence.
proof_strategy: Formalize the Li form on S(U) ⊗ V_π^∞ for compact G, prove convergence via compactness (continuous integrand on compact domain), establish G'-invariance and non-negativity, show L(π) ≠ 0 using the stable range isotropic subspace dimension condition, then invoke the algebraic characterization of theta lift as maximal semisimple quotient of big theta lift (Proposition 2.1) to conclude L(π) ≅ θ(π*).
title: Stable range theta lift preserves unitarity for compact smaller groups

description: For any natural numbers n, l, r such that n >= (l+1)*r + l, there exists an interval packing of maximum possible size (n choose l) in the Boolean lattice restricted to levels l through l+r. This can be formulated as the existence of a function f mapping each l-sized subset T of [n] to an r-sized subset C_T disjoint from T, such that for any distinct l-sized subsets T1, T2, T1 is not contained in T2 union C_T2 and T2 is not contained in T1 union C_T1.
proof_strategy: Define the explicit construction of the function f mapping each l-set T to an r-set C_T using the cyclic sequence method described in the paper. Subsequently, prove that the resulting intervals [T, T ∪ C_T] are pairwise disjoint by showing that for any two distinct l-sets T1, T2, neither T1 ⊆ T2 ∪ C_{T2} nor T2 ⊆ T1 ∪ C_{T1} holds.
title: Engel's Interval Packing Theorem

description: For any field K with char(K) ≠ 2 and quadratic polynomials v, w ∈ K[x], the classical Wronskian v'w - vw' is exactly equal to the derivative-free Remainder-Polynomial Route (RPR) formulation. Specifically, v'w - vw' = 2x · Sres₁(v, w) + (v₁w - w₁v), where Sres₁(v,w) = v₂w - w₂v is the first subresultant of v and w, and vᵢ, wᵢ are the coefficients of xⁱ in v, w respectively. This identity generalizes symmetrically to the full Richelot triple (U, V, W), proving that RPR yields identical codomain polynomials not merely up to scalar units, but as an exact polynomial equality.
proof_strategy: Expand both sides of the identity v'w - vw' = 2x(v₂w - w₂v) + (v₁w - w₁v) using the standard definition of the formal derivative v' = 2v₂x + v₁. Distributing the terms on the right-hand side and collecting coefficients of x², x, and 1 directly yields the expanded left-hand side, (v₂w₁ - v₁w₂)x² + 2(v₂w₀ - v₀w₂)x + (v₁w₀ - v₀w₁), proving the exact polynomial equality purely through algebraic manipulation without relying on scalar units or characteristic restrictions beyond char(K) ≠ 2.
title: Exact Identity of Wronskian and Subresultant Richelot Formulations

description: For any generalized star configuration ideal I of height h defined by n ≥ h+1 forms f₁,…,fₙ in a polynomial ring over a field, where any h of the forms constitute a regular sequence, the standard Veronese degree svd(I) equals lcm(1, 2, …, h). This extends the paper's main theorem for monomial star configurations to the generalized setting, predicting that the Veronese degree depends only on h, not on the specific choice of forms or the ambient polynomial ring.
proof_strategy: First formalize the monomial star configuration result svd(I_{n,h}) = lcm(1,…,h) using the Diophantine condition M framework. Then extend to generalized star configurations by showing the Diophantine structure governing symbolic powers is invariant under regular sequences of forms—potentially via initial ideal arguments preserving svd, or by establishing that the symbolic Rees algebra of a generalized star configuration has the same Veronese structure as its monomial specialization.
title: Standard Veronese Degree of Generalized Star Configurations Equals lcm(1,…,h)

description: For any non-degenerate homogeneous quadratic form Q in 3 variables over ℤ whose zero set in ℙ²(ℚ) is nonempty, the dynamical system on [0,1] constructed by applying Romik's stereographic projection method to the Berggren tree of Q is ergodic and conservative with respect to its absolutely continuous invariant measure obtained via Keane's adaptation.
proof_strategy: For each quadratic form Q, construct the Romik-type map T_Q as a piecewise fractional linear transformation on [0,1] derived from the Berggren matrices. Show T_Q admits a Markov partition with the Gibbs-Markov property. Compute the invariant density using Keane's method (tracking how the quadratic form coefficients transform under the Berggren matrices). Apply the Hopf argument adapted to infinite measure spaces to establish ergodicity, and verify conservativity via the ratio ergodic theorem by checking integrability of the density against the return time function.
title: Ergodicity of Dynamical Systems Induced from Berggren Trees
