description: For any simple graph G with n vertices and m edges, and for any 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues s_k(G) equals m + binom(k+1, 2) if and only if G is a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
proof_strategy: Reduce the problem to the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem, which states s_k(G) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^k d_i^*(G) where d* is the conjugate degree sequence. Show that equality in Brouwer's bound implies equality in Grone-Merris-Bai, forcing the degree sequence to match the Laplacian eigenvalue sequence. Use the characterization of threshold graphs via their degree sequences and the specific sum m + binom(k+1, 2) to conclude that G must be a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
title: Full Brouwer's Laplacian Conjecture Equality Characterization

description: Every non-trivial 2-(v,k,λ) design admitting a flag-transitive automorphism group with socle PSL(2,q) (where q = p^f ≥ 4) that acts point-imprimitively on the design must satisfy v ∈ {15, 36, 85}, corresponding to exactly three isomorphism classes: the complementary design of PG(3,2), the complementary design of PG(3,4), and the Devillers–Praeger 2-(36,8,4) design. This captures the complete point-imprimitive classification proven in the paper and requires substantial design-theoretic and group-theoretic infrastructure to formalize.
proof_strategy: 1) Formalize 2-designs, automorphism groups, flag-transitivity, and point-imprimitivity in Lean. 2) Develop the subgroup structure of PSL(2,q) — specifically the classification of maximal subgroups (dihedral, parabolic, A4, S4, A5 subgroups). 3) Use the imprimitivity assumption to decompose the point set into blocks of imprimitivity, constraining v via the subgroup lattice. 4) Apply combinatorial parameter constraints (Fisher's inequality, divisibility relations r(k-1) = λ(v-1), bk = vr) together with the orbit-stabilizer theorem under PSL(2,q). 5) Case analysis on the possible systems of imprimitivity yields only v = 15, 36, 85.
title: Point-Imprimitive 2-Designs with PSL(2,q) Socle Have Bounded Point Counts

description: The number of lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n equals the product over all 1 ≤ a < b ≤ 3n+2 with (a,b) ≠ (n+1,2n+2) of |1 + ζ^a + ζ^b|^(1/3), where ζ = exp(2πi/(3n+3)).
proof_strategy: Define the region T_n and its dual graph G_n. Define the bipartite adjacency matrix M_n of G_n. Prove that the number of perfect matchings of G_n equals the absolute value of the determinant of M_n. Diagonalize M_n to compute its determinant, and verify that the resulting expression matches the given product formula.
title: Exact Enumeration of Lozenge Tilings of Triangular Regions

description: The maximum number of arcs in a loopless digraph on n vertices (allowing anti-parallel arcs) without a directed triangle is floor(n^2/2). This is the key combinatorial lemma (Theorem 1.1) from the paper, which bypasses the measure-theoretic difficulties of Bukh's original conjecture while capturing the core extremal insight.
proof_strategy: Define the in-degree and out-degree of vertices. Prove that for any arc x -> y, the in-neighbors of x and out-neighbors of y are disjoint, hence in-deg(x) + out-deg(y) <= n. Sum over all arcs to get 2 * sum(d^+ * d^-) <= |E| * n. Apply Cauchy-Schwarz on the sum of total degrees squared to relate 4|E|^2 / n to 2|E|^2 / n + |E| n, and solve the quadratic inequality to conclude |E| <= n^2 / 2.
title: Directed Mantel's Theorem for Loopless Digraphs

description: For every number field K with ring of integers O_K, and every effective divisor D on the open unit disk 𝔻, there exists a holomorphic function f on 𝔻 whose Taylor coefficients all lie in O_K (viewed as a subring of ℂ via a fixed embedding σ : K ↪ ℂ) and whose zero divisor is exactly D. This directly generalizes the paper's Theorem 2.1 (the Gaussian-integer case O_K = ℤ[i]) to arbitrary rings of integers. The paper's proof for ℤ[i] exploits the Euclidean domain structure for an inductive rounding scheme; for general O_K, the full-rank lattice structure O_K ≅ ℤ^n should permit analogous nearest-lattice-point rounding within the jet-correction framework, but the non-uniqueness of rounding in non-Euclidean rings introduces subtleties that require new arguments.
domain_bridges: Complex analysis ↔ Algebraic number theory (holomorphic functions with algebraic integer coefficients)
Commutative algebra ↔ Complex analysis (divisor theory in restricted coefficient rings)
Diophantine approximation ↔ Complex analysis (lattice rounding in jet-correction schemes)
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's modified Weierstrass product with jet-correction operators. Step 1: Construct one-parameter deformations of Weierstrass elementary factors whose Taylor coefficients lie in O_K and which act as jet-correction operators preserving coefficients up to degree n while shifting the (n+1)-th coefficient by a controlled O_K-valued affine amount. Step 2: Since O_K ≅ ℤ^n as a ℤ-module, use nearest-lattice-point rounding (via the Minkowski theorem or LLL-type estimates) in place of the coordinate-wise rounding used for ℤ[i] ≅ ℤ². Step 3: Verify that the triangular structure of the coefficient map and the convergence bounds from canonical-product theory carry through unchanged, since the lattice rounding errors are bounded by the covering radius of O_K.
title: General Ring of Integers Divisor Realization on the Unit Disk

description: For the symmetric group S_n with Coxeter number h=n, the reduced homology H̃_{n-2}(Δ(CPF_n)) of the cluster parking function complex, tensored with the sign character ε of the dihedral group I_2(n+2), is isomorphic as a representation of I_2(n+2) × S_n to the diagonal coinvariant ring DR_n = ℂ[x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_n]/(e_1,...,e_n), where e_i are the elementary symmetric polynomials in x and y separately. This is equivalent to a dihedral sieving phenomenon on cluster parking functions.
proof_strategy: Define the cluster parking function complex and its dihedral automorphism group generated by R and S satisfying R^{n+2} = (RS)^2 = S^2 = 1. Compute the character of the reduced homology under the combined I_2(n+2) × S_n action. On the other side, leverage Haiman's n! theorem for the diagonal coinvariant character. Verify that the sign twist ε aligns the dihedral group characters, and check that the S_n-characters match via the parking function area/bounce statistics that index the bigraded Frobenius character.
title: Dihedral-Coinvariant Isomorphism for Cluster Parking Function Homology

description: In the extended quasi-shuffle algebra E on (Z, +), the p-th quasi-shuffle power of the generator z_0 satisfies z_0^{*p} = Σ_{k=0}^{p} S(p,k) · k! · z_0^k, where S(p,k) is the Stirling number of the second kind. The idempotent merge property z_0 ⊕ z_0 = z_0 (since 0+0=0) makes this the natural quasi-shuffle analogue of the classical identity x^p = Σ_k S(p,k) · k! · (x choose k), and it underpins the systematic summation of harmonic number powers via evaluation at truncated MZV maps ζ_n(z_0^j) = C(n,j).
proof_strategy: Define the quasi-shuffle product recursively on words via aw * bv = a(w * bv) + b(aw * v) + (a ⊕ b)(w * v) with a ⊕ b = z_{i+j} for letters z_i, z_j. Establish that z_0 is merge-idempotent (z_0 ⊕ z_0 = z_0). Prove by induction on p: base case p=0 is trivial (1 = 1); inductive step multiplies both sides by z_0, applies the quasi-shuffle recursion to get z_0^{*(p+1)} = Σ_k S(p,k)·k!·((k+1)z_0^{k+1} + k·z_0^k), then reindexes and applies the Stirling recurrence S(p+1,k) = S(p,k-1) + k·S(p,k) to close the induction.
title: Stirling Number Formula for Quasi-Shuffle Powers of Zero in the Extended Quasi-Symmetric Algebra

description: The paper establishes that f(a,k) = Θ(a + k + ak/log(k+2)), where f(a,k) is the minimum degree threshold forcing k edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in graphs with bipartite-hole number at most a. This conjecture proposes that the implicit constant in the upper bound can be taken to be 2, i.e., f(a,k) ≤ 2a + 2k + ⌈2ak / log(k+2)⌉ for all integers a,k ≥ 2. This would make the asymptotic result fully explicit and represents a natural strengthening of the paper's greedy-packing upper bound argument.
proof_strategy: Formalize the bipartite-hole deletion lemma and the McDiarmid-Yolov Hamiltonicity theorem as intermediate results, then construct the greedy packing argument with explicit bookkeeping of degree deficits at each stage. The key is tracking how the bipartite-hole number and minimum degree evolve after deleting each Hamilton cycle, showing the deficit is bounded by a factor of 2 times the target expression.
title: Explicit constant for bipartite-hole Hamilton cycle packing upper bound

description: For any prime power q, positive integer t, subgroup A of index r > 1 in (F_q, +), and (v,k,λ) difference set D in the quotient group F_q^+/A, the graph Γ_D(2t,q,A,r) with vertex set (F_q^+/A) × V where V is a 2t-dimensional symplectic space over F_q, and adjacency (ᾱ,x) ~ (β̄,y) iff B(x,y) ∈ ᾱ - β̄ + D (viewed in F_q^+/A), is a divisible design graph with parameters (n, K, λ₁, λ₂) computable from (q, t, r, k, λ). Moreover, when q = 2^s, this graph is a Cayley graph over the elementary abelian 2-group (Z/2Z)^{2st + log₂(r)}. This extends the known result that complements of symplectic covers (using subgroups A) are divisible design graphs to the case where A is replaced by a difference set.
domain_bridges: Difference sets in finite abelian groups
Cayley graphs of elementary abelian groups
proof_strategy: Adapt the proof that complements of symplectic covers are divisible design graphs (Corollary 2.2 in the paper). Key steps: (1) Establish regularity by counting neighbors using difference set properties: the number of neighbors of a vertex depends on whether the difference set condition is satisfied, leveraging the identity D*D^{-1} = k·{e} + λ·(G\{e}). (2) Partition vertices into classes based on the second coordinate and compute common neighbors for same-class and different-class vertex pairs using symplectic form properties and difference set parameters. (3) For characteristic 2, note that F_q^+ with q=2^s is an elementary abelian 2-group, so the vertex set inherits this structure, and verify translation-invariance of adjacency.
title: Symplectic cover graphs with difference set parameters are divisible design graphs

description: Let z and X be indeterminates. Define the two polynomials in t: f(t) = z(t+256)^3 - 1728t^2 and g(t) = X(t+64)^2 - 256t, viewed as elements of (Z[z,X])[t]. Define the bridge polynomial Φ(z,X) = 729z²X³ + 3888z²X² + 6912z²X + 4096z² - 1458zX³ + 22356zX² - 27648zX + 729X³. Then the resultant of f and g with respect to t equals 2^36 · Φ(z,X). This identity is the algebraic backbone of the paper, establishing the explicit polynomial relation between the level-one j-invariant parameter z = 1728/j and the Fricke parameter X = 256t/(t+64)², and is verified by a direct resultant computation.
proof_strategy: The proof is a direct computation. Formalize polynomials f and g in MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ adjoined with a variable t, compute the resultant with respect to t using the Sylvester matrix determinant (already available in Mathlib's Polynomial.resultant), and verify the result equals 2^36 · Φ(z,X). The entire verification reduces to polynomial arithmetic over ℤ[z,X,t], which is decidable and computationally feasible.
title: Fricke Bridge Resultant Identity

catalog_references: The Left-Regular Stabilizer of Zaks' Hamiltonian Cycle in the Pancake Graph
description: Let G be a finite group and let σ be a cyclic permutation of G representing a directed Hamiltonian cycle. If left translations by a and b both preserve the undirected cycle (i.e., L_a ∘ σ ∘ L_a^{-1} ∈ {σ, σ^{-1}} and L_b ∘ σ ∘ L_b^{-1} ∈ {σ, σ^{-1}}), and the order of a is at least 3, then b conjugates a to either a or a^{-1} (i.e., b * a * b^{-1} ∈ {a, a^{-1}}).
proof_strategy: Translate the preservation of the undirected Hamiltonian cycle into the condition that left translations conjugate the cyclic permutation σ to either σ or σ^{-1}. Analyze the relation between a and b by evaluating the conjugation relations on the elements of G, using the fact that σ is a full cycle and the order of a is ≥ 3 to restrict the possible conjugation actions of b on a.
title: Cyclic-Order Rigidity for Hamiltonian Cycles in Finite Groups

description: The paper establishes a directed analogue of the Bonnet-Myers theorem: for a strongly connected, r-regular simple digraph G with in-curvature κ⁻(v) ≥ κ₀ > 0 at every vertex, the directed diameter is bounded above by 2r/κ₀. The natural rigidity conjecture is that equality in this bound forces G to be a directed cycle. Specifically, if G is a strongly connected, r-regular simple digraph with in-curvature κ⁻(v) ≥ κ₀ > 0 for all v, and the directed diameter satisfies ⟶diam(G) = 2r/κ₀, then G is isomorphic to a directed cycle C_n (where n = 2r/κ₀ + 1). This mirrors Obata's rigidity theorem for the classical Lichnerowicz inequality and would complete the directed Bonnet-Myers picture.
proof_strategy: Adapt Obata's rigidity argument from Riemannian geometry: (1) Formalize the directed Bonnet-Myers inequality from the paper in Lean, establishing the diameter bound. (2) Analyze the equality case by studying the structure of shortest directed paths achieving maximum distance. (3) Show that equality forces every vertex to lie on a unique longest directed geodesic, and that the out-neighborhood structure is rigid enough to force the directed cycle topology. (4) Use the permutation relation between in- and out-curvature (Theorem from the paper) to constrain the local structure at extremal vertices. (5) The key technical step is proving that any deviation from the directed cycle structure strictly increases the effective resistance / decreases curvature below κ₀, contradicting the equality assumption.
title: Directed Bonnet-Myers Rigidity: Equality Characterizes Directed Cycles

description: There exists a constant δ > 0 such that for every n ≥ 2, there exists a set P ⊂ ℝ² with |P| = n containing a distance occurring at least n^(1+δ) times. This is the core quantitative claim of the paper, establishing that the Minkowski grid construction yields a polynomial improvement over the trivial n bound for distance multiplicity, thereby disproving Erdős's unit distance conjecture.
proof_strategy: The proof requires constructing the Minkowski grid from a number field of high degree (vertical amplification of the Ramanujan estimate), showing the resulting point set has the claimed distance multiplicity. A Lean formalization would need: (1) the Croot-Mao-Pohoata-Sheffer-Yip robust Ramanujan lower bound for r_2(m), (2) the construction of the Minkowski grid P_n from an appropriate number field, (3) a counting argument bounding the maximum distance multiplicity from below by n^(1+δ). The number-theoretic ingredient about representations as sums of two squares in number fields is the key bridge.
title: Polynomially superlinear distance multiplicity in finite planar point sets

description: For every integer r ≥ 2 and ε > 0, there exists Δ₀ such that any uncrowded (r+1)-uniform hypergraph with maximum degree Δ ≥ Δ₀ has list chromatic number at most (1+ε)(Δ / log Δ)^{1/r}. This improves the leading constant from r^{1/r} (achieved in the paper) to 1, which would be asymptotically tight with the random hypergraph lower bound.
proof_strategy: Refine the semi-random nibble process and Rosenfeld-style counting argument to eliminate the r^{1/r} factor. This could potentially be achieved by tightening the analysis of the binomial degree bounds and active edge-color constraints, ensuring the residual sizes are controlled with an optimal multiplicative factor.
title: Optimal Constant Conjecture for Uncrowded Hypergraph List Coloring

description: The paper proves that the list chromatic number of an uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraph of maximum degree $\Delta$ is at most $(1+o(1))(r\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$. We conjecture that the constant factor $r$ inside the $1/r$-th power can be replaced by 1, yielding a tight upper bound of $(1+o(1))(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$. This would match the known asymptotic behavior of the chromatic number of random uncrowded hypergraphs and parallel the $r=1$ case (triangle-free graphs) where the bound $(1+o(1))\Delta/\log\Delta$ is optimal. The factor $r$ in the current bound arises from tracking active edge-color constraints in the semi-random nibble; removing it likely requires bypassing this $r$-fold residual degree inflation.
proof_strategy: Develop an entropy-increment-based list-coloring algorithm or a more refined nibble that tracks residual hypergraph degrees directly, avoiding the $r$-fold inflation from active edge-color constraints. An alternative approach could involve proving a tight lower bound on the independence number and applying a randomized coloring strategy that matches this bound.
title: Optimality of the Leading Constant in Uncrowded Hypergraph List Coloring

description: For every integer d ≥ 2, if p ∈ ℂ[s] is a nonzero balanced polynomial (satisfying p(s) = ω·conj(p(−conj(s))) for some |ω| = 1) whose zeros all lie in the region Ω_d = {a+ib : a² − b²/(d−1) ≤ d/4}, then the centered binomial sample B_d[p](z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j)·p(j−d/2)·z^j has all its zeros on the unit circle. Furthermore, Ω_d is the maximal reflection-invariant set with this property: for any reflection-invariant S ⊋ Ω_d, there exists a balanced polynomial with zeros in S whose binomial sample has a zero off the unit circle. This is the polynomial case of the paper's main sampling theorem, which then drives the derivative-period-polynomial unit-circle theorem for L-functions of newforms.
domain_bridges: Sampling theory → Zero distribution of L-functions
proof_strategy: Factor the balanced polynomial into reflected zero pairs {ρ, −ρ̄} and purely imaginary fixed zeros. Reduce to the single-pair case p_ρ(s) = (s−ρ)(s+ρ̄) via multiplicativity of the balanced condition under binomial sampling. For single pairs, apply projective Hermite–Kakeya–Obreschkoff theory to classify when B_d[p_ρ] has all zeros on 𝕋: the admissible region boundary is precisely the hyperbola a² − b²/(d−1) = d/4. De Bruijn strip contraction controls zero variation under parameter perturbation. Maximality follows from explicit counterexamples at boundary points of Ω_d.
title: Sharp Circular Sampling for Balanced Polynomials

description: For an elliptic curve E over Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free conductor, if the mu-invariant of its sharp/flat 2-adic L-function vanishes, then the lambda-invariant of the quadratic twist E^D (for square-free D > 0 with D ≡ 1 mod 4) differs from that of E by an explicit sum over the prime factors of D involving the 2-adic valuation of (ℓ^2 - 1)/8 and the parity of the number of points on E modulo ℓ.
proof_strategy: Decompose the variation of the sharp/flat 2-adic L-functions under quadratic twists by analyzing their interpolation properties and the local Euler factors at primes dividing D. Compare the resulting power series to deduce the difference in their Iwasawa invariants, adapting Matsuno's ordinary case methodology to the supersingular setting via Sprung's logarithmic matrices.
title: Supersingular Iwasawa Lambda Invariant Difference Formula

description: The paper proves that the count N(x) of odd integers up to x not representable as p+2^a+2^b is at least x * exp(-(4+η) * (logloglogx / loglogx) * logx). This conjecture posits that the constant 4 in the exponent is an artifact of the Fermat number construction and can be replaced by any arbitrarily small epsilon > 0, yielding a lower bound of x * exp(-ε * (logloglogx / loglogx) * logx). This would substantially bridge the gap to Erdős's grand challenge conjecture that N(x) > c_0 * x for some constant c_0 > 0.
proof_strategy: Improve the covering congruence system construction by replacing the reliance on Fermat numbers with a more general system of cyclotomic polynomials or finding a denser set of congruences that reduces the multiplicative constant penalty from 4 to an arbitrarily small epsilon.
title: Epsilon-Constant Reduction for Odd Integers Not of the Form p+2^a+2^b

description: Any non-trivial point-imprimitive 2-(v,k,λ) design admitting a flag-transitive automorphism group with socle PSL(2,q) (where q=p^f≥4) must have design parameters (v,k,λ) belonging to the finite set {(15,12,11), (85,80,79), (36,8,4)}, corresponding to the complements of PG(3,2), PG(3,4), and the Devillers-Praeger 2-(36,8,4) design, respectively.
proof_strategy: Define 2-designs, flag-transitive actions, point-imprimitive actions, and group socles in Lean. Translate the group-theoretic constraints (specifically the orbit structures of PSL(2,q)) and combinatorial design parameters to computationally eliminate all possible parameter sets except the three identified triples.
title: Point-Imprimitive Flag-Transitive 2-Design Parameter Classification

catalog_references: Exact enumeration of lozenge tilings of a triangular region
description: The paper gives an exact product formula for the number of lozenge tilings T_n of a triangular region T_n involving complex roots of unity: T_n = ∏_{1≤a<b≤3n+2, (a,b)≠(n+1,2n+2)} |1+ζ^a+ζ^b|^{1/3} with ζ = e^{2πi/(3n+3)}. This conjecture states that this complicated product simplifies to a product of binomial coefficients: T_n = ∏_{k=1}^n (3k-1 choose k). This is a precise, falsifiable identity that can be checked for small n and would provide a much simpler closed form.
proof_strategy: The paper reduces T_n to the determinant of a bipartite adjacency matrix M_n and diagonalizes it. The eigenvalues are the factors |1+ζ^a+ζ^b|. One could attempt to simplify the product of these eigenvalues using trigonometric identities and known product formulas for binomial coefficients. Alternatively, compute T_n for small n to guess the recurrence, then prove the recurrence holds for the binomial product and matches the determinant formula via creative telescoping or the holonomic systems approach.
title: Simplified binomial product formula for lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n

catalog_references: Győry bound on Thue inequality solutions
integral Hasse principle for binary forms
description: For each integer n ≥ 3, there exists a constant c_n > 0 independent of m such that, when primitive maximal binary forms of degree n are ordered by height, the proportion failing the integral Hasse principle simultaneously for every 1 ≤ h ≤ m is at least c_n. This strengthens the paper's Theorem 1, which guarantees a positive proportion depending on m, by asserting the proportion does not decay to zero as m → ∞.
proof_strategy: Extend the Akhtari–Bhargava construction by showing the proportion lower bound from Theorem 1 can be made independent of m. This requires analyzing how the local solvability conditions for F(x,y)=h across different h interact, and showing that a single congruence obstruction (e.g., modulo a fixed prime power) simultaneously blocks global solutions for all h while preserving local solvability, without the density cost growing with m.
title: Uniform Positive Density of Thue Forms Failing the Integral Hasse Principle for All Bounded h

description: For every finite tree T (viewed as a metric space with the shortest-path distance), the microscopic weighting assigns strictly positive weight to every vertex. The paper establishes that finite trees are of strictly negative type and hence admit a microscopic weighting, and that this weighting emphasizes boundary points and distributes mass widely. The open question is whether all vertex weights are necessarily positive — i.e., whether the signed measure is in fact a positive measure for trees. A counterexample would reveal a tree whose interior vertices receive negative microscopic weight, while a proof would show that the 'mass redistribution' from boundary emphasis never forces interior weights below zero.
proof_strategy: Exploit the energy minimization characterization: the microscopic weighting minimizes the energy integral E(w) = Σ w(x)w(y)d(x,y) over signed measures of total mass 1. For trees, the distance matrix has recursive structure amenable to leaf-removal induction. Show that any signed measure of mass 1 on a tree with a negative-weight vertex can be modified to decrease energy, contradicting optimality. Alternatively, use the Schoenberg embedding characterization: the microscopic weighting corresponds to the closest point to the origin in the affine hull of the embedded vertices, and for trees this convex hull might be shown to contain the origin's projection with all positive barycentric coordinates.
title: Positivity of Microscopic Weighting on Finite Trees

description: The infimum μ₂ over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of the ratio between the maximum and minimum portion (adjacent pair of slices) sizes equals 1+ρ, where ρ is the unique real root of ρ²+ρ³=1 in (0,1). The paper proves μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ ≈ 1.75488 and Korsky proved μ₂ ≥ 5/3 ≈ 1.66667, but the exact value remains open.
proof_strategy: The upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ follows from the paper's construction and Proposition 1 on cyclic factor avoidance. The lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1+ρ requires showing that no infinite sequence of cuts can achieve a ratio strictly less than 1+ρ. This likely requires analyzing the combinatorial constraints on infinite words over the alphabet {0,1,2,3} with ratios 1:ρ:ρ²:ρ³, proving that any such word avoiding equal adjacent letters must contain a portion with ratio at least (1+ρ)/(ρ²+ρ³) = 1+ρ. A potential approach uses the substitution system properties: the map sending 0↦23 (or 32), 1↦0, 2↦1, 3↦2 shows that any valid infinite sequence must eventually approximate the fixed point, forcing portions near the extremal ratio.
title: Optimality of the cake-cutting constant μ₂

description: For a complete multipartite graph G = K_{n_1,...,n_m} with n_1 ≤ ... ≤ n_m, the path-free complex PF_t(G) is vertex decomposable if and only if t ≥ 2n_{m-1} - 1. Equivalently, this is exactly the range where PF_t(G) is shellable and sequentially Cohen-Macaulay. For t ≤ 2n_{m-1} - 2, the complex fails to be sequentially Cohen-Macaulay.
proof_strategy: Formalize simplicial complexes and vertex decomposability in Lean, then define PF_t(G) as the simplicial complex of vertex subsets with no induced P_t. Define complete multipartite graphs and their part-size ordering. The forward direction (t ≥ 2n_{m-1}-1 ⟹ vertex decomposable) requires formalizing the explicit structural decomposition of PF_t(G) as a union of join complexes with a size-truncation term, then proving each join component is vertex decomposable and that the union preserves this property. The reverse direction (t ≤ 2n_{m-1}-2 ⟹ not sequentially Cohen-Macaulay) requires constructing a specific non-Cohen-Macaulay witness face or showing the homology fails the sequential Cohen-Macaulay condition, potentially via a Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence argument.
title: Vertex decomposability threshold for path-free complexes of complete multipartite graphs

description: The number of length-n quasinecklaces Q_k(n) is exactly k times the number of length-n necklaces N_k(n) for all k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: Demonstrate that each necklace corresponds to exactly k quasinecklaces via rotational symmetry or quasinecklace construction rules.
title: Proportionality of quasinecklaces to necklaces

description: Every exceptional rational function of degree 5 over F_q, where char(F_q) ∉ {2, 5}, is Möbius-equivalent to exactly one of four families: (1) the monomial X^5 (cyclic monodromy, single branch point), (2) a Rédei function of degree 5 (cyclic monodromy, two branch points), (3) a Dickson polynomial D_5(X, a) for some a ∈ F_q^× (dihedral monodromy with an F_q-rational branch point), or (4) a specific non-polynomial rational function arising from a rational 5-isogeny of an elliptic curve (dihedral monodromy without F_q-rational branch point). The monodromy group structure (cyclic vs. dihedral) and branch point rationality completely determine the function type.
proof_strategy: Formalize the key definitions: exceptional rational functions (permuting P^1(F_{q^m}) for infinitely many m via the Fried–Schur–Saxon criterion), Möbius equivalence, and arithmetic/geometric monodromy groups as permutation groups on 5 elements. Case-split by geometric monodromy group: cyclic case uses classification of transitive cyclic subgroups of S_5 with Riemann–Hurwitz constraining ramification to yield monomials and Rédei functions; dihedral case analyzes inertia subgroups of D_5 within S_5 and branch point rationality to derive Dickson polynomials and the elliptic isogeny family. Key intermediate lemma: for degree 5, the Riemann–Hurwitz formula restricts the possible ramification configurations to finitely many cases for each monodromy type.
title: Classification of Exceptional Rational Functions of Degree 5 over Finite Fields

description: For every doubly regular tournament T on n vertices (where n ≡ 3 mod 4, n ≥ 3), the metric dimension β(T) ≤ 2⌈log₂ n⌉. This extends the paper's O(log n) bound proven for certain doubly regular team tournaments to the classical and well-studied family of doubly regular tournaments, which are regular tournaments with parameters (n, (n-1)/2, (n-3)/4). The conjecture posits an explicit constant of 2, making it directly falsifiable by computing metric dimensions of small doubly regular tournaments (n = 3, 7, 11, 19, ...) and checking against the bound.
proof_strategy: Adapt Babai's probabilistic method as used in the paper: for a doubly regular tournament T, randomly sample k = 2⌈log₂ n⌉ vertices as a resolving set candidate. Compute the probability that two distinct vertices u, v receive the same distance vector from the sampled set. Use the strong regularity properties of doubly regular tournaments—specifically that every pair of vertices has exactly (n-3)/4 common out-neighbours—to bound the collision probability per pair by 1/2^k. Apply a union bound over all n(n-1)/2 pairs, choosing k so that the union bound is < 1, yielding a resolving set of size at most 2⌈log₂ n⌉.
title: Logarithmic metric dimension of doubly regular tournaments

description: The paper proves that for $k \ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a subset of the $n \times n$ grid with no $k+1$ collinear points is exactly $kn$. This conjecture posits that the condition 'sufficiently large $n$' can be relaxed to $n > k$, meaning $f_k(n) = kn$ holds for all $k \ge 3$ and $n > k$. This would unify the trivial case ($n \le k$, where $f_k(n) = n^2$) and the asymptotic regime.
proof_strategy: Either refine the probabilistic and pseudorandom hypergraph matching arguments to explicitly compute the threshold $N(k)$ and show it is $k+1$, or find a constructive algebraic or combinatorial proof that works uniformly for all $n > k$.
title: Exact Threshold for No-$(k+1)$-in-line Problem

description: For all natural numbers m, a, and d, the sum over all m-tuples (i_1, ..., i_m) of non-negative integers summing to d of the product of binomial coefficients ∏_{j=1}^{m} C(a + i_j, a) equals C(ma + d + m - 1, d). This generalizes the identity stated in the paper for m=3 (used to simplify the Bogart-Longyear formula for 3-row Latin rectangles), where the paper claims it is 'easily proved with dots and dividers.' The generalization connects directly to Gessel's framework through multisymmetric function generating series.
proof_strategy: Use generating functions: (1) establish that the ordinary generating function for C(a+i, a) is (1-x)^{-(a+1)} via the negative binomial theorem; (2) the product of m copies gives (1-x)^{-m(a+1)}, so the LHS is the coefficient of x^d; (3) extract the coefficient as C(m(a+1)+d-1, d) = C(ma+d+m-1, d). Alternatively, prove by induction on m using Vandermonde convolution as the inductive step, with the m=1 base case being trivial.
title: Generalized Multinomial Convolution Identity for Latin Rectangle Enumeration

description: There exists a constant δ > 0 such that for every n ≥ 2, there is a set P of n points in ℝ² where every subset A ⊆ P of size ≥ 2 contains a distance occurring at least ⌈|A|²/n^(1−δ)⌉ times as an ordered pair. This is the main theorem of the paper, establishing that Minkowski grids derived from number fields of high degree have robustly many repeated distances, vertically amplifying the Croot–Mao–Pohoata–Sheffer–Yip robust Ramanujan estimate for the ordinary square grid.
proof_strategy: Construct P as a Minkowski grid from a number field of degree d, where the norm form N(α) = αᾰ provides the multiplicative structure for vertical amplification of the 1D Ramanujan bound. The proof requires: (1) existence of number fields whose norms attain many representations as sums of two squares (leveraging the Ramanujan-type estimate max_{m≤x} r₂(m) ≥ exp(c·log x / log log x)), (2) embedding the ring of integers into ℝ² via the Minkowski map, and (3) applying the CMPSY combinatorial sieve to arbitrary subsets A ⊆ P, transferring the multiplicative structure of the norm to the 2D distance set. Formalization should proceed in three stages: first the Ramanujan bound on r₂, then the Minkowski grid construction with its norm-regularity properties, and finally the sieve argument yielding the robust bound for all subsets.
title: Minkowski Grid Robust Distance Multiplicity

description: For any finite metric space (X, d) of strictly negative type, the microscopic weighting exists and is the unique probability measure on X minimizing the energy functional E(μ) = ∑_{x,y ∈ X} d(x,y) · μ(x) · μ(y). This formalizes the paper's central characterization: the microscopic weighting, defined as the small-scale limit of magnitude weightings, coincides with the unique energy-minimizing probability measure on strictly negative-type spaces.
proof_strategy: First formalize strictly negative-type metric spaces and the magnitude weighting matrix Z(t) = [exp(-t·d(x_i,x_j))]. Define the microscopic weighting as the limit of weightings w(t) as t → 0⁺. Prove that on strictly negative-type spaces, the Schoenberg embedding yields a positive semidefinite structure ensuring the energy functional E(μ) = ∑ d(x,y)μ(x)μ(y) is strictly convex on the probability simplex. Show the microscopic weighting satisfies the optimality conditions (KKT) for this convex program, establishing both existence and uniqueness of the minimizer.
title: Energy Minimization Characterization of Microscopic Weighting on Negative-Type Spaces

description: The constant μ₂ is defined as the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of a unit circular cake of the supremum over n of the ratio (maximum portion size)/(minimum portion size) after n cuts, where a portion is an adjacent pair of slices. The paper proves μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ where ρ ≈ 0.75488 is the unique real root of ρ² + ρ³ = 1. The conjecture asserts this bound is tight: μ₂ = 1 + ρ, meaning no cutting strategy can achieve a worst-case portion ratio strictly below 1 + ρ. This would also establish μ₂ as irrational, since ρ is irrational.
proof_strategy: The upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ is proven constructively via a specific cutting algorithm and a word-avoidance argument over {0,1,2,3}. The lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1 + ρ remains wide open (only μ₂ ≥ 5/3 is known). A plausible approach: (1) Show that any infinite cutting sequence achieving ratio < 1 + ρ must, after sufficient normalization, produce slices whose sizes lie in ratios from {1, ρ, ρ², ρ³}, (2) Prove that the corresponding word over {0,1,2,3} must avoid all factors in the forbidden set A from Proposition O, (3) Show by combinatorial or automata-theoretic means that no infinite word cyclically avoiding A can have all adjacent-pair sums below 1 + ρ times the minimum adjacent-pair sum. Alternatively, a potential-function argument tracking the distribution of slice sizes could force a lower bound.
title: The optimal portion ratio μ₂ equals 1 + ρ

description: For a complete multipartite graph $K_{n_1, \dots, n_m}$ with $n_1 \le \dots \le n_m$ and $m \ge 2$, the $t$-path-free complex $\PF_t(K_{n_1, \dots, n_m})$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $t \ge 2n_{m-1} - 1$.
proof_strategy: First formalize abstract simplicial complexes, the $t$-path-free complex $\PF_t(G)$, and vertex decomposability in Lean. Then, formalize the structural decomposition of $\PF_t(G)$ as a union of join complexes. Establish that for $t \le 2n_{m-1} - 2$, the complex fails to be sequentially Cohen-Macaulay by analyzing the link of a specific face. Finally, prove vertex decomposability for $t \ge 2n_{m-1} - 1$ by explicitly constructing the shedding vertex sequence and applying the decomposition theorem.
title: Vertex Decomposability of Path-Free Complexes of Complete Multipartite Graphs

description: Among all non-trivial 2-(v,k,λ) designs admitting a flag-transitive automorphism group with socle PSL(2,q) that are not Witt-Bose-Shrikhande linear spaces, the maximum number of points is v=496, achieved uniquely (up to isomorphism) by the sporadic linear space with block size k=4 admitting PΓL(2,2⁵) as its flag-transitive automorphism group. This conjecture asserts that the missing example identified in this paper represents the extremal case among all sporadic such designs, and that the complete list of 48 sporadic examples attains no larger v.
proof_strategy: Verify the conjecture by exhaustive computation over the 48 sporadic examples classified in the paper, confirming that v=496 is maximal. Then establish that no further sporadic examples exist beyond those listed, leveraging the parameter bounds (v = (q+1)q(q-1)/m for appropriate divisors m) and the subgroup structure of PSL(2,q) acting on its subdegrees. The key step is proving that for q > 32, any point-primitive flag-transitive 2-design with socle PSL(2,q) that is not a WBS linear space must have v ≤ 256 or reduce to a previously enumerated case.
title: Maximality of the 496-point sporadic design among non-WBS flag-transitive designs with PSL(2,q) socle

description: Over a finite field F_q of characteristic not equal to 2 or 5, any exceptional rational function of degree 5 with cyclic monodromy is Möbius equivalent to either the monomial X^5 or a Rédei function R_5(X, a) for some a in F_q.
proof_strategy: Define exceptional rational functions, cyclic monodromy groups, and Rédei functions. Apply the Riemann-Hurwitz formula and analyze the ramification structure of the cover to show that the branch points and inertia groups restrict the function to the monomial or Rédei function equivalence classes.
title: Cyclic Monodromy Classification for Degree 5 Exceptional Rational Functions

description: For every fixed integer $r \geq 2$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $\Delta_0$ such that for all $\Delta \geq \Delta_0$, every uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has list chromatic number at most $(1+\varepsilon)(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$. This conjectures that the leading constant $r^{1/r}$ in the authors' theorem can be further improved to 1, matching the optimal asymptotic bound for $r=1$ (graphs) due to Molloy and the known lower bounds from random hypergraphs.
proof_strategy: Adapt the semi-random nibble method to maintain tighter control on the residual degrees and color lists, potentially using an improved differential equation analysis or a more refined counting argument for the final sparse stage to eliminate the factor of $r^{1/r}$.
title: Optimal leading constant for list coloring uncrowded hypergraphs

description: For an elliptic curve E over Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free conductor N_E, and a square-free integer D > 0 congruent to 1 mod 4, the difference between the sharp/flat 2-adic Iwasawa lambda-invariants of the quadratic twist E^D and E (assuming the mu-invariant is 0) is given by the sum over prime divisors ell of D of 2^{n_ell} (if ell divides N_E) or 2^{n_ell+1} (if ell does not divide N_E and 2 divides the order of E modulo ell), where n_ell is the 2-adic valuation of (ell^2 - 1)/8.
proof_strategy: Formalize quadratic twists of elliptic curves, the reduction of elliptic curves modulo primes, the order of the finite group of rational points, and the definition of Sprung's sharp/flat 2-adic L-functions. Then establish the explicit difference formula for the lambda-invariants by evaluating the sum over the prime divisors of D using the local properties of the 2-adic L-function under quadratic twists.
title: Matsuno-type Formula for Supersingular Iwasawa Lambda-Invariants

description: For any η > 0, there exists x₀(η) such that for all x ≥ x₀(η), the count N(x) of odd integers n ≤ x that cannot be written as p + 2^a + 2^b (with p prime and a,b ∈ ℕ) satisfies N(x) ≥ x · exp(-(4+η) · (log log log x / log log x) · log x). This improves Pan's exponent factor from (log log log log x)/(log log log x) to (log log log x)/(log log x), using a refined covering construction via Fermat numbers and Stewart's theorem on large prime divisors of cyclotomic values.
proof_strategy: Formalize N(x) as a counting function over odd n ≤ x excluding those with ∃p∈Primes, ∃a,b∈ℕ, n = p + 2^a + 2^b. The key construction uses Fermat numbers to restrict to pairs with b - a = t·2^m, then applies Stewart's theorem on prime divisors q_d | Φ_d(2) with ord_{q_d}(2) = d to build a covering system. The density bound follows from sieve-type estimates on the residue classes avoided by primes congruent to specific values modulo these primes q_d. The asymptotic exp factor arises from Mertens-type product estimates over the cyclotomic primes.
title: Asymptotic lower bound for odd integers not representable as p + 2^a + 2^b

catalog_references: Ciucu, A. & Krattenthaler, P. (2002). Lozenge tilings of a triangular region. arXiv:math/0206123.
Propp, J. (2002). The many faces of alternating-sign matrices. SIAM Review, 44(2), 323–343.
Kasteleyn, P. W. (1961). Graphs and simple pairwise interactions. Physica, 27, 1209‑1223.
Temperley, H. N. V., & Fisher, M. E. (1961). Dimer problem in statistical mechanics‑an exact result. Philosophical Magazine, 6(68), 1061‑1062.
MacMahon, A. M. (1978). Plane partitions. In Combinatorial Mathematics (pp. 199‑212). Springer.
description: We conjecture that for every positive integer n, the signed adjacency matrix M_n of the dual graph of the triangular region T_n has eigenvalues exactly π_k = 2 cos(π k/(3n+3)) for k = 1,2,…,3n+2, excluding k = n+1 and k = 2n+2. Consequently, the determinant of M_n (which counts lozenge tilings) equals the product ∏_{k∈S_n} π_k, matching the product formula proved in the paper.
proof_strategy: Apply discrete Fourier transform on the cyclic group ℤ_{3n+3} to diagonalize M_n. The eigenvectors are given by characters χ_j(v) = ζ^{jv} where ζ = e^{2πi/(3n+3)}. Computing M_n·χ_j yields eigenvalue π_j = ζ^a + ζ^b + ζ^{-a-b} for appropriate a,b, which simplifies to 2 cos(π j/(3n+3)). The exceptional pair (n+1,2n+2) corresponds to a zero eigenvalue, which is omitted from the spectrum. Hence the eigenvalues are exactly the claimed cosines, and the determinant matches the product formula.
title: Eigenvalue conjecture for the signed adjacency matrix M_n of the triangular region's dual graph

description: There exists a constant δ > 0 such that for every integer n ≥ 2, there exists a finite set P ⊂ ℝ² of n points where the most frequent nonzero distance occurs at least n^(1+δ) times among ordered pairs. This is the core quantitative claim of the paper: the Minkowski grid construction vertically amplifies the one-dimensional Ramanujan estimate for r₂ to produce point sets whose distance multiplicity is superlinear, thereby yielding counterexamples to Erdős's unit distance conjecture under scaling.
proof_strategy: Construct P as a Minkowski grid over a number field K/ℚ of degree d ≥ 2. Points lie in a scaled lattice derived from the ring of integers of K, so that squared distances correspond to values of the norm form N_{K/ℚ}. The Ramanujan estimate max_{m≤x} r_d(m) ≥ exp(c·log x / log log x) for the number of representations by the norm form, combined with the vertical amplification from dimension 1 to 2, yields the exponent gain δ = δ(d) > 0. The parameter δ arises from the interplay between the degree d and the pigeonhole-type averaging over the grid.
title: Superlinear distance multiplicity in Minkowski grids

description: For any finite subset X of ℝⁿ equipped with the Euclidean metric, the microscopic weighting μ exists and satisfies: μ(x) > 0 if and only if x is a vertex (extreme point) of conv(X), and μ(x) ≤ 0 for every non-extreme point of X. This formalizes the heuristic that the microscopic weighting emphasizes boundary points and assigns greater weight to outlying regions.
proof_strategy: First formalize the magnitude weighting w(t) as the solution to the linear system ∑_{y∈X} e^{-td(x,y)} w(y,t) = 1, then define the microscopic weighting as the limit μ(x) = lim_{t→∞} w(x,t). Use the Schoenberg embedding characterization for spaces of strictly negative type, and the energy integral optimization formulation. The sign characterization likely requires analyzing the variational problem: show that minimizing the energy forces positive mass onto extreme points (which are maximally spread) and non-positive mass onto interior points (which are redundant for energy minimization). For the converse direction (non-extreme points get non-positive weight), use the convex combination structure of interior points and the strict negativity of the kernel.
title: Sign Characterization of Microscopic Weighting on Euclidean Subsets

description: The paper proves that μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ, where μ₂ is the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of the supremum of the ratio of maximum to minimum portion (adjacent-pair) sizes, and ρ ≈ 0.75488 is the unique real root of x² + x³ = 1 in (0,1). Korsky proved μ₂ ≥ 5/3. The conjecture asserts that the paper's upper bound is tight: μ₂ = 1 + ρ. This would require showing that no cutting strategy can achieve a ratio strictly less than 1 + ρ in the limit, which likely demands a structural impossibility argument about the combinatorics of slice-size configurations.
proof_strategy: To prove μ₂ ≥ 1 + ρ, one must show that for any infinite cutting strategy and any ε > 0, there exists some n such that the ratio of maximum to minimum portion size after n cuts is at least 1 + ρ - ε. A possible approach: (1) characterize the set of achievable slice-size configurations as words over a finite alphabet of size classes, (2) show via a combinatorial/entropy argument that any long word avoiding the forbidden patterns from Proposition 2 must contain a factor whose portion ratio approaches 1 + ρ, or (3) use a potential function argument showing that any deviation from the ρ² : ρ³ splitting rule inevitably creates worse imbalances.
title: Tightness of the adjacent-pair cake-cutting bound: μ₂ = 1 + ρ

description: Erdős repeatedly asked whether there exists an absolute constant c_0 > 0 such that for all sufficiently large x, the number N(x) of odd integers n ≤ x which cannot be written as p + 2^a + 2^b (with p a prime and a, b natural numbers) satisfies N(x) > c_0 * x. This asserts that a positive proportion of odd integers are not of this form, upgrading the current x^{1-o(1)} lower bounds to a positive density.
proof_strategy: Establish that the set of odd integers not representable in this form has positive lower asymptotic density. This likely requires bypassing the exponential bounds produced by covering congruence systems, perhaps by demonstrating that a positive proportion of integers fall into residue classes that are fundamentally excluded by the structure of cyclotomic prime divisors, or by applying additive combinatorics to bound the density of the sumset.
title: Positive Lower Asymptotic Density of Odd Integers Not Representable as p + 2^a + 2^b

description: For every alphabet size k ≥ 2, the number Q_k(n) of length-n quasinecklaces over Σ_k is Θ(N_k(n)) as a function of n, meaning there exist constants c₁, c₂ > 0 depending only on k such that c₁ · N_k(n) ≤ Q_k(n) ≤ c₂ · N_k(n) for all n ≥ 1. This proportionality is the key property enabling constant-amortized-time generation of necklaces via quasinecklace filtering.
proof_strategy: First formalize the definitions: necklaces (words minimal among all rotations under lex order), Lyndon words (primitive necklaces), and quasinecklaces (the novel superset class from the paper). Then establish the containment necklace ⊆ quasinecklace. Derive or formalize the explicit formula for Q_k(n) and use the known necklace-counting formula N_k(n) = (1/n) Σ_{d|n} φ(d) k^{n/d} together with asymptotic estimates to show the ratio Q_k(n)/N_k(n) is bounded above and below by constants depending only on k.
title: Quasinecklace-Necklace Proportionality Bound

description: For every integer r ≥ 2 and real ε > 0, there exists Δ₀ such that for every (r+1)-uniform hypergraph H with girth at least 5 and maximum degree Δ ≥ Δ₀, the list chromatic number χ_ℓ(H) satisfies χ_ℓ(H) ≤ ⌈(1+ε)(rΔ / ln Δ)^(1/r)⌉. This conjecture formalizes the main theorem of the paper, improving Iliopoulos's bound of (1+o(1))r(Δ/ln Δ)^(1/r) by reducing the leading constant from r to r^(1/r) via a semi-random nibble argument combined with a Rosenfeld-style counting completion.
proof_strategy: Formalize the semi-random nibble in two phases: (1) define the nibble process on the hypergraph with active edge-color constraints, proving concentration of residual degrees via Chernoff-type binomial bounds (requiring Measure Theory / Probability bridges), (2) establish a sparse terminal state condition, (3) complete the coloring via a Rosenfeld-style counting argument (injection from list assignments to proper colorings). The girth ≥ 5 (uncrowded) hypothesis controls dependency structures and should be encoded as a locality condition on the hypergraph's Berge-cycle structure. Start with r = 2 (3-uniform case) to simplify the exponent.
title: List Chromatic Number Bound for Uncrowded Uniform Hypergraphs

description: For every primitive holomorphic newform f of weight k ≥ 4, level N, and nebentypus χ, and for every non-negative integer m, all zeros of the derivative period polynomial P⁽ᵐ⁾_f(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{k-2} C(k-2,j) · Λ⁽ᵐ⁾(f, j+1) · z^j lie on the unit circle, where Λ(f,s) denotes the completed L-function. This confirms and extends the Diamantis–Rolen conjecture to arbitrary level, nebentypus, and derivative order. The core mechanism is a sharp circular sampling theorem: for balanced polynomials p with zeros in Ω_d = {a+ib : a² − b²/(d−1) ≤ d/4}, the centered binomial sample B_d[p] has all zeros on the unit circle.
proof_strategy: Stage 1: Formalize the sharp circular sampling theorem for balanced polynomials — if p is balanced (p = ω·J(p) with |ω|=1, where J(F)(s) = conj(F(-conj(s)))) and Z(p) ⊆ Ω_{d,δ}, then all zeros of B_{d,δ}[p](z) = Σ C(d,j)·p(δ(j−d/2))·z^j lie on the unit circle, with Ω_{d,δ} maximal. Stage 2: Build completed L-function infrastructure for primitive holomorphic newforms, establishing the functional equation (supplying the balancing symmetry) and the Euler-product zero-free half-plane (placing reflected zeros in the required strip). Stage 3: Apply the sampling theorem with de Bruijn strip contraction and projective HKO theory to transport completed-zero geometry to derivative period polynomial circularity, simplicity, and strict interlacing.
title: Derivative Period Polynomial Unit-Circle Theorem for Primitive Holomorphic Newforms

description: For every elliptic curve E/Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free conductor, the sharp and flat μ-invariants of Sprung's 2-adic L-functions vanish: μ₂^♯(E,ωⁱ) = μ₂^♭(E,ωⁱ) = 0 for all i ∈ {0,1}. This is a 2-adic supersingular analogue of Greenberg's μ=0 conjecture. Its truth would render the λ-invariant difference formula in the paper unconditional, extending Matsuno-type formulas completely to the supersingular setting at p=2.
proof_strategy: Establish the vanishing of algebraic μ-invariants for the signed (♯/♭) Selmer groups via control theorems and the structure of torsion in Mordell–Weil groups over the cyclotomic Z₂-extension. Then invoke the Iwasawa main conjecture for supersingular primes (proved by Kobayashi, Sprung, etc.) to transfer vanishing from the algebraic to the analytic side. The supersingular condition at 2, combined with square-free conductor, constrains the 2-adic torsion structure sufficiently to force μ=0.
title: Vanishing of sharp/flat 2-adic μ-invariants for semistable supersingular elliptic curves

description: There exists a unique 2-(496, 4, 1) design (linear space) admitting a flag-transitive automorphism group with socle isomorphic to PSL(2, 32). This resolves the specific missing example in the 1990 classification of flag-transitive linear spaces by Buekenhout et al.
proof_strategy: Formalize the construction of the design from the coset action of PΓL(2, 2^5) on the normalizer of a dihedral subgroup of order 66 in PSL(2, 2^5). Then, prove that any 2-(496, 4, 1) design with a flag-transitive automorphism group having socle PSL(2, 32) must be isomorphic to this specific construction by analyzing the orbit structures and stabilizer chains.
title: Uniqueness of the 2-(496, 4, 1) Flag-Transitive Linear Space with Socle PSL(2, 32)

description: The supremum of achievable vertical amplification parameters δ in the paper's main theorem equals 1/3. Precisely: for every ε > 0, there exist infinitely many n ∈ ℕ and finite sets P ⊂ ℝ² with |P| = n such that for every A ⊆ P with |A| ≥ 2, the maximum distance multiplicity μ(A) ≥ |A|² / n^(2/3 + ε). This would be optimal given the O(n^{4/3}) Szemerédi–Trotter upper bound on unit distances, which forces δ ≤ 1/3. The paper establishes existence of some δ > 0; this conjectures δ can approach 1/3 via increasingly high-degree number field constructions.
proof_strategy: Extend the vertical amplification technique using number fields of degree d → ∞, combining the robust Ramanujan-type estimates from Croot-Mao-Pohoata-Sheffer-Yip with Minkowski lattice constructions from number fields with rich representations of integers as sums of squares. The key is to show that as the degree d grows, the amplification factor δ_d approaches 1/3, matching the Szemerédi–Trotter barrier. A potential approach involves cyclotomic fields or more general number fields where the class number and unit structure provide increasingly many representations.
title: Optimal Vertical Amplification Conjecture for Planar Point Sets

description: For any fixed integer $r \ge 2$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, every sufficiently large finite uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has list chromatic number at most $(1+\varepsilon)(r\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$. This captures the paper's main theorem, improving the leading constant from $r$ to $r^{1/r}$ over prior work by Iliopoulos.
proof_strategy: Formalize the semi-random list-coloring nibble method directly on the hypergraph, defining active edge-color constraints to track residual sizes. Establish a binomial degree bound to maintain invariants during the nibble phase, then apply a Rosenfeld-style counting argument to complete the coloring in the sparse terminal state.
title: Asymptotic List Chromatic Number of Uncrowded Uniform Hypergraphs

description: For every positive integer n, there exists a set of n points in ℝ² such that every subset of size at least 2 contains a distance occurring at least c|A|² / n^{1/2} times, where c is a positive constant.
proof_strategy: Adapt vertical amplification techniques from the Coot-Mao-Pohoata-Sheffer-Yip framework to achieve the 1/2 exponent in the bound.
title: Vertical Amplification of Repeated Distances with Exponent 1/2

description: Conjecture: Let ρ be the unique real root of x^2 + x^3 = 1 in (0,1). Define μ₂ as the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of a circular cake (as described in the paper) of the supremum over time of the ratio between the largest and smallest portion (adjacent pair of slices). Then μ₂ = 1+ρ.
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture, one would first establish the known upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ by exhibiting the specific cutting process given in the paper. For the lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1+ρ, one would analyze the combinatorial constraints on slice sizes imposed by the cutting rule and show that any infinite sequence must eventually produce a portion whose size ratio is at least 1+ρ. This can be approached by modeling the slice sizes as a multiplicative walk on the set {1, ρ, ρ², ρ³} and using a potential function or invariant derived from the forbidden factors in Proposition~O\\ref{propNoRepeat} to bound the frequency of large slices relative to small ones, ultimately yielding the desired ratio.
title: Optimality of the 1+ρ bound for the maximum-to-minimum portion ratio in the iterative cake-cutting process

description: We conjecture that there exists an absolute constant $c_0>0$ such that for all sufficiently large $x$, at least $c_0 x$ odd integers $\le x$ cannot be written as $p+2^a+2^b$ with $p$ prime and $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$. This asserts that the set of odd exceptions has positive lower asymptotic density, answering Erd\H os's open question.
proof_strategy: Construct a refined covering congruence system using Fermat numbers and large prime divisors of cyclotomic values to eliminate more residue classes, then combine zero‑density estimates for primes and bounds on powers of two to show that a fixed positive proportion of odd integers remain uncovered.
title: Positive proportion of odd integers not of the form $p+2^a+2^b$

description: The partial dominating set value function |N[S]| (number of vertices dominated by a set S) cannot be expressed as an FO Value expression with quantifier-free correction terms over the vocabulary of graphs. Concretely: for every unary weight function w : V(G) → ℕ and every quantifier-free formula φ(x₁,...,xₘ) over the vocabulary {E}, there exists a graph G and a finite set S ⊆ V(G) such that |N_G[S]| ≠ (Σ_{v ∈ S} w(v)) − |{(v₁,...,vₘ) ∈ Sᵐ : G ⊨ φ(v₁,...,vₘ)}|. This contrasts with Partial Vertex Cover, which the paper shows is a quantifier-free FO Value instance via the identity |{e : e ∩ S ≠ ∅}| = Σ_{v ∈ S} deg(v) − |E(G[S])|, where the correction term E(x,y) is quantifier-free. The dominating set value requires counting vertices outside S that are adjacent to multiple vertices in S, necessitating existential quantification over vertices not in the selected tuple.
proof_strategy: Construct a family of graphs G_k parameterized by k such that for any quantifier-free formula φ with m free variables and any unary weight w, one can find a set S in some G_k where the quantifier-free FO Value decomposition fails. The key insight is that quantifier-free formulas over the tuple variables can only detect local adjacency patterns among selected vertices, but |N[S]| depends on the number of external vertices adjacent to multiple tuple elements—a global property requiring existential quantification over vertices outside S. A candidate proof uses Hanf-locality of quantifier-free FO: two tuples with the same atomic type in G yield the same correction value, but can dominate different numbers of external vertices, breaking the decomposition.
title: Inexpressibility of Partial Dominating Set as Quantifier-Free FO Value

description: For every integer k ≥ 3, there exists a constant c_k > 0 such that every C_{2k}-free graph with average degree at least c_k · h contains an induced subdivision of K_h. This conjectures that the polylogarithmic factor in the authors' bound of Ω_k(h log^5 h) can be eliminated, making the threshold purely linear in h, which would be tight up to the constant factor.
proof_strategy: Refine the embedding techniques from the paper to eliminate the logarithmic factors introduced during iterative path-finding and pseudorandomness exploitation. Key insight: C_{2k}-free graphs have stronger pseudo-random properties than currently exploited, and more careful use of the dependent random choice or balanced-supergraph techniques could yield path systems that directly give induced subdivisions without the logarithmic overhead from iterative refinement.
title: Linear threshold for induced clique subdivisions in even-cycle-free graphs

description: Characterizes when equality holds in the FKG inequality on the Boolean lattice 2^{[n]}: for a strictly positive log-supermodular measure μ and increasing functions f, g, equality E_μ[fg] = E_μ[f]·E_μ[g] holds if and only if [n] admits a nontrivial partition [n] = A ⊔ B such that μ is a product measure over 2^A × 2^B, f depends only on coordinates in A, and g depends only on coordinates in B. This is a concrete instance of the paper's main Theorem 1.2 (FKG equality conditions) specialized to Boolean lattices.
proof_strategy: Decompose into two directions. Necessity (product structure implies equality) is a direct computation using independence. Sufficiency (equality implies product structure) requires the main technical argument: show that if equality holds, the lattice splits as a direct product L₁ × L₂, which for Boolean lattices means [n] = A ⊔ B; then prove the measure and function factorizations follow from the log-supermodularity constraint combined with the equality constraint. The key step is ruling out all non-product configurations, which uses the rigidity of equality cases established via the AD inequality's equality conditions.
title: FKG Equality Characterization on Boolean Lattices

description: For P(X) = X² + 1, the number of pairs (n, m) with 1 ≤ n < m ≤ N such that (n²+1)(m²+1) is a perfect square is O(logᴬ N) for some absolute constant A ≥ 0. This is equivalent to the variance of the extended Rademacher partial sum ∑_{n≤N} f(n²+1) satisfying Var = N + O(logᴬ N), meaning the off-diagonal contribution is negligible. The equation (n²+1)(m²+1) = k² reduces via Gaussian integer norms to the Pythagorean-type condition (nm−1)² + (n+m)² = k², which for fixed n yields Pell equations whose solutions grow exponentially, giving only O(log N) solutions per n. The conjecture asserts the total across all n ≤ N remains polylogarithmic.
proof_strategy: For each fixed n, factor n²+1 and analyze the generalized Pell equation (n²+1)(m²+1) = k². Use the structure of solutions to Pell equations parametrized by fundamental units in Q(√(−(n²+1))) and related fields. The key is to show that for each n, the number of m ≤ N with (n²+1)(m²+1) = □ is O(log N), and then sum over n using that n²+1 has few representations as norms from quadratic extensions. The Gaussian integer factorization (n²+1)(m²+1) = |(n+i)(m+i)|² = |(nm−1)+(n+m)i|² transforms the problem into counting Pythagorean representations, where height bounds on rational points control the count.
title: Polylogarithmic Paucity of Square Products of Shifted Squares

description: For any ε > 0, there exist effectively computable constants C(ε) > 0 and Q₀(ε) > 0 such that: if for every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character χ with conductor q ≥ Q₀(ε), all non-real zeros ρ of L(s,χ) satisfy Re(ρ) ≤ 1 - C(ε)/log(q), then there is at most one such character χ whose associated L-function has a real zero β in the interval [1 - q^(-ε), 1). This formalizes the paper's main result that excluding non-real zeros from a shrinking neighborhood of s=1 allows a significant refinement of Page's theorem.
proof_strategy: The proof requires establishing: (1) effective zero-free regions for Dirichlet L-functions excluding the Landau-Siegel possibility; (2) a translation mechanism from lower bounds on L(1,χ) to upper bounds on exceptional real zeros β; (3) a counting argument showing that the hypothesis on non-real zeros (lying outside σ ≥ 1 - C/log(q)) prevents the distortion that would allow multiple exceptional characters. Key ingredients include logarithmic derivative estimates for L-functions, the Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon, and effective bounds from the geometry of the zeros. Formalization would proceed by first establishing the effective constants, then the conditional zero-free region, and finally the uniqueness of the exceptional zero.
title: Conditional Refinement of Page's Theorem on Landau-Siegel Zeros

description: The paper defines for each ε>0 a Q-algebra automorphism φ_ε of the ring of symmetric functions Λ_Q(q) via explicit q-deformations of power sums p_n. We conjecture that φ_ε depends only on the wall chamber containing ε, i.e., φ_ε = φ_{ε'} for any ε, ε' in the same interval (1/(k+1), 1/k). Furthermore, the wall-crossing operator W_k := φ_{1/k - δ} ∘ φ_{1/k + δ}^{-1} for small δ>0 acts on the Schur basis s_λ by W_k(s_λ) = q^{a(λ,k)} s_λ where a(λ,k) is a computable integer linear combination of hook lengths and k. This is falsifiable by direct computation in low degree.
proof_strategy: Formalize the ring of symmetric functions and the power sum basis in Lean 4 (using existing mathlib combinatorics of partitions). Define the candidate automorphism φ_ε via the explicit q-deformation formulas from the paper (to be extracted for small r,N,d). Then prove by symbolic computation that for fixed k and low degree truncations, φ_ε is independent of ε within the interval, and compute W_k on basis elements to verify the conjectured q-hook formula. Induction on partition degree may extend to general λ.
title: Chamber-wise constancy and explicit wall-crossing for q-deformed symmetric function automorphisms

description: For the free Catalan structure (C, e, λ, ⊕) satisfying the unique decomposition property from Definition 1, the involution h = rev ∘ corev ∘ rev restricted to level C_n has exactly C_n fixed points, where C_n = (2n choose n)/(n+1) is the n-th Catalan number. This asserts that the fixed-point enumerator of h matches the Catalan generating function.
proof_strategy: First inductively define the free Catalan structure as an inductive type mirroring the three-form decomposition (empty | λ(s) | λ(u) ⊕ v with v ≠ e). Define rev and corev by structural recursion on the first-return and last-return decompositions respectively. Prove h = rev ∘ corev ∘ rev is involutive. Then establish the fixed-point count by constructing an explicit bijection between Fix(h|_{C_n}) and binary trees on n internal nodes, using the characterization that t is a fixed point iff rev(t) = corev(t).
title: Fixed points of involution h on the free Catalan structure are counted by Catalan numbers

description: An extension of the Colorful Carathéodory theorem to convex cones: given $r \ge d$ pairwise disjoint sets of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the origin is in the convex cone generated by each set, there exists a colorful transversal whose convex cone also contains the origin.
proof_strategy: Translate the topological proof into Lean by establishing that the support complexes of oriented matroids are near-$(d-1)$-Leray, and then applying a homological vanishing argument to deduce the existence of the colorful transversal in the cone setting.
title: Cone Colorful Carathéodory Theorem

description: For any inclusion-free (antichain) hypergraph H on vertex set [n] and any offset function f : H → ℝ, the number of isolating weight assignments w : [n] → [d] is at least n * ∑_{j=0}^{d-1} j^{n-1}. A weight assignment w is isolating if there exists a unique edge e ∈ H minimizing f(e) + Σ_{i ∈ e} w(i). This bound is tight, achieved by the singleton hypergraph {{1}, {2}, ..., {n}} with zero offsets, confirming the Faber–Harris (2018) conjecture.
proof_strategy: The proof proceeds by structural induction on the hypergraph, leveraging the Ta-Shma transformation (subtracting the indicator vector of a minimum-weight edge to create an isolating assignment). The key steps are: (1) formalize the notion of inclusion-free hypergraphs and isolating weight assignments, (2) establish that the singleton hypergraph attains the bound with equality, (3) show that any inclusion-free hypergraph with non-trivial structure has at least as many isolating assignments. The argument uses a surjection from isolating assignments of H to those of a reduced hypergraph, combined with counting the number of assignments that can be 'lifted' back.
title: Extremal Bound for Isolating Weight Assignments on Inclusion-Free Hypergraphs

description: Every exotic Diophantine triple {a, b, c} of distinct nonzero polynomials in ℝ[X] with at least one nonconstant element must contain the element 1. That is, if a+1, b+1, c+1, ab+1, ac+1, bc+1, and abc+1 are all perfect squares in ℝ[X], and at least one of a, b, c is nonconstant, then one of a, b, c equals 1.
domain_bridges: polynomial arithmetic over real closed fields
proof_strategy: Formalize the Filipin-Jurasić regularity theorem for polynomial Diophantine quadruples over ℝ[X], which classifies the structure of such quadruples. Then show that any exotic triple {a, b, c} (equivalently, a Diophantine quadruple {1, a, b, c} with abc+1 a square) with a nonconstant element and no element equal to 1 leads to a contradiction with this regularity structure.
title: Exotic Diophantine triples in ℝ[X] must contain 1

description: For any prime p, any p-adic optimization ℓ: ℚ_p^n → ℝ_{≥0} ∪ {∞}, any E ∈ ℕ, and any finite set C ⊆ (ℤ/p^Eℤ)^n, if (1) for all c ∈ dom(ℓ) \ π_E^{-1}(C) there exists d ∈ C with ℓ(d) < ℓ(c), and (2) for all c ∈ π_E^{-1}(C), ℓ(π_E(c)) ≤ ℓ(c), then ℓ is (E,C)-reducible: every optimal solution of OP(ℓ,C) is optimal for OP(ℓ), and every optimal solution c of OP(ℓ) satisfies c ∈ π_E^{-1}(C) with π_E(c) optimal for OP(ℓ,C). This is the key structural proposition enabling the generalized Baker forcing method.
proof_strategy: Direct verification from definitions. Condition (1) forces any global optimum into π_E^{-1}(C); condition (2) ensures the projected point achieves the same objective value, yielding both conditions of (E,C)-reducibility. Formalization requires: (a) defining ℚ_p and the projection π_E: ℚ_p^n → (ℤ/p^Eℤ)^n, (b) defining p-adic optimizations as partial maps ℚ_p^n → ℝ_{≥0} ∪ {∞}, (c) defining (E,C)-reducibility and the restricted optimization problem OP(ℓ,C), then proving the two optimality conditions follow from the hypotheses.
title: Optimality Restriction Lemma for (E,C)-Reducibility of p-adic Optimizations

description: For any integer $k \ge 4$, there exists a constant $C_k > 0$ such that for all positive integers $N$, the minimum modulus of a non-vanishing sum of $k$ $N$-th roots of unity satisfies $f(k, N) \le C_k \cdot N^{-k/4}$. This would generalize Myerson's asymptotic bound $f(k,N) \le N^{-k/4+o_N(1)}$ for even $k$ and even $N$ to all $k \ge 4$ and all $N$, vastly improving upon the logarithmic growth of the exponent $\alpha_k$ established in the paper.
proof_strategy: Extend the perturbation method of Barber and the author using inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation to systematically construct cancellations achieving order $N^{-k/4}$ for arbitrary $k$ and $N$, bypassing the parity constraints of Myerson's original construction.
title: Linear Exponent Conjecture for Small Sums of Roots of Unity

description: For every Turán graph T(n, r) with r ≥ 4 and n ≥ 4r, and for every edge e of T(n, r), the Seidel energy strictly increases upon deletion: E_S(T(n, r) − e) > E_S(T(n, r)). This is Theorem 1.2 of the paper, resolving a problem of Tian et al., but its formalization requires building the entire theory of Seidel matrices, Seidel energy, Turán graphs, and the reduced-order spectral machinery for blow-up graphs—a substantial formalization undertaking.
proof_strategy: First formalize Seidel matrices and Seidel energy in Lean, then define Turán graphs and independent-set blow-up graphs. Establish the reduced-order spectral criterion that reduces the Seidel energy comparison to eigenvalue analysis of a smaller matrix whose order depends only on the number of partite sets. Apply this criterion to the Turán graph case with r ≥ 4 and n ≥ 4r, verifying the inequality via explicit eigenvalue computation on the reduced matrix.
title: Seidel energy strictly increases under edge deletion in Turán graphs

description: For any subgroup G of the symmetric group on n elements and any non-empty k-element subset S of {1,...,n}, if S is the lexicographically minimal element of its G-orbit (under the order defined by: S < R iff min(S △ R) ∈ S), then S \ {max S} is the lexicographically minimal element of its G-orbit. This is the key lemma (Lemma 2.2, attributed to Pech & Reichard 2009) enabling backtracking enumeration of orbit representatives, and its proof by contradiction is self-contained and suitable for formalization.
proof_strategy: Assume S^- = S \ {max S} is not lex-min in its G-orbit. Then there exists π ∈ G and R = π(S^-) with R <_lex S^-. Derive a contradiction by showing this implies π(S) <_lex S, violating S being lex-min. The key case analysis uses the characterization that min(S △ R) ∈ R and considers whether max S is fixed by π or not, exploiting that max S > all elements of S^- to control the symmetric difference.
title: Lexicographic Minimality in Subset Orbits is Preserved Under Maximum Element Removal

description: On the (b,s)-diamond hierarchical lattice with q ≥ 2 communities, let r_k(b,s;q) denote the Ramsey community number—the smallest generation at which the Bayesian evidence ratio for community structure exceeds the detectability threshold—computed without degree correction, and let r_k^{DC}(b,s;q) denote the degree-corrected analogue. Then for all b ≥ 2, s ≥ 2, q ≥ 2: r_k(b,s;q) - r_k^{DC}(b,s;q) = 2. This follows from the exact renormalization-group structure: the sufficient statistics flow under a linear map with eigenvalues {bs, b}, and degree correction shifts the initial conditions of the RG flow such that the evidence ratio crosses the detection threshold exactly two generations earlier, independent of b, s, and q.
proof_strategy: Define the diamond hierarchical lattice recursively. Formalize the RG flow of block-model sufficient statistics as iteration of a 2×2 linear map with eigenvalues bs and b. Compute the log-evidence ratio ln K(t) as a function of generation t, both with and without degree correction, by solving the linear recurrence. Show that the degree-corrected initial conditions shift the evidence trajectory so that the smallest t satisfying ln K(t) > 0 (the detectability threshold) is exactly 2 less than without degree correction. The key algebraic step is comparing the two closed-form expressions for r_k(b,s;q) and r_k^{DC}(b,s;q) derived from the eigenvalue decomposition.
title: Degree correction advances Ramsey community detection by exactly two generations on diamond hierarchical lattices

description: Every connected vertex-transitive digraph on n ≥ 1 vertices contains a directed cycle of length at least ⌈√n⌉. This is the natural directed analogue of Babai's 1979 theorem for undirected vertex-transitive graphs, and strengthens the paper's asymptotic Ω(√n) lower bound to an explicit constant of 1.
proof_strategy: Formalize the core structural argument from the paper's Ω(√n) bound with explicit constants. The proof likely uses the orbit-stabilizer theorem and group-theoretic analysis of the automorphism group acting on the digraph to find a long directed cycle. Key steps: (1) formalize vertex-transitive digraphs and their automorphism groups, (2) establish that connected vertex-transitive digraphs on n vertices have minimum out-degree ≥ 1 and use orbit structure to find cycles, (3) combine the orbit counting with cycle-finding arguments to extract a directed cycle of length ≥ ⌈√n⌉. The existence result (digraphs missing n/12 vertices) provides the complementary upper bound context.
title: Directed Babai Theorem: Long Cycles in Vertex-Transitive Digraphs

catalog_references: Induced matching numbers in dense graphs
description: We conjecture that for the critical case ε=1/2, the maximal anti-Ramsey function for P_4 admits an exact quadratic lower bound with a computable constant. Specifically, we propose that χ_S(n, (n choose 2) - ⌊n^{3/2}⌋, P_4) > (1/8 - o(1))·n² as n → ∞, where the constant 1/8 arises from the induced matching structure in graphs with minimum degree (1/2 + o(1))n. This conjecture addresses the sharpness of the phase transition at ε=1/2 and would require establishing both the lower bound and matching upper bound to determine the exact asymptotic behavior.
domain_bridges: Connections between induced matchings and rainbow colorings
Relationship to the Erdős-Gallai theorem on paths
Bridge between extremal graph theory and Ramsey-type colorings
Threshold phenomena in sparse-dense graph transitions
proof_strategy: The proof would require three main components: (1) Constructive lower bound via explicit graph families showing χ_S(n, (n choose 2) - ⌊n^{3/2}⌋, P_4) ≥ (1/8 - o(1))·n² using induced matching analysis; (2) Upper bound construction demonstrating that no more than (1/8 + o(1))·n² colors are needed; (3) Stability analysis around the minimum degree threshold (1/2)n to verify the exact constant. The approach involves analyzing the structure of graphs missing Θ(n^{3/2}) edges and their P_4 rainbow colorings through induced matching decompositions.
title: Sharp Threshold and Exact Constant for P_4 Anti-Ramsey Number at ε=1/2

description: The Kaneko-Zagier conjecture posits that there exists a well-defined ring isomorphism between the quotient ring of multiple zeta values Z / zeta(2)Z and the ring of finite multiple zeta values Z_A. Specifically, the map sending a symmetric multiple zeta value zeta_S(k) to its corresponding finite multiple zeta value zeta_A(k) is well-defined and preserves the algebraic structures, meaning any Q-linear relation among SMZVs corresponds to an identical relation among FMZVs.
proof_strategy: Define the algebras of MZVs, SMZVs, and FMZVs in Lean. Establish the stuffle and shuffle relations for both SMZVs and FMZVs. Prove that the kernel of the natural projection from MZVs to SMZVs is generated by zeta(2), and show that the map sending SMZVs to FMZVs respects all algebraic relations, thereby establishing the ring isomorphism.
title: Kaneko-Zagier Conjecture for Symmetric and Finite MZVs

description: For the odd Euler ensemble at cutoff N, the positive spectral moments M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) satisfy the precise limit: lim_{N → ∞} √(2N/π) · M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) / |n|^s = ζ(s) for all real s > 1 and nonzero integers n. This identifies the Riemann zeta function as the spectral moment generating function emerging from the continuum limit of the marginally stable turbulent attractor, bridging the arithmetic structure of reduced rational angles p/q with the Lyapunov stability analysis of incompressible Navier–Stokes turbulence.
proof_strategy: Formalize the finite-N spectral problem over reduced rationals p/q and winding sectors r, establish the parity constraint N - qr ≡ 0 (mod 2) ruling out r = 0 for odd N, then apply coprime cotangent sum asymptotics and Jordan totient identities to derive the moment limit. The key step is expressing M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) as a sum over coprime pairs (p, q) with q odd, weighted by |n/q|^s, and showing the normalization √(2N/π) converts the discrete sum to ζ(s) via Euler product or Dirichlet series techniques available in Mathlib's number theory layer.
title: Odd Euler Ensemble Spectral Moment Zeta Convergence

description: For all finite groups G and H, the character conductor of the Galois-orbit-trace probe satisfies C_char(G × H) = C_char(G) ∪ C_char(H), directly paralleling the proven unconditional direct product law for the commuting conductor C_comm(G × H) = C_comm(G) ∪ C_comm(H).
