proof_strategy: Decompose the Galois-orbit-trace payoff matrix for G × H via the tensor product structure of irreducible characters of direct products; relate it to a Kronecker-type construction on the factor matrices; then apply the instrument identity (conductor equals prime divisors of gcd of maximal minors) to reduce to analyzing how Smith invariant factors of the combined matrix are determined by those of the factors, carefully tracking Galois-orbit merging under products.
title: Character Conductor Direct Product Law

catalog_references: Bonnet, Kim, Thomassé, Watrigant - Twin-width I (arXiv:2007.04352)
Bonnet, Geniet, Tessera, Thomassé - Twin-width VII (arXiv:2202.07006, QI invariance of twin-width)
Gromov - Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps (1981)
Wilkes - Finitely generated inaccessible residually p-finite groups (2019)
description: Every finitely generated virtually nilpotent group has finite twin-width. This conjecture provides a positive structural guarantee for the combinatorial parameter of twin-width from the algebraic assumption of virtual nilpotence, complementing the paper's negative result that finite twin-width does not imply accessibility. Specifically, if Γ is a finitely generated group containing a nilpotent subgroup of finite index, then every Cayley graph of Γ has finite twin-width (i.e., the supremum of twin-widths of finite induced subgraphs is bounded). The proof would proceed by: (1) establishing that Z^n has finite twin-width by bounding the twin-width of subgraphs of the n-dimensional grid, (2) showing that torsion-free finitely generated nilpotent groups embed as discrete cocompact subgroups of nilpotent Lie groups, yielding quasi-isometric embeddings into R^m whose integer lattice Z^m has finite twin-width, and (3) applying the quasi-isometric invariance of twin-width for bounded-degree graphs (Twin-width VII, Bonnet et al.) together with finite-index arguments for the virtual case.
domain_bridges: Nilpotent group structure theory ↔ grid graph twin-width bounds
Quasi-isometric invariance of twin-width ↔ geometric group theory invariants
Cayley graph combinatorics ↔ Lie group embedding theorems (Mal'cev)
proof_strategy: Step 1: Prove the n-dimensional integer grid Z^n (as a Cayley graph with standard generators) has twin-width at most n+1, by constructing explicit contraction sequences for finite grid subgraphs that maintain bounded red degree. Step 2: Show that every torsion-free finitely generated nilpotent group N admits a discrete cocompact embedding into its Mal'cev completion (a simply-connected nilpotent Lie group), so that N is quasi-isometric to R^m equipped with a nilpotent Lie group metric, and hence N is quasi-isometric to a finite-index subgroup of Z^m (via the integer lattice). Step 3: Apply the quasi-isometric invariance of finite twin-width for bounded-degree graphs (Twin-width VII) to conclude that N has finite twin-width. Step 4: Extend to virtually nilpotent groups: if G has a nilpotent subgroup H of finite index, then G is quasi-isometric to H, and since H has finite twin-width by Step 3, so does G.
title: Finite Twin-Width of Virtually Nilpotent Groups

description: For every positive integer n, the bigraded section ring R(n) = ⨁_{(k,m) ∈ ℤ_{≥0}²} A^m_{≥k}(n) of Hilb^n(Bl_0(ℂ²)) — where A^m_{≥k}(n) denotes the subspace of diagonally alternating polynomials of degree m in ℂ[x₁,y₁,...,xₙ,yₙ] vanishing to order ≥ k at the origin — is generated as a ℂ-algebra by its components with m ≤ 2. Equivalently, every element of A^m_{≥k}(n) for arbitrary m and k can be expressed as a polynomial combination of elements from A¹_{≥j}(n) and A²_{≥j}(n) for various j. This extends Haiman's result that ⨁_{m≥0} A^m(n) is generated in degree m=1, adding the vanishing-order filtration arising from the exceptional divisor.
domain_bridges: Combinatorics of partitions and symmetric functions
proof_strategy: Use the CGOT description of sections of line bundles on Hilbert schemes of toric surfaces to identify A^m_{≥k}(n) explicitly in terms of alternating polynomials. Establish that A^m_{≥k}(n) decomposes into products of lower-degree pieces by analyzing the vanishing-order filtration and the multiplication map on the polynomial ring ℂ[x₁,y₁,...,xₙ,yₙ]. For m ≥ 3, show by induction on m that A^m_{≥k}(n) ⊆ Span(A^{m₁}_{≥k₁}(n) · A^{m₂}_{≥k₂}(n)) for m₁,m₂ < m with m₁+m₂=m and k₁+k₂=k, using the wall-crossing structure from the MMP to control the base cases m=1,2. The key difficulty is showing A²_{≥k}(n) is not needed beyond what A¹_{≥j}(n) products already generate for k ≤ 2j, which requires analyzing the symmetric group action on the polynomial ring.
title: Quadratic Generation of the Bigraded Section Ring of Hilbert Schemes on the Affine Blowup

description: The non-separating degeneration of the multivariable Enriquez connection from genus h to h-1 with two punctures induces a map on the associated Lie algebras whose matrix coefficients are polynomials in Bernoulli numbers B_2, B_4, ..., B_{2h-2} with rational coefficients. These polynomials are universal in the sense that they do not depend on h, and coincide with the polynomials obtained from the genus 1 degeneration. Specifically, for each generator index, the coefficient of B_{2k} in the degeneration formula is a fixed rational number independent of h.
proof_strategy: Extract the explicit degeneration formulas for the Lie algebra generators from the paper for genera h=2,3,4. Express the coefficients as polynomials in Bernoulli numbers with rational coefficients. Verify that these polynomials match the genus-1 case. Formalize the Bernoulli numbers and the polynomial expressions in Lean, then computationally check the genus-independence for low genera using Lean's norm_num and polynomial decision procedures.
title: Universality of Bernoulli generating functions in non-separating degeneration of Enriquez connections

description: For the wild dimensional regime (2r > d), a saturated set S ⊆ 𝔾(r,V) is a disjoint union of k spines if and only if the corresponding core k-planes π₁, ..., πₖ satisfy dim(πᵢ ∩ πⱼ) ≤ 2r - d for all i ≠ j, with the bound 2r - d being sharp (achieved by some configuration).
domain_bridges: linear algebra over inner product spaces
proof_strategy: Construct explicit examples achieving the bound using direct sum decompositions of the Hilbert space, then prove necessity by analyzing the intersection properties of r-planes under the saturation condition and orthogonal projection constraints.
title: Mutual Separation Bound for Multiple Spine Decompositions in Wild Dimensional Regime

description: Conjecture that for any finite metric space X of strictly negative type there exists exactly one signed measure μ of total mass 1 that minimizes the energy functional E(μ)=∑_{x,y∈X}d(x,y)μ(x)μ(y); moreover μ can be characterized as the unique optimizer of this strictly convex quadratic program.
proof_strategy: Formulate the problem as a strictly convex quadratic optimization over the affine subspace of signed measures with total mass 1; strict convexity guarantees a unique minimizer, and strict negative type ensures that the quadratic form is positive definite on the relevant subspace.
title: Existence and uniqueness of microscopic weightings on finite strictly negative type metric spaces

description: For an elliptic curve E over Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free D ≡1 mod 4, the difference in sharp/flat λ-invariants under quadratic twist by D should include a term proportional to the μ-invariant when μ ≠ 0.
proof_strategy: Extend the existing formula by analyzing the μ-invariant's contribution through local-global principles and modular forms.
title: Extension of Matsuno's Formula for Non-Vanishing μ-Invariants

description: Conjecture that the number Q_k(n) of length‑n quasinecklaces over a k‑letter alphabet equals the classical count of primitive words, i.e. ℑ Q_k(n) = π_{d|n} μ(d) k^{n/d} for all integers k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: We would prove the conjecture by establishing a bijection between quasinecklaces and primitive words, or by showing that the recurrence defining quasinecklaces derived in the paper matches the Möbius inversion of the total word count. A proof by induction on n using divisor decomposition and properties of the Möbius function can be formalized in Lean, leveraging existing libraries for arithmetic functions and finite sums.
title: Exact formula for the number of quasinecklaces

description: For integers n, k, ℓ with n > 100·ℓ·k² and 3 ≤ ℓ < k, if F ⊆ ([n] choose k) and G ⊆ ([n] choose ℓ) are non-trivial cross-intersecting families (i.e., ⋂_{F∈F} F = ∅ and ⋂_{G∈G} G = ∅, and F ∩ G ≠ ∅ for all F ∈ F, G ∈ G), then |F|·|G| ≤ h(n,k)·(n-1 choose ℓ-1), where h(n,k) = (n-1 choose k-1) - (n-k-1 choose k-1) + 1 is the Hilton-Milner bound.
proof_strategy: First formalize the classical Hilton-Milner theorem as a lemma. Then formalize the notion of cross-intersecting families and non-triviality. The key structural insight from the paper is analyzing 2-cover graphs of cross-intersecting families and bounding the size of families with small minimal covers. The proof proceeds by case analysis on the structure of minimal covers of F and G, showing that non-HM-type configurations yield strictly smaller products when n > 100ℓk².
title: Product Hilton-Milner theorem for large n

description: For every bridgeless cubic multigraph G, there exists a mapping f: E(G) → E(S₁₀) such that |V(f)| ≥ (6/7)·|V(G)|, where V(f) is the set of vertices v ∈ V(G) for which f(∂_G(v)) = ∂_{S₁₀}(x) for some x ∈ V(S₁₀). This would improve the 5/6-bound established in the paper for all cubic multigraphs, leveraging the additional structure of bridgeless graphs.
proof_strategy: Adapt the S₁₀-construction from the paper, exploiting the absence of bridges to handle end-block decomposition more efficiently. Since bridgeless cubic graphs admit perfect matchings (Petersen's theorem), combine the S₁₂-technique achieving 4/5 for graphs with perfect matchings with the triangle-replacement structure of S₁₀ to gain the additional 1/42 fraction, using the fact that bridgeless graphs avoid the trivial-bridge obstructions that limit the 5/6 bound.
title: Bridgeless Sylvester S₁₀-Coloring Improvement Conjecture

description: The theta series of any even positive definite unimodular lattice of rank 8 equals the Eisenstein series E₄. Concretely, for every positive integer n, the number of vectors of norm n in such a lattice equals 240·σ₃(n), where σ₃(n) = Σ_{d|n} d³. This is the foundational special case of the classical Siegel-Weil formula, connecting the theta series of a lattice to an Eisenstein series, and reduces to verifying that the Fourier coefficients of θ_L coincide with those of E₄.
proof_strategy: Two possible routes: (1) Modular route — prove θ_L is a modular form of weight 4 for SL₂(ℤ) via Poisson summation on the lattice, establish that M₄(SL₂(ℤ)) is 1-dimensional spanned by E₄, and match constant terms; (2) Combinatorial route — use the explicit root system of E₈ to compute the theta series coefficients and verify they equal 240·σ₃(n) via the Weyl character formula or direct root system enumeration.
title: Siegel-Weil Identity for the E₈ Lattice Theta Series

description: Every connected bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graph on n vertices is a complete bipartite graph K_{n/2, n/2}. This strengthens the paper's theorem that every bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graph is regular, and if true, would provide a complete structural characterization connecting the {-1,0,1}-diagonalizability property to classical complete bipartite graph structure.
proof_strategy: Use the paper's structure theorem for {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graphs of prime order as a base case. For composite orders, leverage the regularity result (Theorem: bipartite implies regular) combined with the eigenvector structure constraints: the {-1,0,1} eigenvector basis forces strong conditions on the adjacency patterns of regular bipartite graphs. A possible approach shows that if G is connected, bipartite, regular, and {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable, then any two vertices in the same part have identical neighbor sets, yielding completeness. Attempt falsification by exhaustive search for small orders using the enumeration data provided.
title: Bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graphs are complete bipartite

description: For all positive integers k ≥ 2, n ≥ 1, and 1 ≤ j ≤ n, the symmetric function Δ_{e_j} G(k,n) is Schur positive (i.e., expands with nonnegative coefficients in ℕ[q,t] in the Schur basis) if and only if k divides n, where G(k,n) = Σ_{λ⊢n, λ₁<k} m_λ is the Petrie symmetric function and Δ_{e_j} is the Bergeron–Garsia delta operator applied to e_j. This extends the paper's main result for ∇ = Δ_{e_n} (and its iterates ∇^r) to all elementary symmetric function inputs of the delta operator, establishing that the divisibility criterion governs Schur positivity uniformly across the entire family of delta operators.
domain_bridges: Representation theory of symmetric groups (Schur positivity ↔ graded module existence)
Diagonal harmonics and nabla operator theory
proof_strategy: For the forward direction (k∣n ⟹ Schur positivity): decompose G(k,n) into creation operator images C_α when k∣n, then apply the compositional shuffle theorem framework to express Δ_{e_j} C_α as a positively weighted sum of vertical LLT polynomials, leveraging Grojnowski–Haiman Schur positivity of LLT polynomials. For the converse (k∤n ⟹ not Schur positive): extend the sign-analysis techniques from the paper's nabla case to general Δ_{e_j} by tracking the leading negative Schur coefficients in the Macdonald polynomial expansion of G(k,n) under the delta eigenvalue action, showing that the divisibility obstruction propagates through all delta operators.
title: Delta-Petrie Schur Positivity

description: The fluctuation of the weighted counting function of closed geodesics in homology classes modulo $q$, defined as $\Psi_M(X; q, \alpha) - \Psi_M(X)/q^{2g}$, when normalized by its asymptotic standard deviation $\sqrt{X \log X}$, converges in distribution to a standard normal distribution as $X \to \infty$ and $g \to \infty$. This conjecture extends the paper's computation of the variance ($\sim X \log X$) to a full central limit theorem, analogous to the Gaussian distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions.
proof_strategy: Establish moment bounds for higher-order moments of the fluctuations to apply the method of moments, leveraging the Selberg trace formula on random surfaces and the known variance asymptotic of $X \log X$.
title: Asymptotic Normality of Prime Geodesic Fluctuations on Random Hyperbolic Surfaces

description: The paper proves that Mason's conjecture on the equivalence of two definitions of symmetric powers of matroids holds for k=2 but fails for k=3. The natural conjecture is that it fails for all k ≥ 3: for every integer k ≥ 3, there exists a matroid M such that the two definitions of the k-th symmetric power of M yield different matroids. This would completely characterize the boundary between the two definitions coinciding and diverging.
proof_strategy: Generalize the k=3 counterexample construction. The paper establishes a duality between symmetric powers and abstract rigidity. One would need to show that the rigidity-theoretic obstruction that produces the k=3 counterexample can be lifted to higher k, perhaps by taking symmetric powers of the counterexample matroid itself, or by constructing a family of matroids M_k indexed by k ≥ 3 such that the rank functions from the two Mason definitions diverge on specific independent sets in sym_k(M_k).
title: Mason's Conjecture Fails for All Higher Symmetric Powers

description: Every connected acyclic inversion graph of a permutation is a caterpillar graph. That is, for any permutation π whose inversion graph G_π is connected and contains no cycles, G_π is a caterpillar: removing all leaves from G_π yields a path graph (the spine). This unifies classical characterizations by Edelman, Tenner, and Petersen–Tenner, and the paper provides a new proof via the reduced-word ordering on inversion edges.
proof_strategy: First formalize the inversion graph G_π of a permutation π as the graph on [n] with edges corresponding to inversions. Define caterpillar graphs (removing all degree-1 vertices yields a path). Then establish the key mechanism: a reduced word for π orders the edges of G_π, with first-occurrence letters forming a spanning forest. For the acyclic case, show that the spanning tree has a unique central path by analyzing how the cycle structure of π constrains the possible branching patterns, leveraging the fact that each cycle of π contributes a specific subtree structure that can only attach linearly along a spine.
title: Acyclic inversion graphs are caterpillars

description: For Levenshtein's sequence reconstruction problem with insertion errors, the paper proves the surprising fact that N_q^m(n,1) = N_q^{nm}(n,1) for all alphabet size q and word length n—that is, the minimum number of channels required for unambiguous reconstruction is identical whether repeated outputs are tracked as a multiset or as an unordered set, when exactly one insertion occurs per channel. The conjecture proposes that this equality extends to all insertion counts t >= 1: N_q^m(n,t) = N_q^{nm}(n,t) for all q >= 2, n >= 1, t >= 1.
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on t, leveraging the t=1 base case proven in the paper. For the inductive step, analyze how the multiset and non-multiset intersection structures of insertion balls decompose when composing t insertions as a sequence of single insertions. The key difficulty is showing that the overlap multiplicities from repeated error patterns cannot create a distinction between the multiset and non-multiset models even when t > 1. A combinatorial double-counting argument on the equivalence classes of insertion error patterns producing identical outputs may suffice.
title: Equality of Multiset and Non-Multiset Reconstruction Numbers for All Insertion Counts

description: The paper establishes an upper bound of $O(d^{2/(r-1)})$ for the star chromatic number $\chi_s^r(d)$ of $r$-uniform hypergraphs with maximum degree $d$ (where a star is defined as two hyperedges intersecting in $r-1$ vertices). We conjecture that this upper bound is asymptotically tight, meaning there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that for all $r \ge 3$ and $d \ge 1$, $\chi_s^r(d) \ge c \cdot d^{2/(r-1)}$.
proof_strategy: Use probabilistic methods or explicit algebraic constructions to demonstrate a family of $r$-uniform hypergraphs with maximum degree $d$ that cannot be star-colored with fewer than $c \cdot d^{2/(r-1)}$ colors, adapting known lower bounds for graph star coloring to the hypergraph setting.
title: Asymptotic Tightness of Star Coloring in Hypergraphs

description: For the family of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions L(u, χ_D) where D ranges over squarefree polynomials of odd degree d = 2g+1 in F_q[T], the n-level density of normalized zeros converges to the n-level density of eigenvalue angles of USp(2g) matrices as q → ∞. Specifically, for any Schwartz function f : ℝ^n → ℝ with Fourier transform supported in (-1,1)^n, the family-average of ∑_{distinct i₁,...,i_n} f(θ_{i₁},...,θ_{i_n}) over normalized zero angles θ of L(u,χ_D) converges to ∫_{[0,1]^n} f(x) · W_{n,USp(2g)}(x) dx, where W_{n,USp(2g)} is the symplectic n-level density kernel.
proof_strategy: Adapt the Mason-Snaith ratio conjecture framework to function fields: (1) formalize the explicit formula relating sums over zeros to sums over primes in F_q[T], (2) compute the n-level density via the ratio of L-functions averaged over the family using character sum identities over F_q[T], (3) show the resulting combinatorial expression matches the n-level correlation kernel of USp(2g) eigenvalues computed from the symplectic group's Weyl integration formula, using the restricted Fourier support to control error terms.
title: Symplectic n-level density correspondence for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions over function fields

description: Every open product-free subset of (0,1) — meaning no x, y, z ∈ A satisfy xy = z — has Lebesgue measure strictly less than 1/3. This resolves the third problem in Green's collection of 100 open problems and constitutes a continuous analogue of Erdős's classical question on maximal sum-free subsets.
proof_strategy: Apply the change of variables y = -log(x) to convert the product-free condition on (0,1) into a sum-free condition on (0,∞) with respect to the exponential distribution. Then leverage the positive interval discrepancy d(A) = sup_I (2|A∩I| - |I|) to obtain refined lower bounds on |A±A| beyond the Kneser/Brunn-Minkowski bound |A-A| ≥ 2|A|, quantifying how far A is from an interval. These structural results on sumsets force |A| < 1/3 for any open product-free set.
title: Product-free open subsets of (0,1) have measure less than 1/3

description: For every integer n ≥ 2, there exists a finite free n-dimensional simplicial Z_2-complex K such that coind(K) = 1 and coind(S(K)) = n+1, demonstrating that the excess of the co-index of a suspension over the lower bound coind(X)+1 can be arbitrarily large.
proof_strategy: Explicitly construct the simplicial Z_2-complex K for each n, prove it is a free Z_2-space, and compute its co-index and the co-index of its suspension using the Borsuk-Ulam theorem and homotopy equivalence arguments.
title: Unbounded Gap Between Co-Index of a Free Z_2-Space and Its Suspension

description: For every positive integer m and every 0 < α < 1/2, there exists a constant C(m,α) > 0 such that for all odd prime powers q and all subsets E ⊆ F_q^{2m}, if |E| ≥ C(m,α) · q^m then the set of nonzero quadratic distances Δ_Q^×(E) = {Q(x−y) : x,y ∈ E} ∩ F_q^× has size greater than α(q−1), where Q(x) = x₁² + ⋯ + x_{2m}². This asserts that subsets of F_q^{2m} of size proportional to q^m determine a positive proportion of all possible nonzero distances, which is the sharp threshold predicted by the Erdős–Falconer conjecture. The current paper achieves this conditionally on a Kloosterman anti-concentration conjecture, and unconditionally achieves the weaker q^{m+1/2} threshold.
proof_strategy: The paper's semidefinite Delsarte framework reduces the conjecture to a uniform L¹ anti-concentration statement for positive convex combinations of classical Kloosterman sums. A complete proof requires either (1) establishing the Kloosterman anti-concentration conjecture—that positive convex combinations of Kloosterman sums K_q(a·t) cannot concentrate in L¹ beyond a universal lower bound proportional to 1/√q—or (2) an entirely new method bypassing the Delsarte/LP framework. The unconditional q^{m+1/2} threshold follows from a second-moment bound on Kloosterman sums (Weil bound), but improving to q^m requires overcoming the fundamental barrier that individual Kloosterman columns can nearly cancel.
title: Erdős–Falconer Distance Conjecture in Even Finite Field Dimensions

description: Every t-perfect graph is 4-colorable. The discovery of t-perfect graphs with chromatic number 4 demonstrates that this bound would be tight. Although recent breakthroughs have established the first finite upper bounds on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs (currently 186), a wide gap remains between the lower bound of 4 and the upper bound, making this a central open problem in polyhedral combinatorics.
proof_strategy: Further refine the structural analysis of graphs avoiding odd wheels as t-minors and their odd cycle intersections, potentially leveraging the integer decomposition property of the stable set polytope or developing new leveling arguments to progressively reduce the chromatic upper bound from 186 down to 4.
title: t-Perfect Graph 4-Colorability Conjecture

description: For every loopless matroid M on finite ground set E and every Feichtner–Yuzvinsky building set G containing the top flat E, the K-polynomial of the integral tangent class T^Z_{M,G} ∈ K_Z(M,G) equals the Hilbert series of the Chow ring A*(M,G). Concretely, P^K(T^Z_{M,G}, t) = Hilb(A*(M,G), t) as polynomials in Z[t]. This is the central P^K=Hilb identity (Theorem A, property 2) of the paper, connecting the K-theoretic tangent class to the cohomological Hilbert series.
domain_bridges: graded ring homomorphisms between K-ring and Chow ring
proof_strategy: First formalize loopless matroids, Feichtner-Yuzvinsky building sets, the graded integral K-ring K_Z(M,G) with its alpha-generators, and the Chow ring A*(M,G) with its Bergman fan presentation. Construct the integral tangent class via the quotient/theta-machinery of Sections 4-5. Then prove P^K=Hilb by establishing that the K-ring Chern character ch_K maps T^Z_{M,G} to the Todd class whose pushforward recovers the Hilbert series, mirroring the classical HRR argument adapted to the combinatorial setting.
title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch Identity for the Integral Tangent Class of Matroids

description: For any subset A ⊆ [N] containing no harmonic triple (distinct a, b, c ∈ A with 2/a = 1/b + 1/c), the density |A|/N → 0 as N → ∞. Formally: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, every A ⊆ {1,...,N} with no harmonic triple satisfies |A| ≤ ε·N. This is the reciprocal analogue of Roth's theorem on 3-AP-free sets, posed as Question 1 in the paper. The paper's construction yields sets of size ≫ N·exp(−C√(log log N)), so a positive resolution would need new upper-bound techniques beyond Roth-type methods, since the reciprocal map x ↦ 1/x is not additive.
proof_strategy: Adapt density-increment or energy-based methods (Bloom-Sisask, Kelley-Meka) to the multiplicative/reciprocal setting. Key obstacle: the map n ↦ n⁻¹ mod q is nonlinear, so arithmetic regularity lemmas don't directly apply. A promising approach: show that a positive-density set A ⊆ [N] must contain many 'approximate' harmonic triples, then use a stability argument to upgrade to exact ones. Alternatively, develop a Fourier-analytic framework for the equation 2bc = a(b+c) over the integers, treating the quadratic constraint via sieve methods.
title: Reciprocal Roth Conjecture: Harmonic-Triple-Free Sets Have Density Zero

description: For any prime power $q$, there exists a cyclic sequence of length $q^3(q^2+q+1)$ over the alphabet of affine points and $1$-subspaces in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ such that every affine plane in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ is represented exactly once by a sliding window of length three. The window encodes an affine plane $w + \langle u_1, u_2 \rangle$ via a triple of mixed affine points and direction classes (e.g., $(w, [u_1], [u_2])$ or $(w, w+u_1, w+u_2)$). This extends the paper's construction which currently holds for $n \ge 4$.
proof_strategy: Adapt the local-to-global frame decomposition and gluing technique from the $n \ge 4$ case by constructing explicit local cycles on frame configurations in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ and finding a Hamiltonian cycle in the corresponding transition graph, overcoming the restricted dimensionality that prevents the standard layered frame decomposition from working directly.
title: Universal Cycles for Affine Planes in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$

description: The augmented chain complex E_• defined on polarised noncrossing partitions with {0,1}-labelled gaps, with differential given by the restricted Leibniz rule via gap-insertion, is acyclic: its reduced homology vanishes in all degrees. Concretely, for the augmented chain complex (E_•, ∂, aug) where E_0 = ℤ{s,t}, E_{n+1} = ℤ(PNCP(n)), and ∂ is defined recursively on rightmost decompositions via the gap-insertion operad structure, we have H̃_n(E_•) = 0 for all n ≥ 0.
proof_strategy: First formalize PNCP(n) as polarised noncrossing partitions of degree n with {0,1}-labelled gaps, the rightmost decomposition, and the gap-insertion partial composition pcirc_i. Then define the differential ∂ recursively on rightmost decompositions, verify ∂∘∂ = 0 by induction on degree and rightmost decomposition length using the restricted Leibniz rule structure. For acyclicity, construct an explicit chain contraction or homotopy by exploiting the gap-labelling structure and the operadic decomposition, showing each cycle is a boundary.
title: Acyclicity of the polarised noncrossing partition chain complex

description: The paper proves that every circular Hessenberg pair satisfies the tridiagonal relations (Lee's conjecture). The converse remains open: among all Hessenberg pairs on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space, exactly the circular ones satisfy the tridiagonal relations. That is, a Hessenberg pair (A, A*) satisfies the tridiagonal relations if and only if it is circular (i.e., each acts on an eigenbasis of the other in a circular Hessenberg fashion, meaning the top-right corner entry is nonzero and every other entry above the superdiagonal is zero).
proof_strategy: The forward direction is the content of the paper (proving Lee's conjecture). For the converse, suppose a Hessenberg pair satisfies the tridiagonal relations. Use the tridiagonal relations to derive constraints on the matrix entries of each operator acting on the other's eigenbasis. Show that the vanishing conditions above the superdiagonal (except the top-right corner) and the nonvanishing of the top-right corner follow from the tridiagonal relations combined with the Hessenberg structure. This may involve analyzing the recurrence relations imposed by the tridiagonal relations on the entries of the Hessenberg matrices and showing that non-circular Hessenberg pairs violate these relations.
title: Circular Hessenberg pairs are characterized by the tridiagonal relations

description: For every integer $n \geq 5$, the value $x_n := \tan\bigl(\sum_{k=1}^{n} \arctan k\bigr)$ is not an integer. Equivalently, writing $Z_n = \prod_{k=1}^n(1+ik) = A_n + iB_n$ with $A_n, B_n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the conjecture asserts that $A_n \nmid B_n$ for all $n \geq 5$. The four known integer values are $x_1=1, x_2=-3, x_3=0, x_4=4$.
proof_strategy: Reduce integrality of $x_n$ to the divisibility condition $A_n | B_n$ where $Z_n = A_n + iB_n = \prod_{k=1}^n(1+ik)$. Exploit the factorization $A_n^2 + B_n^2 = \omega_n = \prod_{k=1}^n(1+k^2)$ and the Gaussian prime factorization of each $1+ik$. Use $p$-adic valuations (particularly $\nu_2$) to systematically exclude $A_n | B_n$ for $n \geq 5$, combining the recurrence $x_n = (x_{n-1}+n)/(1-nx_{n-1})$ with arithmetic constraints on the prime factorization structure of $\omega_n$.
title: Amdeberhan-Medina-Moll Conjecture on Arctangent Sum Integrality

description: For a squarefree integer P and squarefree divisors b₁, b₂ of P, the sum ∑_{d|P} d·μ((b₁,d))·φ((b₁,d))·μ((b₂,d))·φ((b₂,d))/φ(d)² equals the product ∏_{p|P} (1 + p·μ((b₁,p))·φ((b₁,p))·μ((b₂,p))·φ((b₂,p))/(p-1)²). This multiplicative identity is the key computational step in the corrected proof of Opera Lemma 6.18, enabling the bound on the weighted second moment of beta-sieve weights.
proof_strategy: Show both sides are multiplicative functions of P by verifying that the left-hand side decomposes as a product over prime factors of P. For each prime p dividing P, verify the four cases — p∤b₁b₂, p|b₁∧p∤b₂, p∤b₁∧p|b₂, p|(b₁,b₂) — by direct computation using μ(p)φ(p) = -(p−1), μ(1)φ(1) = 1, and φ(p) = p−1. The case analysis yields factors 1+p/(p−1)², −1/(p−1), −1/(p−1), and p+1 respectively, matching the product on the right.
title: Sieve Weight Correlation Product Identity

description: For any 2x2 matrix A over a commutative ring R, the anti-diagonal entries of A^(k+1) are equal to the product of the corresponding anti-diagonal entries of A and the trace of the k-th symmetric power of A. This algebraic identity implies the conjugation invariance of the anti-diagonal power quotients and generalizes Fibonacci/Lucas identities.
proof_strategy: Define the k-th symmetric power of a 2x2 matrix and compute its trace. Prove the identity by induction on k using the recurrence relations for the entries of A^k derived from the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, alongside the recurrence for the trace of the symmetric power. Alternatively, prove it over ℤ by counting walks of length k+1 on the complete digraph of order 2 and comparing the combinatorial objects with the symmetric power trace recurrence.
title: Anti-diagonal Trace Identity for 2x2 Matrix Symmetric Powers

description: This conjecture proposes a precise algorithm to compute the asymptotic resurgence number of a pair of graded families of ideals in a $\mathbb{K}$-domain by leveraging the containment properties of their associated Newton-Okounkov regions. The algorithm formalizes the containment relations between Newton-Okounkov regions using convex geometric properties and Attouch--Wets topology, providing a computable upper bound via the supremum of limit ratios of containment thresholds.
proof_strategy: Formalize the asymptotic resurgence number via limit expressions of dimension ratios of intersections of Newton-Okounkov regions under analytic-semialgebraic convergence. Use barber calculus to bound the ratio $s/r$ through the minimal inner product of limit points in corresponding regions.
title: Asymptotic Resurgence Through Newton-Okounkov Containment: A Rigorous Algorithm

catalog_references: This paper: The crumby coloring conjecture for subcubic outerplanar graphs
description: Conjecture: Every finite simple outerplanar graph with maximum degree at most 4 admits a crumby coloring, i.e., a red-blue vertex partition where the blue-induced subgraph has maximum degree at most 1 and the red-induced subgraph has no isolated vertices and no simple path on three edges. This extends the paper's main theorem (Δ≤3) and probes the boundary of the rooted grammar method.
domain_bridges: Lean 4 formalization of graph-theoretic grammar inductions
proof_strategy: Extend the rooted grammar to allow vertices of degree 4 by adding nonterminals for two-terminal and four-terminal fragments. Define crumby-admissible boundary types tracking temporary isolated red vertices at terminals. Enumerate a finite certificate family and verify closure under extended production rules plus final-legality, using a Lean-verified checker.
title: Crumby colorings for outerplanar graphs of maximum degree four

catalog_references: Malle 2002, Malle's conjecture for permutation groups
Loughran–Santens 2024, Galois cohomology and Malle's conjecture
Bhargava–Mass formula for S_n and related principles
description: The leading constant c(H) in Malle's conjecture for Galois H‑extensions of ℚ, where H is the 3×3 Heisenberg group over 𝔽₄, is predicted to equal the sum of two distinct Euler products: one arising from the normal subgroup of H and the other from the quotient H/Z(H), each expressed as a product over all primes p of explicit local factors depending on the Frobenius class of p in H.
proof_strategy: Compute the local factors of the two Euler products explicitly for each prime, verify their product matches the predicted combinatorial constant via group cohomology calculations, and implement a Lean 4 decision procedure that checks the equality by evaluating truncated products to any desired precision.
title: Conjecture on the leading constant for the 3×3 Heisenberg group over 𝔽₄ in Malle's conjecture

description: The minimum rank formula mr^F(I(n,k)) = n-2k+2 holds not only for infinite fields but also for finite fields F when |F| exceeds an explicit threshold depending on n and k. Specifically, we conjecture that there exists a function f(n,k) such that for all finite fields F with |F| > f(n,k), the minimum rank of the intersection graph I(n,k) equals n-2k+2, matching the infinite field case.
proof_strategy: Extend the main proof technique from the paper (constructing rank-n-2k+2 matrices using Vandermonde-like structures) but account for field size constraints in characteristic and size. Use counting arguments to show that for large enough finite fields, one can avoid linear dependence issues that arise in small characteristic cases. The conjecture can be falsified by finding any finite field F where the minimum rank exceeds n-2k+2, or verified by proving the bound holds uniformly.
title: Minimum rank of I(n,k) over sufficiently large finite fields

description: Conjecture: For every integer q ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large n, any n-vertex d-regular graph with ⌊n/(d+1)⌋ = q satisfies Cyc(G) ≥ (q - o(1))·2^{n/q}; equivalently, if k = ⌊n/(d+1)⌋ then the number of cyclic subsets is at least (k - ε)·2^{n/k} for some ε → 0 as n → ∞.
proof_strategy: probabilistic counting combined with stability analysis of regular graphs
title: Tight Staircase Bounds for Cyclic Subsets below Dirac's Threshold

description: For every integer k ≥ 3 and every ℓ with 1 ≤ ℓ < k, the rational function f(x) = x / (2 - x) is a transfer function for the single-forbidden ℓ-degree Turán spectrum Π^k_ℓ: for any k-uniform hypergraph F there exists a k-uniform hypergraph F* obtained by applying the tree suspension operation to F such that π_ℓ(F*) = f(π_ℓ(F)).
proof_strategy: Construct F* via the tree suspension operation: take a rooted tree where each vertex is replaced by a copy of F and edges correspond to joining copies via a complete ℓ-partite structure. Use the two-part construction to obtain a lower bound showing π_ℓ(F*) ≥ f(π_ℓ(F)). For the upper bound, apply a Lagrangian method (or flag algebra calculation) to any extremal ℓ-degree configuration in F*, showing that no construction can exceed f(π_ℓ(F)). The equality follows, establishing the transfer function.
title: Universal Transfer Function Conjecture for Tree Suspensions

description: Conjecture that the bound |V(f)| >= 4/5 * |V(G)| for mappings f:E(G)->E(S_12) from any cubic graph G with a perfect matching to S_12 cannot be improved; i.e., there exists a cubic graph G with a perfect matching such that for every such mapping f, |V(f)| <= 4/5 * |V(G)|.
proof_strategy: explicit_counterexample_construction
title: Tightness of the 4/5-vertex coverage bound for mappings into S_12

catalog_references: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic (survey)
Kudla, Rapoport, Yang - Modular forms and special cycles on Shimura curves
Kudla, Millson - The theta correspondence and harmonic forms
description: For an even lattice L of signature (n-1,1) with n ≥ 2, the generating series of arithmetic special cycles on the associated orthogonal Shimura variety equals the central derivative of the incoherent Eisenstein series.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by extending the geometric Siegel-Weil formula (which identifies the generating series of volumes of special cycles with an Eisenstein series) to the arithmetic setting. This requires constructing integral models of orthogonal Shimura varieties, defining arithmetic special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups, and computing their arithmetic intersection numbers. Techniques from p-adic uniformization, modular forms, and the theory of Eisenstein series are essential. Partial results exist for Shimura curves (n=2) and some higher-dimensional cases via the work of Kudla-Rapoport-Yang and others.
title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil Formula for Orthogonal Shimura Varieties

description: A graph G is bipartite and {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable if and only if G is a spanning subgraph of a tensor product of complete bipartite graphs K_{2,2}. This conjecture formalizes the observed structural property that bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graphs must arise from specific tensor product constructions.
domain_bridges: Algebraic graph theory connects matrix eigenvalue properties with graph structure
Design theory provides tools for tensor product constructions
Computational group theory offers algorithmic approaches to verify tensor product decompositions
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by (1) establishing the necessity direction through careful analysis of eigenvector entry constraints in bipartite graphs with the {-1,0,1} property, leveraging the fact that bipartite adjacency matrices have symmetric spectrum; (2) proving sufficiency by constructing explicit diagonalizing matrices from tensor product bases; (3) using the structure theorem for prime-order graphs as a foundation to extend to composite orders via tensor product decompositions. The proof would require developing characterizations of when graphs admit diagonalizations with restricted eigenvector entries.
title: Bipartite {-1,0,1}-Diagonalizability Characterization

description: For any fixed approximation factor $c\in[1,\sqrt{2})$ there exists an infinite family $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of finite metric spaces such that any finitely presented $c$‑approximation of the Vietoris–Rips filtration of $X_n$ (i.e. a simplicial filtration $\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal A_r\preceq_c\operatorname{Rips}(X_n)_r$ for all $r\ge0$) contains at least $2^{\Omega(n)}$ simplices. Consequently, no sub‑exponential size $c$‑approximation exists for $c<\sqrt2$.
proof_strategy: Construct families of metric spaces from bounded‑degree expander graphs with distances $1$ (edges) and $c$-scaled distances to enforce a large ‘clique’ structure in the Vietoris–Rips complex. Show that any $c$‑approximation must contain all simplices of a large induced sub‑graph, which yields an exponential count. Formalise the construction in Lean by defining finite metric spaces as weighted graphs, defining $c$‑approximations via a dependent pair of a simplicial filtration and a family of interleaving maps, and proving a lower bound on the total number of simplices using combinatorial arguments about the expander’s independence number.
title: Exponential lower bound for $c$‑approximations of the Vietoris–Rips filtration below $\sqrt{2}$

description: For every 3 ≤ s < r, there exists an explicit piecewise polynomial function f_{s,r} : [0, x_s,max] → [0,1] such that the minimum possible K_r-density among all graphons W with prescribed K_s-density x equals f_{s,r}(x). This function is given by f_{s,r}(x) = max_{k=0}^{s-1} p_{s,r,k}(x) where each p_{s,r,k} is a computable (s-r+1)-nomial derived from the edge-to-clique multipartite profile, and the maximum is achieved precisely when W is equivalent to an (r-k)-partite graphon under cut distance.
proof_strategy: 1) Characterize the extremal graphon structure via flag algebra computations; 2) Prove that any near-extremal graphon has cut-distance closeness to a multipartite graphon using the stability theorem; 3) Establish uniqueness of the extremal family through convexity arguments on the graphon space; 4) Derive the explicit polynomial pieces by analyzing the limiting behavior of balanced (r-k)-partite graphons as k ranges from 0 to s-1.
title: Explicit Formula for Higher-Order Clique Density Lower Envelope

description: For any finite simple d‑regular graph G on n vertices, every integer vector q = (q_0,…,q_d) satisfying Σ q_i = n, Σ i·q_i even, and |q_i − n/(d+1)| ≤ 1 (0 ≤ i ≤ d) can be realized as the exact degree‑count vector of a spanning subgraph of G. The paper proves this for d ≤ n^{1/12−ε}, but the conjecture is that it holds for all d (i.e., for every n and d).
proof_strategy: Extend the threshold random subgraph construction and local‑adjustment scheme to handle any d.  One would need a uniform bound on the expected prefix‑norm of the degree error that scales like O(d^2√n) for all d up to n, and a refined edge‑atom estimate that works without the n^{‑1/12} restriction.  An iterative correction algorithm using only edge moves of type (a,b) with a+b = d‑2 or d‑1 would adjust the degree‑count vector to the target q while preserving simplicity, terminating after a polynomial number of steps.
title: Exact Alon–Wei degree distribution conjecture

description: If for every graph in an F-free class, there exists a walk-realizable F-supporter (determined via linear programming), then the class is generalized spectrally closed.
proof_strategy: Reduce existential quantifier over F-free graphs to linear programming feasibility via β-closed walk expansion
title: Existence of walk-realizable F-supporter for all F-free graphs implies generalized spectral closedness

description: For all integers n, k, ℓ with n ≥ 2k > 2ℓ ≥ 4, if F ⊆ 𝒞(n,k) and G ⊆ 𝒞(n,ℓ) are non‑trivial cross‑intersecting families (i.e., ⋂F = ∅ and ⋂G = ∅ and F ∩ G ≠ ∅ for all f ∈ F, g ∈ G), then the product of their sizes is maximized by the product of the standard Hilton‑Milner families: |F|·|G| ≤ |HM(n,k)|·|HM(n,ℓ)|, with equality only when F and G are (up to isomorphism) the canonical Hilton‑Milner constructions.
proof_strategy: Employ combinatorial double counting, analysis of minimal covers, and structural properties of 2‑cover graphs to bound the sizes of non‑trivial intersecting families and their products.
title: Product Hilton-Milner Conjecture

description: For the Ahlswede-Daykin inequality applied to a finite distributive lattice L with functions f₁, f₂, g₁, g₂ satisfying the ordering f₁ ≤ g₁ and f₂ ≤ g₂ pointwise, equality holds in the AD inequality if and only if L is isomorphic to a direct product L₁ × L₂ of distributive lattices, and each function decomposes as a product of functions on the respective factors. This conjecture provides a complete structural characterization of equality cases that is both necessary and sufficient, extending the paper's stated sufficient condition to a bidirectional equivalence.
proof_strategy: Establish the converse direction: assuming equality in AD inequality with the product structure hypothesis, prove that the lattice must decompose. Use the discrete concavity properties of the logarithm of the inequality ratios, combined with the Möbius inversion on the lattice to show that any violation of the product structure would create strict inequality. Leverage the rigidity lemma from the paper that equality requires constant ratios on intervals, then apply lattice-theoretic arguments to force the direct product decomposition.
title: Necessary and Sufficient Lattice Product Structure for AD Inequality Equality

description: For the quadratic polynomial P(X)=X^2+1, the number of integer quadruples (n1,n2,n3,n4) with 1≤ni≤N such that (n1^2+1)(n2^2+1)(n3^2+1)(n4^2+1) is a perfect square equals 2N^2 - N + O(N^{2-δ}) for some δ>0. This sharpens the paucity phenomenon of the paper by specifying the exact diagonal contribution and asserting a power-saving error term for non-diagonal solutions.
proof_strategy: Count diagonal solutions explicitly: because P(x)=x^2+1 is injective on positive integers, the only diagonal configurations are (a,b,a,b) and (a,b,b,a), giving exactly 2N^2 - N tuples. For non-diagonal solutions, adapt the paper's paucity argument using Evertse–Silverman and Reuss bounds, combined with explicit Pell equation analysis for x^2+1 = d y^2 and a squarefree sieve, to extract a power saving O(N^{2-δ}).
title: Exact paucity asymptotic for (n^2+1) quadruple square products

description: Conjecture that for all positive integers k,n,r, the Schur expansion of ∇^r G(k,n) has only non‑negative coefficients exactly when k divides n; otherwise at least one Schur coefficient is negative.
proof_strategy: Prove by induction on r using the compositional shuffle theorem and known Schur‑positive bases (C_α), together with a combinatorial interpretation of ∇ in terms of LLT polynomials and parking functions; reduction to checking the divisibility condition for r=1 and extending via the shuffle product.
title: Schur positivity pattern of iterated nabla on Petrie symmetric functions

description: Godel's incompleteness theorem says there are true statements that cannot be proved. But what if we turn incompleteness into a GAME? Define Godel's Casino: a game where the player bets on the truth value of statements that are independent of ZFC. The house deals cards representing arithmetic statements, and the player must bet TRUE or FALSE. The Continuum Hypothesis is the first card — you can bet either way and you're RIGHT in some model. Conjecture: Godel's Casino has a winning strategy that guarantees expected profit > 0, even though individual bets are undecidable. The strategy: bet TRUE on Sigma_1 statements (they're true if provable, and ZFC is Sigma_1-complete), bet FALSE on Pi_1 statements that are known to be independent (like Con(ZFC)), and bet on the CONSERVATIVE extension for statements that are genuinely undecidable. The expected profit per round is at least 1/3 because at least 1/3 of arithmetic statements are decidable (by the arithmetic hierarchy: the fraction of statements at level n that are decidable at level n is at least 1/3). Test: simulate Godel's Casino with 1000 independent ZFC statements and verify the winning strategy achieves expected profit > 0. Impact: incompleteness is not a barrier — it's an opportunity. You can WIN at the game of undecidability.
proof_strategy: Define Godel's Casino: each round, the house presents a statement phi in the language of arithmetic. The player bets TRUE or FALSE. If ZFC proves phi, TRUE wins. If ZFC proves not-phi, FALSE wins. If phi is independent of ZFC, BOTH bets win (the player gets their stake back plus a bonus). Strategy: bet TRUE on Sigma_1 statements, FALSE on negations of Con(ZFC) and similar independent Pi_1 statements. Prove expected profit > 0: by the arithmetic hierarchy, Sigma_1 statements are decidable (true iff provable). For a random statement at level n, the probability of decidability is at least 1/3 (by counting). So E[profit] >= (1/3) * (stake) > 0. The key: even though individual bets are undecidable, the AGGREGATE strategy is profitable because most arithmetic statements ARE decidable. Test: simulate with 1000 randomly generated arithmetic statements at various levels of the hierarchy.
title: Godel's Casino: Incomplete but Winnable Games

description: Prime gaps — the spaces between consecutive primes — are like empty cells in a crossword puzzle. The gaps are 1, 2, 2, 4, 2, 4, 2, 4, 6, 2, 6, 4, 2, 4, 6, 6, 2, 6, 4, 2, ... (OEIS A001223). The pattern seems random, but the crossword has rules: (1) All prime gaps are even (except the first gap of 1 between 2 and 3). (2) A gap g can only appear at position n if n+g is prime and all of n+1, n+2, ..., n+g-1 are composite. (3) The density of gap g near n is approximately 2*C_2/(g*log(n)) where C_2 is the twin prime constant. Conjecture: The prime gap crossword is uniquely solvable — given the pattern of gaps up to N, the next prime is determined with probability 1 - O(1/log(N)). More precisely, the conditional probability that the next prime after p is p + g, given all primes up to p, is approximately 2*C_2/g * (1/log(p)) * product_{q prime, q | g} (q-1)/(q-2). This is the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture for prime gaps. But the crossword has a surprise: certain gap patterns FORCE the next number. For example, if the gaps near n are 6, 4, 2, 6, then the next gap is almost certainly 4 (the only way to fill the crossword). Test: compute the conditional probabilities for prime gaps up to 10^8 and verify they match the Hardy-Littlewood prediction. Find forcing patterns (gaps that uniquely determine the next prime) and prove they occur with positive density. Impact: prime gaps are not random — they are a solvable crossword puzzle with deterministic rules.
proof_strategy: Define the prime gap sequence g(n) = p(n+1) - p(n) for n >= 1. State the Hardy-Littlewood gap conjecture: P(g(n) = g | g(n-1) = g_{-1}, ...) = 2*C_2/g * (1/log(p(n))) * product_{q prime, q | g} (q-1)/(q-2) where C_2 = 0.66016... is the twin prime constant. Define forcing patterns: a sequence of gaps g_{-k}, ..., g_{-1} is forcing if P(g(0) = g | g_{-k}, ..., g_{-1}) > 0.99 for exactly one value of g. Prove forcing patterns have positive density: the pattern [6, 4, 2, 6] is forcing because after primes p, p+6, p+10, p+12, p+18, the next prime must be p+22 with probability > 0.95 (since p+20 is even, p+21 is divisible by 3 if p ≡ 1 mod 3, etc.). Compute conditional probabilities numerically for N = 10^8. Test: enumerate forcing patterns and compute their density.
title: The Prime Number Crossword: Filling the Gaps in the Primes

description: A meme is a unit of cultural information that replicates through human minds. Model meme propagation as a sheaf over the social network graph: each node is a person, each edge is a communication channel, and the meme is a section of the sheaf that must satisfy consistency conditions at each node. Define meme fitness as the sheaf cohomology group H^1(G, M) where G is the social network and M is the meme sheaf. A meme with H^1 = 0 is universally transmissible (it has no consistency barriers — anyone can understand it). A meme with H^1 of dimension d requires d 'interpretation steps' to cross between communities. Conjecture: The most viral memes have H^1(G, M) = 0 but H^0(G, M) of maximal dimension — they spread everywhere AND mean different things to different communities. The dimension of H^0 counts the number of distinct interpretations. A meme that means the same thing to everyone has dim(H^0) = 1 and dim(H^1) = 0. A meme that means different things to different communities has dim(H^0) > 1 and dim(H^1) = 0. A meme that CANNOT spread between communities has H^1 > 0. Test: model Twitter/X retweet networks as graphs G with 1000 nodes, assign meme sheaves based on community structure, compute H^0 and H^1, and correlate with actual virality data. Impact: meme virality is a topological property — it's not about content quality but about the sheaf cohomology of the social network.
proof_strategy: Define the meme sheaf M on social network G: for each community C_i (cluster in G), M(C_i) is the set of interpretations of the meme in community i. For each edge between communities, there is a restriction map M(C_i) -> M(C_j) that transforms the meme's meaning. Define H^0(G, M) = kernel of the coboundary map (interpretations that are consistent across ALL communities). Define H^1(G, M) = cokernel (obstructions to consistent interpretation). Prove: dim(H^0) = number of universal interpretations. Prove: dim(H^1) = number of community-pairs where the meme CANNOT be consistently transmitted. Virality = dim(H^0) / (dim(H^0) + dim(H^1)) — the fraction of interpretations that spread without obstruction. Test: for 3 communities with sheaf values M(C1) = R, M(C2) = R, M(C3) = R^2 and restriction maps that mix coordinates, compute H^0 and H^1 and verify that high virality memes have H^1 = 0 and dim(H^0) > 1.
title: The Mathematics of Memes: Viral Information Topology

description:
# Future Directions — Congruence Rigidity of Sums of Squares

This cycle established that the entries of an integer right triangle are forced into
strong divisibility patterns — one leg is a multiple of three, the legs jointly carry a
factor of four, one entry is a multiple of five — and that a four-dimensional right
"box" (a solution of `a² + b² + c² = d²`) is even more rigid: at most one of its three
spatial edges can be odd. We also pinned down exactly which whole numbers can serve as a
leg. These findings point to several bold, testable conjectures.

## 1. The correct modulus for a power of two grows with the power
**Conjecture.** In any solution of `a² + b² = c²`, the two-adic valuation of the leg
product `a·b` is governed one level deeper than naive reduction suggests: deciding
whether `2^k` divides `a·b` is a question about residues modulo `2^{k+1}`, never modulo
`2^k`.
*The key insight is* that a difference of two odd squares is always divisible by eight,
so each additional factor of two in the product must be certified one binary place
further out than one would guess. *Why now?* Having isolated the exact `mod 8`
obstruction behind the factor of four, we can test the pattern mechanically for `k = 3,
4, 5` and either confirm a clean "shift-by-one" law or expose its first exception.

## 2. A universal super-divisor for higher-dimensional right figures
**Conjecture.** For every dimension `r`, solutions of `x₁² + ⋯ + x_r² = y²` obey a single
universal divisibility law: there is a constant `D(r)`, depending only on `r`, such that
`D(r)` divides the product `x₁·x₂·⋯·x_r` for *every* solution, and `D(r)` is the largest
such constant.
*The key insight is* that reduction to a finite residue ring turns "for all solutions"
into a finite, decidable statement, so the optimal constant `D(r)` is computable and
should grow in a structured (conjecturally multiplicative-over-primes) way. *Why now?*
The three-dimensional case already yields `4 ∣ x₁x₂x₃`; comparing it against the planar
constant `12` suggests a dimension-indexed sequence worth charting and predicting.

## 3. Parity collapse in higher dimensions
**Conjecture.** As the number of squared terms increases, the number of edges permitted to
be odd stays uniformly bounded: in `x₁² + ⋯ + x_r² = y²` at most three of the `x_i` can be
odd, regardless of `r`.
*The key insight is* that the sum of squares equals the count of odd terms modulo four,
while a perfect square is `0` or `1` modulo four, capping the admissible odd-count no
matter how many terms are added. *Why now?* We proved the cap is "at most one" in three
dimensions; extending the modular bookkeeping to arbitrary `r` is a self-contained next
step that would reveal whether the cap is truly dimension-independent.

## 4. A sharp threshold characterization of legs in every dimension
**Conjecture.** Just as the whole numbers that are a leg of a right triangle are exactly
those `≥ 3`, in each higher dimension there is a sharp finite threshold above which every
integer appears as an edge of some right figure, and the finitely many exceptions can be
listed explicitly.
*The key insight is* that a single explicit construction, split according to the parity of
the target edge, realizes all sufficiently large values, while the small exceptions are
forced by a factorization that would otherwise require a vanishing edge. *Why now?* The
planar threshold `3` and its sharpness (the failures at `1` and `2`) give a template that
should transfer verbatim to the box equation and beyond.

## 5. Divisibility as a sieve against near-solutions
**Conjecture.** The combined congruence obstructions (`12 ∣ a·b`, `60 ∣ a·b·c`, and their
higher-dimensional analogues) are strong enough that a random integer triple satisfying
them has a positive, computable probability of being genuinely Pythagorean — i.e. the
congruence conditions capture a constant fraction of the "arithmetic mass" of true
solutions.
*The key insight is* that each universal divisor removes a fixed proportion of impostors,
so stacking independent prime-power obstructions multiplies into a sieve of predictable
density. *Why now?* With the exact obstructions in hand for the primes `2, 3, 5`, one can
immediately measure how much of the solution set they explain and calibrate whether a few
more primes suffice to pin down solutions almost completely.
title: That the entries of an integer right triangle are forced

description:
# Future Directions: Log-Concavity in the d-Hoggatt Hierarchy

This cycle established a sharp dichotomy for the *total* d-Hoggatt numbers
`H_d(n) = ∑_k H_d(n,k)`: the `d = 1` totals `2^n` are infinitely log-concave
(indeed log-linear), while the `d = 2` totals (Catalan numbers) are strictly
log-convex, and the `d = 3` totals (Baxter numbers) are empirically log-convex.
The following conjectures are the natural next targets.

## Conjecture 1 — Universal log-convexity of the totals for d ≥ 2

For every `d ≥ 2`, the total d-Hoggatt numbers are strictly log-convex:
`H_d(n+1)² < H_d(n) · H_d(n+2)` for all `n ≥ 0`.

The key insight is that each `H_d(n)` is a positively weighted sum of products
of binomial coefficients whose dominant growth ratio increases with `n`, so the
totals inherit the log-convexity of the Catalan case rather than the
log-concavity of the individual rows. Why now? The Catalan (`d = 2`) case is now
settled from a two-term recurrence, and the Baxter (`d = 3`) case matches it
term-by-term in the computed data, suggesting a single recurrence-driven
argument covers the whole family.

## Conjecture 2 — Row-sum log-convexity is a summation phenomenon

If `T(n,k)` is any triangle whose rows are log-concave and whose row-ratio
`T(n+1,k)/T(n,k)` is nondecreasing in `n`, then the row sums `S(n) = ∑_k T(n,k)`
are log-convex.

The key insight is that log-convexity of the totals is not special to Hoggatt
triangles but follows from monotone amplification of a common growth factor
across rows, a Chebyshev-sum / rearrangement effect. Why now? Having seen the
same negative discriminant `Δ_n < 0` for both Catalan and Baxter totals, the
phenomenon is clearly structural rather than coincidental and deserves a triangle
-level hypothesis.

## Conjecture 3 — Infinite log-concavity of the rows

For every `d ≥ 1`, each fixed row `k ↦ H_d(n,k)` of the d-Hoggatt triangle is
infinitely log-concave.

The key insight is that the log-concavity operator, when applied to a finite
positive log-concave row with the golden-ratio-squared safety factor
`a_k² ≥ ((3+√5)/2) · a_{k-1} a_{k+1}`, reproduces that same safety factor, so a
single closure lemma propagates through all iterates. Why now? The threshold
constant `(3+√5)/2` is exactly the fixed point of the operator's worst-case
ratio, and the toolkit built this cycle (the operator `𝓛`, its annihilation of
log-linear sequences, and closure under products) already contains the moving
parts needed to attack the closure lemma.

## Conjecture 4 — A log-concave "renormalization" of the totals

For every `d ≥ 2` there is an explicit positive normalizing sequence `w_d(n)`
(e.g. a ratio of factorials) such that the renormalized totals
`H_d(n) / w_d(n)` are infinitely log-concave, even though the raw totals are
log-convex.

The key insight is that log-convexity of the totals is caused by a smooth,
predictable growth factor which can be divided out, leaving a residual sequence
governed by the same infinite-log-concavity mechanism as the rows. Why now? The
exact growth ratio `(n+2)(2n+3)/((2n+1)(n+3))` for the Catalan totals is now
known in closed form, giving a concrete first candidate for `w_2` and a template
for higher `d`.

## Conjecture 5 — Tropical dequantization of the dichotomy

Under the tropical (min-plus) limit that sends a positive sequence `a_n` to its
valuations `v_n = −log a_n`, log-concavity becomes convexity of `v` and
log-linearity becomes affinity of `v`. The `d = 1`/`d ≥ 2` dichotomy then reads:
`v` is affine for `d = 1` and strictly concave for `d ≥ 2`.

The key insight is that the log-concavity operator degenerates, in the tropical
limit, to a second finite difference, so infinite log-concavity corresponds to a
sequence of iterated finite differences retaining a fixed sign — a purely
piecewise-linear, tropical-geometric condition. Why now? Casting the numeric
dichotomy in the min-plus semiring links this combinatorial question to tropical
convexity, where second-difference sign conditions are the natural objects and
powerful piecewise-linear tools are available.
title: Sharp dichotomy for the *total* d-Hoggatt numbers
